News.title: Victim stabbed to death in broad daylight horror attack at council HQ near Wembley – as emergency crews swarm scene
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

KNIFE ATTACK Victim stabbed to death in broad daylight horror attack at council HQ near Wembley – as emergency crews swarm scene

A PERSON has tragically died after a horror broad daylight stabbing at a council HQ near Wembley Stadium.

Officers cordoned off the Brent Civic Centre in Wembley, North West London, after the horror unfolded this afternoon.



Metropolitan Police and London Ambulance Service (LAS) crews rushed to the HQ at around 2.25pm.

Staff in the building, which is home to Brent Council, were also reportedly evacuated.



Air ambulance crews were among the emergency response scrambled following reports of the stabbing, according to the LAS.

A spokesperson said: “We were called at 2:25pm to reports of a stabbing at Brent Civic Centre, Wembley, HA9.

“We sent an ambulance crew, paramedics in fast response cars and an incident response officer.

“We also dispatched London’s Air Ambulance.

“Sadly, despite the best efforts of our crews, a patient was pronounced dead at the scene”.

News.title: Moment ‘absolute hero’ M&S driver stops on busy UK motorway to casually put out blazing van fire with extinguisher
News.content:
THIS is the moment a “hero” M&S lorry driver calmly put out a blazing van fire on a busy motorway with an extinguisher.

A white Peugeot Partner was filmed with flames and thick black smoke erupting from the bonnet after stopping on the M25 at Junction 21 near Watford in Hertfordshire.



In the video, the food truck driver can be seen walking to the cab’s passenger side and pulling out a fire extinguisher.

He then stands about a foot away with no protective equipment and puts out the inferno.



At one point, he is even engulfed in a cloud of white smoke as he douses the flames on the hard shoulder.

The unnamed driver was hailed for his quick thinking on social media.



On Instagram, West London and Southall page UB1UB2 wrote: “No word on what caused it or whether anyone was hurt, but fair to say the van driver owes him a shop at M&S.

“This is your Percy Pig energy. Absolute legend or what?”



After the clip went viral, Adit Gupta responded: “In a time where most would drive past while pulling out their phone to record it, this man had the courage to do the right thing.”

Toni Kirby couldn’t resist riffing on the food chain’s famous slogan, writing: “This isn’t just a lorry driver…this is an M&S lorry driver.”

Summing up the thoughts of many, Syed Shah wrote: “Absolute legend and immense respect to him. Not all heroes wear capes.”

Jane Mackie said simply: “What a hero.”

Kieron White added a note of caution, writing: “Nice and calm, no panic hopefully the bosses don’t reprimand him.”



Hertfordshire Fire and Rescue Service confirmed that the professionals were called to help put out the blaze shortly before 6pm on Thursday, August 20.

The police were called but didn’t need to attend.

Marks and Spencer declined to comment.

News.title: Company director in bitter row with neighbours over huge state-of-the-art golf simulator built in garden without warning
News.content:
TEEING OFF Company director in bitter row with neighbours over huge state-of-the-art golf simulator built in garden without warning

A COMPANY director has found himself in a bitter row with his neighbours after building a huge state-of-the-art golf simulator.

Businessman Pete Bransky constructed the 23ft-wide cabin at the bottom of his garden in Christchurch, Dorset, to practice his swing.



The shed boasts a glass skylight, artificial grass and soundproof panelling on the walls.

But neighbours say the timber hut is far too big, and complained to the council claiming Mr Bransky had not been upfront about the true size of the shack.



They also said the building creates a fire hazard as it is too close to their fences.

Mr Bransky is thought to have bought a rundown bungalow a decade ago, knocking the home and garage down and replacing them with a pair of contemporary three-bedroom homes.



One neighbour claims that because of the plot split the property does not have permitted development rights.

Mr Bransky’s golf shack, which is roughly 23ft wide and 13.5ft long, takes up the entire width of the back garden.

In the plans, the company director stated the height to the eaves was 7ft 8ins and the distance to the back fence was 1.1m.

But furious neighbours claim the garden room towers above the 6.5ft fence.



One even used a laser measuring device and believes the overall height is 13ft if you include the central glass canopy, or about 10ft to the eaves.

Both next-door neighbours claim Mr Bransky’s cabin creates a fire hazard by only leaving about 20 inches between the building and the boundary fence.

Neighbour Mike Woolley said: “The submitted drawings and supporting information do not accurately reflect the structure for which permission has been sought.

“Based on measurements taken using a laser measuring device, the existing building differs significantly from the proposed development in terms of its footprint, overall height and proximity to the site boundaries.

“These are material planning considerations that differ substantially from the proposal.



“Furthermore, the existing structure is of timber construction and is located less than one metre from the site boundary.

“I have seen no evidence that the fire safety provisions required by the Building Regulations for a building in such close proximity to a boundary have been incorporated.

“While I have significant concerns regarding the existing structure, I would reluctantly support its replacement with a building that more closely reflects the scale and limitations ordinarily associated with permitted development.”

John Allan, whose smart bungalow home backs onto the golf hut, said that Mr Bransky’s claim the building sits 1.1m from boundary fence was incorrect, alleging it is actually 50cm.

An arboricultural assessment said the structure had a “relatively modest footprint” and was set back from neighbours’ boundaries by 3.5ft but a neighbour sent the council pictures measuring the distance showing the gap to the sides was only 1.6ft.



Mr Bransky, who runs a printing business, told council officials any noise from the simulator is “negligible”.

He has fitted acoustic sports panels to the walls and ceiling and soundproof carpet tiles to the floor to reduce any noise.

The businessman also put in a rubber anti-shock and noise reduction framed base to reduce sound when he strikes the balls and installed a high-end quad layered pro+ golf simulator impact screen so the balls will not be hitting any walls.

Mr Bransky said: “Any noise from the golf simulation is negligible. With the double glazed door closed you cannot hear anything from outside the building.”

The consultation period for public comments to the application ends on August 26 and after that planning officials will make a decision.



The Sun has approached Mr Bransky for comment.

News.title: Mystery behind death of pastor’s wife after claims he injected her with testosterone, & ‘paid homeless to assault her’
News.content:
LIVING HELL Mystery behind death of pastor’s wife after claims he injected her with testosterone, & ‘paid homeless to assault her’

WHEN Mica Miller dialled 911 from a national park in South Carolina, alarm bells immediately went off.

The mum told the operator she was about to kill herself and that she wanted her family to know where to find her body.



Mica’s body was subsequently found at the Lumber River State Park – more than an hour away from her home – on April 27, 2024, and her death was promptly ruled a suicide.

Holding his hand next to his heart, Mica’s husband, John-Paul Miller, the pastor of her family’s church in Myrtle Beach, broke the devastating news to the churchgoers.



“My wife has passed away.”

“I told them for years this would happen and I said ‘If she gets off her medicine suicide is… is the next thing,” the father-of-five, 46, said in an interview with a news channel.

The case drew national attention after evidence surfaced that Mica, who was 30 at the time, had previously claimed to be the victim in a stalking plot by her seemingly picture-perfect husband – even telling police officers she was “afraid for her life” just a month before her death.

“She said, ‘He’s gonna put a bullet in my head and told everybody I killed myself’,” said Bruna Pabon, a churchgoer who had become close with Mica.



The tragic and shocking story is told in a new three-part documentary series, Death of the Pastor’s Wife, on Netflix.

Mica and her family – a total of six siblings – first met John-Paul Miller when they moved to Myrtle Beach in South Carolina and started going to the local church. From there, Mica developed a close relationship with religion and eventually became a worship leader – someone who is in charge of the choir.

Just two years later, Mica married “godly man” Jeremy Deas – two “inseparable” high-school sweethearts who both attended the church. From early on, Mica knew she wanted to become a pastor’s wife – and Jeremy was the perfect opportunity to fulfil the fairytale dream.

The couple tied the knot in September 2012 and it was John-Paul Miller who presided over the ceremony.

Not long after, Mica became John-Paul’s assistant, being at the church for most of the week getting his sermons ready, getting notes together and putting presentations together. Young Mica also became the Miller family’s babysitter and the couple went on many double dates with the pastor and his wife Ali.



But what began as a platonic friendship between Mica and John-Paul soon turned into something more romantic three years later – and the word that the two, 21 and 36 at the time, had started an affair quickly spreading across the church.

After divorcing from their partners, Mica and John-Paul got engaged with a romantic proposal on the beach – despite claims that the pastor had cheated on her earlier, a mistake John-Paul allegedly vowed never to make again.

But behind closed doors, the documentary claims that issues started to brew.



Mica, who her family claimed had never wanted to change her body, suddenly decided to get breast augmentation “to be the perfect woman in his eyes”.

“She started having insecurities,” said Sierra Francis, Mica’s sister.

“I’m sure he was comparing her to these other women. Mica never mentioned she wanted to have a breast augmentation until after she was with John-Paul.”

“I feel like he made my sister feel like she wasn’t beautiful enough,” Nate Francis, Mica’s brother, continued.

After the surgery, Mica had a bad reaction to the sedatives the surgeons had given causing her to suffer problems with her mental health and, according to the documentary, her husband was allegedly pushing to have Mica “institutionalised”.



Despite Mica’s family’s objections, doctors admitted her to a mental institution where she was diagnosed with bipolar disorder.

Just six days after Mica was discharged, the couple officially got married, with John-Paul promising to “remain faithful, loyal” and Mica becoming stepmum to John-Paul’s five kids from his previous marriage.

Talking about her marriage issues, Mica was said to be “vague”. But her friends claim they soon started noticing controlling behaviour from John-Paul, allegedly giving Mica just two to three hours to hang out with them before calling her ‘every five minutes’ to check when she’s coming home.

Once Mica did start opening up more than a year later, there were said to be other “red flags” – Mica allegedly knew that if they didn’t engage in sex “every single day”, sometimes as often as four times a day, he’d “get it from somewhere”.

Shockingly, her friends also claimed that not only would John-Paul sometimes allegedly withhold her medicine from Mica – but that he had also supposedly injected testosterone in his wife so that she would “keep up with his sex drive and make it easier”.



“Mica was usually very well put together. But lately, she didn’t really look like herself,” fellow member of the church Erica Rahr said in the documentary.

“She had started having trouble with her voice. There were times off and on where she would lose her vocals – or her voice changed. Why would you ever recommend that, or do that, to your wife?”

Things took a darker turn in November 2022 when Mica went to stay at Sierra’s place after the pastor had accused her of being unfaithful with her friend. Hours later, John-Paul sent them a message – he was on his way, and he was armed.

Despite the threats, Mica decided to not press charges and returned to her husband, with her friends admitting they had a gut feeling that “something bad” was about to happen.

Despite her efforts, it was claimed that Mica later found out her husband had cheated on her again – this time, with a churchgoer, Suzie Skinner, whose husband had passed away in what was described as mysterious circumstances just a year earlier.



Having grown close to the church and its members and wanting to protect the church’s reputation, it is alleged that Mica couldn’t see herself leaving the institution, so she made her husband sign a document – if the affairs continued, she would be out.

But there was one horrific act that John-Paul subjected his wife to that would finally push her to breaking point.

“The horror that she had to live with was something I had never heard of,” churchgoer Bruna Pabon said.

“Many times, they would leave dinner, and he will pull the truck and just see a random homeless person, and he’d pay him to do things (to her.)

“She told me that a nighttime, after they’ve had sex four or five times during the day, and he would try and initiate something, and (if) she would deny him, he wouldn’t let her sleep.”



Bruna continued: “Sometimes she said that he would wait until she’s falling asleep, and then he’ll go and turn on all the rights in the room just to wake her up. He would mentally torture her like this – until she gave him what he wanted.

“So many nights, I would get to church and see her with deep, dark eyes.

“She said that sometimes her body was physically in pain and there was nothing else she could do, and so she just accepted it.”

Mica moved out and started working at a restaurant in a hope of finding a fresh start.

But the nightmare was far from over.



Despite constantly moving houses and staying with those close to her, John-Paul allegedly launched a vicious stalking campaign, arranging flower deliveries, terrorising Mica with texts, sticking razor blades in her tyres and even placing trackers in her car.

Then, one day, the pastor also uploaded a naked photo of Mica on Facebook without her consent according to witnesses.

Eventually, she filed for divorce and John-Paul was served the papers in April 2024. But despite begging for a restraining order, the hearing wasn’t scheduled to take place until June – more than three months later.

On April 27, Mica left the apartment where she was staying with a close friend to go to work. But instead of going to the restaurant for her shift, Mica drove to a pawn shop to purchase a gun before making an hour-long journey to the Lumber River state park.

Shortly before 3pm, she made the heartbreaking 911 call. Less than two hours later, a man found her body in water.



The death sent shockwaves through Mica’s family – who also received text messages from John-Paul saying “this is what happens [when] you tell them they don’t need medicine and that they’re not ill when they are”.

The following morning John-Paul hosted a sermon, talking about music and likening reading the Bible to watching a “Steven Spielberg movie” before announcing that Mica had passed away. He preached that it was a suicide before the coroner’s report had even come out.

After the sermon, John-Paul apparently tried to collect all of Mica’s belongings from her family and friends, even telling Mica’s attorney, Regina Ward, that she had allegedly tried to end her life on numerous occasions.

Although the investigation ruled her death as suicide, it was claimed that Mica’s family struggled to accept it and felt like she was “lured to where she was found” and had purchased the gun “for protection”.

The story exploded on social media where it also caught the attention of Rich McHugh, investigative correspondent at Newsnation.



“[Mica] continued north towards the Lumber River State Park. It’s kind of an eerie place, hours away from Myrtle Beach, so why go there?” he said.

When the police found Mica’s deceased body, she was face down in the river. They found two spent casings and a live round on the bank of the river – 100ft away from her body.

“The stretch of water where she was found has very little current, making it unusual for a body to drift that far,” Rich said.

Despite claims that some in the local community felt like John-Paul has “Mica’s blood” on her hands and that he was responsible for her tragic death, as of now no charges have been brought against the 46-year-old. The FBI have since launched an investigation.

In December 2025, a federal grand jury indicted John-Paul on two counts – one count of making false statements to federal investigators during the investigation into Mica’s death and one count of cyberstalking, alleging a pattern of harassment toward his estranged wife, Mica, between November 2022 and April 2024.



John-Paul has entered a plea deal of not guilty to the federal charges against him. He has not been charged in connection with Mica’s death.

One year after Mica’s death, on June 1st, 2025, John-Paul tied the knot with Suzie Skinner.

“These charges reflect only a fraction of what he did to her,” said Mica’s brother Nate.

“People need to remember that this isn’t just a story – this is a story about a real person.”

“That man tortured our sister in every way possible,” said Sierra.

News.title: One in five Brits ‘wake up on the wrong side of the bed’ three days a week
News.content:
RISE & WHINE One in five Brits ‘wake up on the wrong side of the bed’ three days a week

ONE in five Brits ‘wake up on the wrong side of the bed’ at least three days a week.

A poll of 2,000 adults found 43 per cent feel grumpy, irritable or easily annoyed immediately after waking at least once a week, rising sharply to 72 per cent among Gen Z.



More than a third (35 per cent) confessed they regularly start the day feeling tired, low on energy or simply not quite themselves.

After experiencing a less-than-ideal wake-up, nearly two thirds (63 per cent) said the way they feel first thing in the morning often affects the rest of their day.



Many admitted a lack of motivation (49 per cent), irritability (32 per cent), feeling emotionally low (31 per cent) and stress (28 per cent) are common experiences that can impact their day-to-day lives.

The research was commissioned by Samsung Health to showcase the Vitals feature on the Galaxy Watch9 and Galaxy Watch Ultra2, which helps users better understand their overnight recovery.



Eight in 10 respondents agreed they would like a deeper understanding of what their body is telling them when they wake up feeling different from usual.

However, attitudes toward overnight recovery vary by generation – as 28 per cent of Baby Boomers admitted they have little interest in it.

But this rises to 80 per cent of Gen Z and 84 per cent of Millennials.

Overall, 72 per cent said they would be interested in understanding how well their body recovers overnight.



The findings point to a growing shift in how people manage their sleep and wellbeing, with 63 per cent saying they pay closer attention to their health than they did five years ago.

Meanwhile, 54 per cent are now more proactive about monitoring their wellbeing than in the past.

Many are already turning to technology to support this approach, with 68 per cent currently tracking at least one aspect of their health.

The most commonly monitored factors are sleep (35 per cent), weight and body composition (34 per cent), and activity levels (29 per cent).

A quarter are tracking their nutrition, while 21 per cent use technology to keep an eye on their heart health.



One in five (20 per cent) are also making use of tools designed to help monitor and manage stress levels.

Two thirds (66 per cent) believe technology can help them better understand the signals their bodies are sending and support healthier everyday habits.

News.title: Cops hunt man over three sexual assaults on different trains as CCTV released
News.content:
SEX ATTACKS Cops hunt man over three sexual assaults on different trains as CCTV released

COPS have released CCTV in the urgent hunt for a man following a string of alleged sexual assaults on different trains.

The victims were all reportedly targeted on services travelling from London to Essex over a five-month period.



The first reported sexual assault and attempted sexual assault occurred in March, cops said.

Following one of the sickening attacks, the man is said to have left the train at Westcliff-on-Sea, Essex.



Months later, the same man allegedly sexually assaulted a woman while travelling on a service from London to Benfleet.

The vile attack reportedly occurred shortly after midnight on July 5, according to British Transport Police (BTP).



Officers have now released CCTV images of a man they are hunting in connection with the assaults.

They believe he may have information that could assist their investigation.

The force has urged anyone with information or who recognises the man to get in touch.

A BTP spokesperson said: “Detectives investigating three sexual assaults on board trains to Essex have released these images in connection.



“Detectives believe the man in the images could have information that may assist their enquiries.

“Anyone who recognises him is asked to text BTP on 61016, or call 0800 40 50 40, using the reference Op Valhalla.

“Information can also be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

It comes as cops continue to hunt for another man after two women were sexually assaulted two days apart on the Tube.

The first incident occurred at around 8.40pm on August 1, when a woman was reportedly attacked on board a Northern line train at Waterloo.



The same man is understood to have sexually assaulted another woman at around 8pm on August 3, on the Northern line near Euston.

News.title: Will it rain this weekend? Latest Met Office weather forecast for the August bank holiday in the UK
News.content:
BRITS gearing up for the August bank holiday are keeping a close eye on the skies.

After a relatively sunny and settled start, the final week of meteorological summer is expected to bring a shift in the weather.



Experts predict a wave of low pressure to sweep in from the south.

So if you’re planning a weekend BBQ or a staycation, you may need to keep the umbrellas on standby alongside the sun cream.



Will it rain this bank holiday weekend?

At the time of writing, it’s looking like a mixed bag for the extended weekend.

The Met Office says an area of low pressure is forecast to sweep in from the Atlantic just as the bank holiday begins.

That will bring with it unsettled conditions, though where you are in the country could prove key.

The service says north-western areas currently appear the most likely to experience the driest conditions over the three-day break.

Heading into Friday, both Northern Ireland and western Scotland will enjoy some of the best conditions, with plenty of sunshine and comfortable temperatures in the high teens to low twenties.

For the rest of the UK, conditions will be far more hit-and-miss as damp, muggy weather takes over.



Forecasters say there could be a “brief respite from the unsettled conditions early on Saturday”, giving you a potential window to fire up the grill, hit the beach, or get out for a walk.

Don’t get too comfortable though – further spells of rain and showers are likely to develop as the weekend progresses into Sunday and Bank Holiday Monday.

What is the weather doing this week?

The shift in weather will be felt well before Saturday arrives.

The Met Office says the UK is facing a “marked change in the weather” as the week progresses.

While Tuesday, August 25 offered a pleasant day for many, Wednesday will see the risk of showers and thunderstorms increase across the south and west.



That forecast has prompted a yellow weather warning across a large chunk of England and Wales.

Despite the looming storms, temperatures will remain high, reaching the mid-to-high twenties.

Thursday is currently tipped to be the hottest day of the week, with temperatures hitting 28C in parts of southern and eastern England.

But a yellow warning for thunderstorms remains in place from 6am to 10pm.

The Met Office says there will be “increasing humidity, warmer temperatures and a growing risk of heavy rain and thunderstorms.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Some areas could see 30 to 40mm of rainfall in a very short space of time, bringing a risk of surface water flooding, hail and lightning.

By Friday, the forecast becomes even more unpredictable as the low-pressure system shifts north-eastwards, taking the heaviest rain towards northern and eastern parts of England.

News.title: Raging bulls kill 2 & injure 11 as spectators are hurled in air & thrown like rag dolls by beasts set loose in streets
News.content:
RAGING bulls have killed two people and injured 11, hurling spectators in the air like rag dolls as they charge through the streets at a festival.

Juan Manuel Filomeno Herrera, 29, died from serious head and chest injuries after he was gored at a gory Mexican version of Pamplona’s famous Running of the Bulls festival.



Luis Xolocotzi Ramirez, 57, suffered a skull fracture and gore injury to his chest at Saturday’s event in Huamantla, east of Mexico City.

He had to be rushed to hospital by air ambulance, where he died of his injuries.





A 24-year-old American woman from Texas is reportedly among those hospitalised at this year’s Huamantlada festival.

It saw 21 fighting bulls let loose in the street.

Injuries included a woman who was thrown in the air by one of the huge animals and struck in the face.

Terrifying footage shows her attempting to flee the animal as it charged at her.



But it catches the woman with its horns and flips her over its back.

She crashes to the ground in front of horrified onlookers, as the bull rounds on her again.

The woman is knocked over once more, but scrambles to her feet and runs for her life before being helped to safety.



More harrowing video shows one of the men thought to have lost his life at the festival being charged at and gored.

The clip shows him being tossed in the air before his is dragged away.

The deaths were the first for eight years at the festival.

Juan, the youngest fatality, lived locally.

He is said to have been gored by a bull after losing his balance and falling to the ground.



Many people questioned the festival’s traditions after the deaths.

Bruno Gonzalez shared a photo of Juan and wrote on Facebook: “At what point does tradition become thoughtlessness, violence and negligence?

“And when it becomes that, is it worth perpetuating it over time? May he rest in peace.”

It comes after several people were injured at this year’s running of the bulls at Pamplona’s San Fermín festival.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They included a Brit tourist who was rushed to hospital.



William Mitchinson, 24, was trampled as he tried to outrun the animals on the half-mile course in the north of Spain.

News.title: Barcelona fire live: 'Explosion' heard as flames and smoke seen from plane
News.content:
An image of the blaze taken from a Ryanair plane

A huge fire has broken out in Barcelona, with smoke visible from a Ryanair flight amid unconfirmed reports of an explosion

A huge fire has broken out in Barcelona, sending a thick cloud of black smoke above the city which could be seen from a Ryanair flight.

The blaze is in the Collserola area, close to the Canyelles neighbourhood in Nou Barris, with images from the scene showing flames and smoke billowing into the sky.

One person posting on X claimed a high-voltage tower had exploded, although this has yet to be confirmed by authorities. Smoke from the fire was also visible from a Ryanair flight above Barcelona.

News.title: Mum of teen killed in wrong-way M9 crash apologises to family left in hospital
News.content:
Mum of teen killed in wrong-way M9 crash apologises to family left in hospital

Mourners today gathered for the funeral of Jack Kennedy, 17, who died alongside four others after the car they were travelling in was driven the wrong way down the M9 motorway in Ireland

Jack Kennedy: Funeral held for teenager killed in M9 crash in Ireland

The mother of one of the five young people killed when their car went the wrong way down the M9 in Ireland, before crashing into another car, has apologised to a family left in hospital.

‌



The funeral mass for 17-year-old Jack Kennedy, who died in the crash on the M9 in Co Kildare last weekend, also heard calls to “please, please, please, stop” engaging in criminal activity.

‌



Sisters Ella Hendricken, Niamh Kinsella and Alma Kinsella, who are aged in their 20s and 30s, were rushed to hospital after their car was struck by the vehicle travelling the wrong way. They were travelling with a child, who was also hospitalised, when their Hyundai was hit by the BMW at around 3am on August 16.

‌



Garda officers were stationed in Kildare ahead of Jack's funeral today, but less than was seen at the services held last week for the other four who died in the crash.

View 4 Images Jack Kennedy

Police probe as several motorists seen driving wrong way on M6 following crash READ MORE :

Jack died alongside Jeremy O’Brien, Kamil Pustkowski, Joe Carthy and Alex McCarthy when their car collided head-on with the other vehicle.

‌



Jack’s mother Sarah spoke at the funeral at St Michael’s, Athy, Kildare, on Tuesday morning. She apologised to the family still recovering in hospital as a result of the crash.

“Five young boys made a bad choice,” she said. “Five young boys paid the ultimate price. Five families lost their babies. Five families got a life sentence. May they all rest in peace.

View 4 Images The cortege for Jack Kennedy makes its way through Athy, Co Kildare, ahead of his funeral at St. Michael's Parish Church (Image: Evan Treacy/PA Wire)

‌



“Secondly, we all want to send our deepest, heartfelt apologies to the families who were injured. You are all in our thoughts and our prayers. We pray to God that you all make a full recovery and once again, we are sorry.”

In the eulogy, Canon Frank McEvoy referred to anger that has been expressed on social media surrounding the incident. He said: “Words can hurt, and words have the power to heal. It’s also true of actions. Our actions can hurt people, and our actions can heal people.

“In all those situations, we’re responsible for the words that we use, and above all, we’re responsible for the actions that we take.”

‌



He said the feeling in the parish after the crash was “one of shock, confusion, disbelief, and above all, anger”. “Anger is a very dangerous emotion, and when it starts to curdle and get going in the community, anything can happen,” he said.

View 4 Images Ella Hendricken (L), Niamh Kinsella (C) and Alma Kinsella (R) were seriously injured in the crash

“When you watch social media and you watch the responses and you hear what people are saying, that’s the result of bad actions and very often, then, in all of that, there’s so much hurt created for the family.

‌



“Sarah put it so well, she doesn’t wish any of you to walk in her shoes, to have to bury her son. There’s no great future in all of that.

“And again, as I say, the dust has settled somewhat, and the week has passed by, there is something I want to say, and especially to Jack’s friends, and it’s this – if you’re considering continuing this criminal activity, will you please stop?

“Just one word, stop. Because this is the end of it."

‌



View 4 Images Jack was one of the five teenagers who died in a motorway crash in Co Kildare earlier this month (Image: Evan Treacy/PA Wire)

“This is a family broken, and the consequences of that will happen to you too, for you yourself, for your families, the communities in which you live in, and then you’ll have the innocent victims, like the people who are in hospital trying to recover.

“There is no need for it. So again, I say to you, please, please, please, stop.”

Article continues below

One of the items brought to the altar was a car to represent Jack’s “love for cars”.

Young, Wild & Free by Snoop Dogg and Wiz Khalifa played as the coffin was taken from the chapel for a private cremation.

News.title: 'Little-known' Sudocrem use people might not know about
News.content:
'Little-known' Sudocrem use people might not know about

The lesser-known use could be especially helpful for families with children

View 3 Images People might not know about the multiple uses (Image: Getty)

Many families have a tub of Sudocrem in their first-aid cupboard. Parents often use the antiseptic healing cream to treat nappy rash, but it has a lesser-known use.

‌



Sudocrem is also licensed to treat and heal minor burns and surface wounds. Highlighting the advice in a social media post, Sudocrem told Facebook users to 'stop using this just for nappy rash.' The caption explained: "Sudocrem Antiseptic Healing Cream is a medicine for minor burns and surface wounds. Always read the label. We all know the grey tub is the go-to for nappy rash. But once the Crawling Era hits, it takes on a whole new job."

‌



It adds: "Did you know? Sudocrem Antiseptic Healing Cream isn’t just for nappy rash. It is actually licensed to treat and heal minor burns and surface wounds. So when the speed-crawling leaves a mark, you know exactly what to reach for to help soothe the area."

‌



More information is available on Sudocrem's website. It says the cream can be used for acne spots, eczema, chafing, pressure sores, nappy rash, or cuts and grazes. The advice says it helps cuts and grazes as the cream 'treats and protects the wound' and 'minimises the chance of infection'.

Sudocrem also 'soothes pain' and 'protects with a shielding layer', according to the product description. The guidance says: "If the bleeding is minimal and the wound superficial, it can typically be treated at home.

View 3 Images Many people keep the cream in their first-aid box (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

‌



"If the bleeding is heavy or the wound appears deep, seek medical attention immediately. Rinse the wound with water or a sterile wipe, then gently pat dry. Keep an eye on the wound.

"Any increase in redness, swelling or warmth, or if it’s just not healing properly, seek medical attention. Carefully apply a thin layer of Sudocrem Antiseptic Healing Cream. Protect the wound with a sterile dressing, such as gauze or a plaster."

The NHS website says most cuts and grazes can be treated at home, but that a medical professional should treat serious wounds. "You can treat a cut or graze yourself by stopping any bleeding, cleaning the wound, and covering it with a plaster or dressing.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Sudocrem could be helpful for surface wounds (Image: Getty)

"This will help stop it getting infected. If it's painful, you can take painkillers such as paracetamol or ibuprofen (but do not give aspirin to children under 16)," the guidance says.

The NHS says you should call 999 or go to A&E if the wound is very large, you cannot stop the bleeding, there's something stuck in the cut, or you lose feeling near the wound.

News.title: UK weather maps show thunderstorms hitting 16 counties in just two hours – list
News.content:
UK weather maps show thunderstorms hitting 16 counties in just two hours – list

Heavy rain and lightning are coming this week, with the Met Office having already issued two weather warnings, and several areas could see thunderstorms across a wild two-hour period

View 3 Images Map shows where thunderstorms are likely at 2pm on Wednesday (Image: Ventusky)

Thunderstorms are expected in the UK this week, with weather models showing at least 16 counties facing heavy rain and lightning across just two hours on Wednesday.

‌



BBC Weather says thundery showers are expected in southern parts of England and Wales tonight, before progressing slowly northwards tomorrow. Some showers are expected in Northern Ireland and southern Scotland by the afternoon and evening, the BBC adds.

‌



Further rain and thunderstorms should follow on Thursday, according to BBC Weather, with northern areas most at risk then.

‌



Weather modelling data suggests the south and south-east will see the worst of the thunderstorms at around 2pm on Wednesday, with London potentially in line for heavy rain.

View 3 Images Map shows where thunderstorms are likely at 4pm on Wednesday (Image: Ventusky)

UK weather maps show 13 counties face heavy rain on Thursday with thunderstorms READ MORE :

Just two hours later at 4pm on Wednesday, the models show potential thunderstorms stretching as far north as Staffordshire. In total, the data suggests 16 counties could see serious thunderstorms across those two hours.

‌



UK counties facing thunderstorms on Wednesday

Sussex

Surrey

Kent

Middlesex

Hampshire

Wiltshire

Buckinghamshire

Berkshire

Essex

Bedfordshire

Northamptonshire

Warwickshire

Leicestershire

Derbyshire

Staffordshire

Nottinghamshire

Met Office weather forecast

The Met Office forecast is very similar to BBC Weather, and predicts “heavy showers and thunderstorms” will develop tonight - and could potentially reach Northern Ireland before Wednesday.

The Met Office adds for Wednesday: “Bands of heavy showers and thunderstorms will continue to move northwards through the day. Sunnier moments in between, where it will feel very warm and humid, especially in the south.”

‌



View 3 Images Areas covered by Met Office weather warning on Wednesday (Image: Met Office)

The Met Office has issued a weather warning for thunderstorms on Wednesday, spanning 59 areas across England and Wales. It is in place from 3am and lasts until 10pm. A second warned has been issued for Thursday.

‘Spanish plume’ causing thunderstorms

BBC Weather said a “Spanish plume type of system” could be responsible for the thunderstorms this week.

Article continues below

‘Spanish plume’ is a meteorological term referring to warm air moving northward from Spain which rises and cools, leading to the formation of thunder clouds in the UK

The Met Office explains: “As cooler air spreads from the west, instability increases and the very warm air rises through the cooler air, enhancing the formation of thunderstorms.”

Despite this, temperatures are expected to remain above average this week - potentially peaking at 28C in southern areas on Wednesday.

News.title: Expert warns Brits 'overwhelmed' by money jargon are avoiding their finances
News.content:
Expert warns Brits 'overwhelmed' by money jargon are avoiding their finances

Personal finance expert Rajan Lakhani warns that not understanding key phrases like 'capital gains' and 'compound interest' could cost people dearly, and urges banks to offer clearer explanations.

View 3 Images Money jargon means some Brits are avoiding their finances altogether (Image: Getty Images)

The 25 most baffling financial terms and acronyms include 'capital gains', 'compound interest' and 'variable rate'. A survey of 2,000 adults found that 56% feel overwhelmed by financial jargon, with 42% admitting it puts them off investing altogether.

‌



Almost a third (31%) don't fully grasp what 'capital gains' means, while 23% aren't confident they could explain what 'APR' stands for. Others struggle to understand what an 'unarranged overdraft' (17%), 'credit score' (17%) or 'standing order' (15%) actually means.

‌



The research also revealed that fewer than one in five (17%) feel they completely understand the upcoming changes to ISAs, which will see the Cash ISA allowance changed from £20,000 a year to £12,000 for under 65s, as well as a 22% tax on interest earned on uninvested cash held within a Stocks & Shares ISA.

‌



Even amongst those who claimed at least some understanding of the changes, 41% could not correctly identify the new Cash ISA allowance as £12,000.

View 3 Images Misunderstanding financial jargon can affect Brits’ money decisions (Image: Getty Images)

The study was commissioned by smart money app Plum, which is helping to demystify the confusion by creating a glossary of the most perplexing financial terms.

‌



Rajan Lakhani, personal finance expert for the app said: "Finances can be tricky to navigate, especially with the forthcoming changes to Cash ISAs and Stocks & Shares ISAs.

"Money is something we deal with every day and not understanding something related to our personal finances could cost us dearly. But some of the jargon can be overwhelming – leaving many people simply avoiding their finances and possibly missing out as a result."

He added: "For example, investing has historically been the most reliable way to help avoid inflation eroding the value of your money in the long-term, yet many people are missing out because they don't understand the terms.

‌



"We want people to feel confident managing their money, so hope these clear explanations of the most confusing terms will help when someone isn't sure what something means and how it will impact them."

View 3 Images Low confidence is stopping many Brits from investing (Image: Getty Images)

The research revealed that 28% of adults have no confidence in understanding information from banks and financial providers, with 54% feeling overwhelmed when it comes to making savings and investment decisions.

‌



The internet remains the go-to resource for financial decision-making (41%), ahead of banks (29%) and family members (21%). However, 27% of Gen Z turn to social media for guidance, compared to just 1% of Boomers.

Clearer explanations from banks (51%), financial education in schools (46%) and the use of less jargon in emails and correspondence (43%) were all cited as key solutions to improving understanding.

Rajan Lakhani, from Plum, added: "The research shows confusion about financial terminology makes decisions about money more daunting. It also highlights that many people are not turning to reliable, curated and regulated sources of information.

Article continues below

"We hope by making bitesize financial information accessible and easier to understand, we can help people of all generations feel assured taking control of their finances and planning for the future."

News.title: Airport worker dead as he's run over by plane in front of 'screaming' passengers
News.content:
Airport worker dead as he's run over by plane in front of 'screaming' passengers

A signaller at Montreal-Trudeau International Airport in Canada went under a plane as horrified passengers looked on - the man was rushed to hospital but sadly has died

View Image Montreal-Trudeau International Airport in Montreal, Quebec, Canada (file photo) (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

An airport worker has been killed after a passenger plane ran him over while it was on the tarmac.

‌



The signaller at Montreal-Trudeau International Airport in Canada was rushed to hospital following the horror incident on Monday night - but he has since died.

‌



Preliminary information suggested the plane may have been backing up when the victim was hit, according to local police. The accident occurred shortly before an aircraft due to fly to Paris had been scheduled to take off.

‌



A horrified passenger told Radio Canada of the moment she saw a man go under the plane while it was moving. She reported panicked scenes on board, adding: “Many were screaming.”

Police probe as several motorists seen driving wrong way on M6 following crash READ MORE :

Yves Beauchamp, President and Chief Executive Officer of Montréal Airport said: “The loss of a member of our airport community affects us all deeply. During this difficult time, our thoughts are with the employee’s family, loved ones and colleagues, to whom we extend our heartfelt sympathy and sincere condolences."

‌



The case has reportedly been passed to Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) which will be conducting an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The plane, from the low-cost, long-haul Paris-based airline French Bee, had been due to take off at 6am but was delayed until after midnight, Radio Canada reported.

A French Bee spokesperson said on Monday: “The precise circumstances of the incident have not yet been established.

Article continues below

“French Bee is cooperating fully with Canadian authorities and the various parties involved to help establish the facts.

“The airline's immediate priority is caring for those affected by the incident and supporting its passengers and crew.”

News.title: Notorious Israeli mob boss shot dead by assassin at point-blank range in broad daylight
News.content:
Notorious Israeli mob boss shot dead by assassin at point-blank range in broad daylight

The leader of an Israeli crime group called the 'Caucasian Mafia' was shot and killed by a gunman after stepping out of a petrol station with two associates - a manhunt was launched

View 5 Images Israeli crime boss Yanis Yushvaev was shot dead in public (Image: @PrzemekShura/X)

CCTV caught the moment a dangerous Israeli crime boss was shot in the back of his head and killed by an assassin.

‌



Yanis Yushvaev, the head of Israel's Caucasian Mafia, was killed after stepping out of a petrol station with two associates, on Sunday afternoon. Footage from the petrol station, in the town of Caesarea, between Tel Aviv and Haifa, showed the crime boss and two men walking out of the building while another man, wearing a grey hoodie and cap, walked up the stairs and stood to the side.

‌



The assassin, who made it seem like he was waiting to go into the petrol station, suddenly turned around after the three men walked past and pulled a gun out of his pocket.

‌



View 5 Images Israeli crime boss Yanis Yushvaev was shot dead in public (Image: @PrzemekShura/X)

This shocking footage then showed the killer point the gun right at the back of Yushvaev's head before he pulled the trigger. The 40-year-old mob boss collapsed to the ground and the assassin fled the scene.

One of the crime leader's accomplices attempted to run away as the other man stood and looked around in shock. Yushvaev sustained critical injuries and was pronounced dead shortly after.

‌



View 5 Images Yanis Yushvaev was arrested by police multiple times but never convicted of a crime (Image: @PrzemekShura/X)

Police have launched a probe into the shocking daylight killing and a manhunt for suspects, who they believe fled the scene in vehicles.

Yushvaev in the past claimed he was just a restaurant owning businessman who "drives a Bentley, and that bothers police", but cops said he was the head of "a criminal gang in blood feuds".

‌



View 5 Images The assassin killed the crime boss outside a petrol station (Image: @PrzemekShura/X)

The man had been arrested several times on suspicion of involvement in grenade attacks, shootings and car burnings. Despite this, none of the cases ended up in a conviction, according to the Times of Israel.

Yushvaev was last arrested at Ben Gurion Airport, in Tel Aviv, after travelling from Russia in February - he was released days later. An unnamed police officer previously told Israel's Channel 12 it was "hard to convict him".

Article continues below

View 5 Images The gunman pulled the weapon out of his pocket (Image: @PrzemekShura/X)

This cop said the mob boss "almost never talks on the phone" as he believed his devices were wiretapped and only allegedly only communicated through his "loyal" associates.

Yushvaev, in 2021, was charged and accused of threatening a businessman over an alleged $1.1m debt, according to Ynet. Prosecutors said that when the businessman told the mob boss he could not afford to pay that money within a month Yushvaev allegedly told the man to take out a loan or sell him house, adding: "You have until Dec. 1 to transfer $1.1 million to me or we'll eliminate you."

News.title: Girl dies as air ambulance scrambled to Cornwall cricket club tragedy
News.content:
Girl dies as air ambulance scrambled to Cornwall cricket club tragedy

Emergency services were called to Grampound Road Cricket Club near St Austell as the girl was taken to Derriford Hospital via air ambulance

View Image The chair of the cricket club has offered his 'deepest sympathies' to the girl's family and friends (Image: GOOGLE MAPS)

A teenage girl has died after collapsing at a cricket club in Cornwall during a "tragic incident".

‌



Emergency services including an air ambulance were called to Grampound Road Cricket Club near St Austell after it was reported the girl had collapsed.

‌



She has since died after she was taken to Derriford Hospital in Plymouth following the incident on Thursday evening.

‌



In a statement, Grampound Cricket Club said: "It is with profound sadness that Grampound Road Cricket Club can confirm a tragic incident took place on Thursday evening. A teenage girl collapsed and was taken to hospital, but has now sadly died. This is believed to be a medical incident not connected to cricket."

The club chair Lewis Sanders added: "Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with her family, friends and everyone who knew and loved her at this unimaginably difficult time. We will respect the family’s privacy and ask others to do the same.

‌



"We would also like to thank all those who responded on Thursday evening, particularly those who provided immediate first aid and the emergency services including the Cornwall Air Ambulance."

Cornwall Live reports two double-crewed land ambulances, an air ambulance, an operations officer and a doctor were sent to the scene.

A spokesperson for the South Western Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust (SWASFT) said: "We were called at 20:02hrs on Thursday, August 20, to an incident near St Austell. We sent two double-crewed land ambulances, an air ambulance, an operations officer, and a doctor to the scene.

Article continues below

"We conveyed one patient by air ambulance to Derriford Hospital."

News.title: Father's house rammed before son died in A66 crash
News.content:
A house rammed by a car before the fatal A66 crash in Middlesbrough belonged to the father of a teenager who died in the incident.

Cole Worthy, 17, was one of five young men who died when a Volkswagen Passat travelling in the wrong direction hit a Cleveland Police armed response vehicle, also killing two police officers.

The force said that in the early hours of Saturday, and the previous night, it had received multiple reports of two cars driving dangerously around the town and a Volvo XC60, believed to be linked to the Passat, was seen ramming properties.

There is no suggestion Worthy's father was involved in criminal activity.

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died in the crash, as did Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Worthy.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct said officers had been pursuing the Passat for almost seven minutes after it was connected to earlier alleged criminal activity, but the pursuit was abandoned 10 seconds before the crash when it turned on to the dual carriageway.

Both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number plate recognition technology.

News.title: Trump may hope an 'economic onslaught' will pressure Iran - its leaders are betting otherwise
News.content:
The US says it has launched an "economic onslaught against Iran's financial connections around the globe". Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said sanctions included digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. Any nation financially partnering with Iran would be isolated.

However, Bessent's announcement of what he termed an "economic D-Day" may have sounded more dramatic in Washington than in Tehran.

Shortly after the announcement, Iran's Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh called it "the same old talk" and said Iran was ready for "every scenario". He said Tehran had expected the measures and had plans to deal with them.

His reaction points to the main question Iranian leaders are likely to be asking: What can the US do now that it has not already tried?

Bessent has threatened wider secondary sanctions against countries, banks and companies that continue doing business with Iran. But the basic policy is not new. Iran has faced US sanctions for years, including penalties against foreign companies trading with it.

What matters to Tehran is whether Washington can enforce sanctions more widely than before.

The US blockade has already made a difference. It has reduced Iran's ability to export as much oil by sea as it did before and made it harder to import goods and equipment. Iran has long land borders with seven countries and years of experience using them to bypass sanctions. But land routes cannot easily replace trade by sea, especially oil exports.

The pressure could therefore become much more serious if Washington manages to close channels that survived previous sanctions, particularly those involving China and Iran's neighbours. That is a big ask. China's foreign ministry said on Tuesday that it firmly opposed the sanctions, calling them illegal.

If the sanctions fail, Bessent's announcement could strengthen those inside Iran who oppose a deal with the US.

They could argue that Washington has returned to economic pressure because its other choices are limited. A new military campaign carries risks, while years of sanctions have failed to force Iran to accept US demands.

Washington has also left little room for diplomacy.

Although Pakistan and other mediators are still trying to revive talks, the US has not ruled out further strikes. The renewed threats could weaken Iranian officials who favour a deal.

News.title: Man dies in crash after police pursuit
News.content:
A man has died and two women have been injured in a crash after a police pursuit near Stratford-upon-Avon.

Officers tried to stop a black Audi on Birmingham Road shortly before 17:30 BST on Monday but the driver failed to pull over, Warwickshire Police said.

A pursuit began and 15 minutes later the Audi crashed into a white Ford Puma, the force added, with the Audi's male driver confirmed dead at the scene by paramedics.

The driver of the Ford, a woman, was seriously injured and remains in hospital in critical condition, while injuries to a second woman - her passenger - were serious but not believed to be life-threatening. An investigation by the police watchdog is under way.

Officers said after failing to stop, the Audi made off in the direction of the A46 before travelling back towards Stratford on the A439 Warwick Road where the crash occurred.

A number of other cars were damaged during the pursuit, police said.

Warwick Road was closed on Monday from the Marraway roundabout to its junction with Ingon Lane and Sand Barn Lane, with the stretch remaining shut on Tuesday morning.

It has since reopened.

News.title: Yellow weather warnings issued as thunderstorms and flooding forecast
News.content:
Yellow weather warnings have been issued by the Met Office as heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecast to break out over parts of the UK later this week.

The warnings span Wednesday and Thursday and include parts of east Wales, the Midlands, northern England, East Anglia and southern England - including London.

It is likely to be the one of the most widespread outbreaks of heavy rain across southern and central parts of the UK this summer.

While good news for regions plagued by drought, significant accumulations could lead to flash flooding where the ground is too dry and hard to absorb the downpours. Lightning, large hail and gusty winds are also possible.

News.title: Young people leaving care have death rate four times higher than national average
News.content:
Young adults who have left care have a death rate around four times higher than the general population, a new review, external shows.

Often left alone "with no safety net," the report says the consequences can be catastrophic.

On turning 18, people leaving care in England often lose "significant levers of support", the Government-commissioned report concluded, as it warned the so-called "care cliff" must be addressed.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4 Today, report co-author and broadcaster Ashley John-Baptiste, who grew up in care, called the deaths a national tragedy.

There were 112 deaths of care leavers aged 18 to 24 notified in 2025, which the review said equalled about 130 deaths per 100,000 care leavers.

John-Baptiste recalled his own experience of turning 18 and moving out of the last of four foster homes he'd lived in.

"I was made to live alone and work out how to be an adult," he said.

Unable to afford a bed frame, he says he slept on a mattress on the floor of his council flat and felt a deep sense of abandonment and isolation.

News.title: US judge rejects Ghislaine Maxwell's 'frivolous' appeal against conviction
News.content:
Ghislaine Maxwell's latest bid to overturn her sex trafficking conviction has been rejected by a US judge, who dismissed her claims as "frivolous" and "meritless".

The 64-year-old is serving a 20-year prison sentence for her role in procuring girls for the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein after being found guilty in December 2021.

Maxwell had appealed against her five felony convictions, claiming her constitutional rights had been "violated in multiple respects".

But a New York judge flatly rejected the appeal, describing it as "lengthy and rambling".

Maxwell said Epstein-related documents released by the US Justice Department earlier this year supported her case that she had been wrongly convicted.

But the judge ruled that "far from exculpating her, it incriminates her or reinforces the correctness" of her conviction.

The judge also said her appeal "falls very far from the mark", adding: "Nearly all its claims are procedurally barred; the overwhelming testimonial and documentary evidence adduced at trial conclusively established her guilt; and her petition's claims are demonstrably meritless, and generally based on speculation, distortions, and/or outright falsehoods.

"There is no fact that Maxwell fairly puts in dispute that has any potential to disturb the outcome of her trial."

The judge warned Maxwell against making further appeals, saying it "would not be taken in good faith" by the court.

Maxwell was found guilty in 2021 of facilitating Epstein's abuse. Prosecutors said she recruited and groomed girls, some as young as 14, between 1994 and 2004, before they were abused by Epstein, who died in prison in 2019.

Maxwell appeared virtually before the US House Oversight Committee in February this year but refused to answer questions, invoking her right to remain silent as she pleaded the Fifth Amendment.

Republican House Oversight Committee chairman James Comer said the situation was "very disappointing", adding: "We had many questions to ask about the crimes she and Epstein committed, as well as questions about potential co-conspirators."

Maxwell has previously sought a pardon from US President Donald Trump.

When asked last October whether he would consider pardoning Maxwell, Trump said he "wouldn't consider it or not consider it", adding: "I don't know anything about it, so I will speak to the [Department of Justice]."

The US Senate last month passed a resolution declaring its opposition to a presidential pardon for Maxwell.

News.title: Boy, 3, injured in crocodile attack returns home from hospital
News.content:
A three-year-old boy who was seriously injured in a crocodile enclosure has been discharged from hospital and is settling back in at home, his family has said.

The child returned home "a few weeks ago" and is "happy to be home, playing with his toys, sleeping in his own bed and being a big brother", his parents said in an update posted online.

The boy was visiting Johnsons of Old Hurst near Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, with his family on 18 June when he was attacked by at least one of the animals.

In an update shared on a fundraising page on Monday, the boy's family said it was "nice to have us all back together in the comfort of our own home".

Cambridgeshire Police arrested and bailed a 30-year-old man from Norfolk on suspicion of attempted murder after the incident.

News.title: Inspectors to assess police after Henry Nowak murder
News.content:
An inspection into how a police force responds to violent incidents has been launched in the wake of Henry Nowak's murder.

The 18-year-old student was stabbed in Southampton by Vickrum Digwa, who lied to police and insisted he had been the victim of a racist attack.

Hampshire Police officers initially arrested Nowak and placed him in handcuffs as he lay dying.

His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Service (HMICFRS) will assess the force's processes, training and how officers are supported to make sound and impartial judgements.

The inspection was requested by Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones, who said the public "must have confidence" in the force.

"This inspection will provide an independent assessment of the force's training, processes and culture, including the handling of allegations of racially aggravated assault," she said.

"Henry's family deserve answers, and the public deserve reassurance that their police service is equipped to recognise victims and provide the highest standard of care when it matters most."

News.title: Legendary rugby league winger Boston dies aged 92
News.content:
Rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston has died aged 92.

Last year, he became the first player in rugby league's 130-year history to receive a knighthood.

Born in Cardiff in 1934, Boston grew up playing union but - overlooked by his home club - came to the attention of rugby league scouts while on national service in the north of England, signing for Wigan in 1953 as a 19-year-old.

Despite having played just a handful of games in league, the young winger's talent was quickly evident and Boston was picked for the 1954 Great Britain side that went to Australia and New Zealand - becoming the first black British player to tour down under.

He reached the 100-try milestone in just 68 matches after his switch from union.

Boston's scoring ratio is extraordinary, claiming 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan and helping them win three Challenge Cups and the Championship.

News.title: 'We just want to get home' - dozens stranded in Tunisia after cancelled Belfast flight
News.content:
Dozens of people from Northern Ireland have been left stranded in Tunisia after their EasyJet flight back to Belfast was cancelled and the airline told them it had no other flights available for another 10 days.

A number of people have scrambled for alternative journeys back to Northern Ireland, with one man saying he has spent more than Â£4,000 to get his family of five home.

Some told BBC News NI of passengers running out of medication since the cancellation on Saturday, while others criticised EasyJet over a lack of support and communication.

EasyJet has said it is operating an additional direct flight to Belfast on Tuesday night, and that it was "very sorry" for the inconvenience.

BBC News NI understands more than 100 people were booked onto the cancelled flight that was due to leave Enfidha-Hamamet Airport three days ago.

Stuart McCartney, from Dromore, County Down, said he had spent thousands on accommodation and flights to get his family home via a flight to Brussels.

"I'm willing to pay Â£4,000 to get us home, if needs be, and then battle for reimbursement if I have to after that," he said.

"But we shouldn't have to pay. My holiday was a fraction of what I'm paying to get home right now."

McCartney said EasyJet provided two nights of accommodation but then told the family to find alternative accommodation for the rest of the delay.

He said his mother Katherine, who accompanied his wife and children on the trip, relies on heart medication and they have had to keep a close eye on her remaining supply as the delay continued.

An EasyJet spokesperson said they were "very sorry" that the flight had been cancelled and that the company "have been doing everything we can to support Mr McCartney, providing hotel accommodation and meals and we will be reimbursing expenses that may have been incurred".

Another woman, Martine Murray, said she had run out of an inhaler to treat her COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease) and is anxious to get home to her mother, who is seriously ill.

Chloe McGinty, a student from County Donegal, said it had been "an absolute nightmare".

News.title: More than 70,000 social and affordable homes to be built across England over 10 years
News.content:
Ministers have announced where more than 70,000 social and affordable homes will be built in England over the next 10 years as part of an initial allocation of almost Â£10bn in a bid to address the housing crisis.

Funding has been granted to Greater Manchester, the West Midlands, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, North East England, and Liverpool. An additional Â£6bn was previously announced for London.

It is the first part of a wider plan to build 300,000 social and affordable homes, under the government's Â£39bn social housebuilding programme.

Housing charities welcomed the news but said it was still not enough to meet demand, while the Conservatives said it was an "unfunded spending commitment".

Social housing provides affordable homes at a low cost, managed by social landlords. It includes affordable rented properties as well as low-cost home ownership, such as shared ownership, and can be provided by local authorities and housing associations.

Earlier this year, before he became prime minister, Andy Burnham had called for the entire Â£39bn affordable housing budget for England to be spent on homes for social rent - which means the cost of the unit is about half that of market rents, and there are strict criteria for who can apply for it.

"I would actually devote all of it to social housing," Burnham told The Social Housing Podcast in May.

But of the new homes announced on Monday, 60% would be for social rent.

Housing Minister Matthew Pennycook told BBC Breakfast he did not accept Burnham had failed to meet his previous commitment, saying the government had taken a "pragmatic approach" and wants to "get money out the door".

He said the next tranche of funding would be more focused on council houses - which are usually also classed as homes for social rent.

It is understood ministers decided against giving councils more of the funding announced in the first tranche because they did not believe councils would be in a position to build the required number of social homes.

News.title: Andrew Tate exaggerates and did not own supercars in photos, his lawyers say
News.content:
Controversial influencer Andrew Tate portrays himself as "uberwealthy" but did not own cars and a yacht featured on his social media and exaggerated his lifestyle for online attention, his legal representatives have said.

Tate and his brother Tristan are currently being held in a Florida jail but are seeking release on bail while they await the outcome of extradition proceedings.

They were arrested last month after British prosecutors unveiled new charges including alleged sexual offences against them, which both men deny.

Prosecutors have argued the Tates are a "flight risk", citing the brothers' past statements about their wealth and influence and having multiple identities to evade the law.

In a legal submission to the court, the brothers' legal representatives said the Tates' business model "depends on online attention".

"The outrageousness of the posts by them and about them is the point. The more hyperbolic and outlandish the post, the more likely it will generate views and likes, which in turn generates income. In short, they are playing a role," it says.

At times Andrew Tate has also exaggerated and used hyperbole for "comedic effect" with no intention to be taken seriously, the submission argues.

"The government alleges that the Tates are a risk of flight based on their social media claims that they are 'self-proclaimed billionaires' who own 'high-end vehicles, private jets, and a custom $50-million-dollar superyacht and have unrestricted access to traditional funds, cryptocurrency, and bitcoin,'" it says.

"But the government has not established these grandiose claims are true," it adds.

News.title: Man guilty of killing student after fake Rolex row
News.content:
At about 17:00 GMT on the night he died, Oladipo left his girlfriend's flat carrying a plastic bag of leftover snacks and was on the phone to her while he walked back to his accommodation nearby to watch football.

But outside the De Montfort University's Innovation Centre Innovation Centre, he was met by Dennis who was captured on CCTV walking up and down in the "busy" area.

"It took less than 30 seconds for the two men to come together, to struggle and for the defendant to leave," Osborne told the court.

The court was told Oladipo's girlfriend heard him say "why did you come up and stab me?" over the phone before asking for her to call the ambulance.

A post-mortem examination showed he had suffered six wounds, five to the chest including one which penetrated his heart, and one to his thumb.

Despite being taken to the Leicester Royal Infirmary, he was pronounced dead just over an hour after the stabbing, which took place near the DMU campus.

Giving evidence in his defence on Wednesday, Dennis said he was "fearful" for his life when Oladipo approached him with a knife, adding he was "wrestling" to prevent the 20-year-old from stabbing him.

In cross-examination, prosecutor Jane Osborne KC asked if Dennis knew he had stabbed Oladipo, to which he replied: "I didn't know and I didn't know he was hurt, and I didn't intend to cause any serious harm."

Jurors were shown CCTV footage of Oladipo and Dennis walking towards each other, with Osborne suggesting Dennis used his hands to open a folding knife.

Dennis denied the suggestion he had a knife in his possession, and said he did not leave his accommodation with one.

Addressing Dennis, the prosecutor said there was "bad feeling" between Dennis and Oladipo - and suggested Dennis left his accommodation with a knife "to settle it".

News.title: Burnham refuses to rule out tax rises in autumn Budget
News.content:
Andy Burnham has refused to rule out tax rises in the upcoming autumn Budget, saying he "won't be unrealistic" about the "challenging" state of public finances.

The prime minister said he would take a "careful approach" to the economy, and defended his previously announced cost of living pledges as funded spending commitments.

Burnham became prime minister in July promising to give people breathing space and help with the cost of living, but questions remain over how major policies such as social care reforms will be funded.

Experts have previously warned that he and Chancellor John Healey will have little financial room to manoeuvre in their first Budget on 28 October.

Speaking during his first visit to Ukraine, Burnham said the policies announced so far including capping bus fares at Â£2 and cutting VAT on household electricity bills were "the first steps that I've felt able to make", and were doable because he was able to reprioritise funding from elsewhere.

"I took the decision early on that digital ID wasn't the top priority for now. And so we've reprioritised funding to other priorities," he said in an interview with ITV.

Asked if the public needed to accept some of the new policies would have to be paid for in tax rises, Burnham said they wouldn't necessarily have to accept that.

Pushed on whether he would need to raise taxes to cover spending gaps, he said: "I will always take a careful approach to things. I ran Greater Manchester for 10 years and we ran a very tight ship with rock solid finances.

"Nothing will change as I come into this role as prime minister. I won't take risks with people's jobs or their livelihoods or their family finances.

"I will try to help them in whatever way I can, I have already done some things that will help them."

Burnham previously told the BBC he accepts his earlier announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.

Speaking during his first official overseas visit on Monday, he said while he would do what he could, "I won't be unrealistic and people really need to understand that.

"We are in a challenging position, whatever I do will be carefully thought through, it will be funded and there will be more to come as we go into the autumn."

Last week official figures showed the the government borrowed more than expected in July, despite a record month for income tax receipts.

Inflation also reached a four-month high of 2.9% in July and is expected to rise further due to the ongoing impact of the Iran war, which has hit energy prices and fuel costs.

Experts have warned Burnham and Healey that they need to either raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

Both the prime minister and chancellor have vowed to stick to the fiscal rules set by former chancellor Rachel Reeves.

The rules are designed to ensure day-to-day spending is funded through tax revenue by the end of the Parliament, and to reduce debt as a proportion of GDP.

Rain Newton-Smith, chief executive of the Confederation of British Industry, said business owners wanted to create opportunities for young people but "the cost of employing people has gone up so much".

"The business leaders I speak to say that the cost of doing business has gone up so much that it's holding them back from creating opportunities," she told the Today programme.

She said targeted support for businesses would create "more growth and more opportunities that saves money for the government and ultimately leads to higher tax receipts".

News.title: Man convicted after being caught on CCTV upskirting girl in shopping centre
News.content:
A man has pleaded guilty to filming beneath a young girl's skirt in a shopping centre before running off and later being tracked down on CCTV.

Alex Allegretto, 39, admitted the offence of operating a mobile phone beneath the clothing of another person for the purpose of obtaining sexual gratification.

Police were called to St David's 2 shopping centre on the morning of 7 July after a mother reported Allegretto, who was unknown to them, for upskirting her daughter.

He was caught on CCTV heading back to his car and was later arrested for voyeurism at his home in Maesteg, in Bridgend County Borough.

Allegretto was sentenced at Cardiff Magistrates' Court on 5 August.

The CCTV footage shows Allegretto sat on a bench before quickly walking up behind the victim and her mum in the busy shopping centre and putting his phone by her legs before running away.

Sgt Luis Antony, from South Wales Police, said the victim had continued to be impacted by the incident.

"She is worried about people walking behind her and is anxious when out and about," he added.

Antony said that "nobody should be subjected to this kind of offence".

"The footage clearly shows Alex Allegretto's intentions and what he did to this young girl while she was innocently out shopping with her mother," he added.

"We hope the outcome at court provides some comfort to her and allows her to rebuild her confidence."

The court heard that Allegretto must be registered with the police in accordance with the Sexual Offences Act 2003 , externalfor five years.

He must also do 140 hours of unpaid work, complete rehabilitation activity requirements and pay a financial penalty of Â£199.

News.title: New 10p coin enters circulation - will you spot one?
News.content:
Something new might appear in your change when you pay in cash from now on: a 10p coin featuring the portrait of King Charles and the world's largest grouse.

Sufficient demand for the coins mean newly-minted 10p pieces are entering circulation for the first time for about four years, this time with a new design.

The Royal Mint says shoppers and collectors should discover the coins, which were minted and dated in 2023 and 2026, across the country.

The reverse side of the coin depicts an image of the capercaillie which is found in a small part of Scotland and threatened with extinction.

The redesigned suite of coins to celebrate the King's love of the natural world were unveiled in October 2023 by The Royal Mint.

The tails side of every newly-minted coin from the 1p to the Â£2 now features the country's flora and fauna - from bees to an oak tree leaf.

Coins in circulation in the UK carrying the portrait of King Charles have so far been limited to the 5p, 50p and Â£1.

Old coins with the image of the late Queen Elizabeth II can still be used, so the new coins are only struck in response to demand.

That is why, with 1.4 billion 10p coins in circulation, there has been no need for the new 10p to be released until now by The Royal Mint.

Now. 600,000 of these coins, dated 2023, and 6.5 million dated 2026 have been released to banks and post offices nationwide.

However, King Charles III coins still only represent about 1% of the 24.1 billion coins in circulation across the UK, making any new ones highly sought after by seasoned numismatists and new coin collectors.
