Republicans expect Sen. Darline Graham of South Carolina to lose her runoff race against Rep. Ralph Norman for the primary to replace her brother Lindsey Graham as the Republican nominee for Senate in November, according to a report

President Donald Trump endorsed Graham to replace her brother in the Senate and then to run for a full term after Lindsey Graham died suddenly last month.

But Republicans doubt that Graham, who has no experience in politics before Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her to the seat, can beat Norman, NOTUS reported.

She infamously flubbed a question during a debate with Norman last week about the U.S. position on the South China Sea and Taiwan, when she said “I’m just going to be honest here, I’m not that informed on national security” before adding “But I do support the military.”

“You’re running a campaign with a virtual unknown that took on all of her brother’s unfavorables without any of the goodwill that her brother has in a very short-sprint special election,” one operative with experience in South Carolina told NOTUS.

Lindsey Graham served as the senator since 2003. During that time, he developed a reputation for being a military hawk. But many also saw Graham as a Republican in Name Only for his past support for immigration reform. He initially criticized Trump before becoming one of the president’s biggest allies in Congress.

Sen. Darline Graham (R-SC) speaks during a press conference at a campaign office on August 24. Republicans are now expecting her to lose in a run-off election, according to a report ( Getty )

By contrast, Norman is a member of the hardline House Freedom Caucus, which is often a thorn in the side of Republican leadership. Norman ran for governor earlier this year, but failed to make it to the runoff race alongside fellow Republican Rep. Nancy Mace, who endorsed him for Senate.

Few polling outlets have conducted surveys in South Carolina. But Trafalgar, the conservative pollster, showed a dead heat between Graham and Norman.

“Her only good is hyper-engaged Trump voters. There is no Darline Graham voter,” the operative told NOTUS. “No one’s voting for Darline because of Darline.”

Rep. Russell Fry, who also ran for the Republican nomination for Senate, has endorsed Graham, while former governor Mark Sanford has endorsed Norman.

Trump has for his part gone all-in with Graham. MAGA Inc., the super PAC affiliated with Trump spent $827,711.11 to support her campaign. On Friday, Trump campaigned for her in Myrtle Beach and held a tele-rally for her Monday evening. As a whole, super PACs have pumped in more than $6 million to support her campaign.

One Senate Republican had a blunt response to Graham’s performance.

“Fire the debate preppers,” they told NOTUS. “Anybody with a couple of weeks should have been ready enough for that debate, and there was no evidence of ready in that debate.”

Graham has also criticized people who say she lacks experience, pointing to her work leading the South Carolina Commission for the Blind and her votes as a senator.

“I feel like I’ve done more … in 20 days than he has done in 20 years,” she said.

But Graham faces a challenge considering Norman’s conservative credentials. Organizations such as Turning Point USA have endorsed him.

“He can always outflank you to the right,” the operative told NOTUS, citing how Trump has not criticized Norman too much, despite the fact he endorsed Nikki Haley in the 2024 Republican presidential primary.

“All of the negatives have already been used against him,” the operative said.

Andy Burnham’s £10bn plan to build 70,000 new homes has been billed as the return of the council house – but plenty of Independent readers aren’t convinced it goes far enough.

The prime minister unveiled the funding this week, with 60 per cent earmarked for social rent – a climbdown from his earlier pledge that the whole pot would go on council housing.

The charity Shelter has already warned the total falls well short of the 90,000 homes a year needed to end homelessness, and our community picked up on that gap.

Many pointed out that Britain used to build far more council housing than this, with one commenter estimating annual output was many times higher decades ago than it is now, making Burnham’s promised uplift look modest by comparison.

Others traced the shortage back to Margaret Thatcher’s Right to Buy sell-off in the 1980s, while a lively side debate broke out over who should actually qualify for a council house in the first place.

Here’s what you had to say:

The return of the council house

The plan to allocate funding to councils to build 70,000 new homes is a positive start, although many more will be needed given the shortage of affordable places to live. It’s important for everyone to have a safe, comfortable home – homelessness is never acceptable.

On every occasion when new houses and apartments have been built in my area of Suffolk, promises to add social housing into the mix have been broken, much to my disappointment. This has been happening at intervals over the past 24 years. I really welcome this change in policy and look forward to seeing these buildings completed as soon as possible!

JanetC

We’d need over a million additional skilled workers

So how’s that housing pledge coming along, Angela? 1.5 million new homes over the course of this parliament equates to 300,000 housing starts a year. After two years of Labour, housing starts are running at about 160,000 annually – 10 per cent less than were being built under the Tories in the pre-Covid years.

The housing industry employs about 2 million skilled workers – brickies, electricians, plumbers, plasterers and so on. To increase production to 300,000 units a year, we’d need over a million additional skilled workers. We do not have a million skilled workers idly sitting around, so they’d have to be imported from overseas. Their first ten years or so in the UK would be spent merely building enough new homes to accommodate themselves. Duh.

tobias1

This country struggles to build anything

Sad to see such negativity and pessimism in the comments – no wonder this country struggles to build anything! This is genuinely good news: when these homes are built, they’re built on brownfield, town-centre sites at a reasonably high density with good infrastructure – exactly the places private developers don’t go. I’d like to see powers to strip land from developers who are land-banking, too.

Garlbalunzie

The black hole of the public sector machine

£9bn to councils – that’ll soon melt away into the black hole of the public sector machine.

Councils, irrespective of their political make-up, are painfully slow, bureaucratic and expensive to run. Give them £1,000 for a project and you can bet £950 will be spent on consultants and committees before a brick is laid.

Burnham, Reeves and the chancellor need to find the money for the water, drainage and sewage infrastructure to support all this new building too – and that’s before even one new home is built, let alone the 1.5 million being banded around.

Pablo

It will be 2050 by the time they build them

If the build speed is like a site near us it will be 2050 by the time they build them. Four years to build 72 houses, with numerous issues created for the users of the A road it was built along.

GrampyJeff

A shake-up of allocation rules

If the country can get these houses built, great. But I think the entire process of allocation needs to be re-examined and clarified.

Are council houses to be allocated for life, or only for as long as need exists? The late Bob Crow, of the RMT, had a salary of around £145,000 and yet still occupied his council house. With that level of income, he could have afforded a regular mortgage – by staying in his council house, he was effectively denying its use to a family in greater need.

A family with a son and a daughter may be allocated a three-bedroom house – once the children have grown up and left, should the empty-nest parents be required to downsize? Whatever the outcomes are, they must be transparent and justifiable to the public.

DaveAni

Social housing should never be for sale

The building of new council homes has to be renamed ‘social housing’, and they should never be for sale to tenants or renters. They are designed to accommodate the poor and the needy, not as a money-making proposition. These homes should only be available to local UK citizens and families – end of story.

PJK

The criteria for social housing

Oh dear – so after all the complaints that there aren’t enough affordable homes, it seems, from the comments before this one, that those sounding like angry Reform voters don’t actually want that at all. None of them seem to have read or understood the criteria for being given social housing, including the importance of being locally born or having worked locally for some years – one of many criteria local councils use.

Fallingapart

Your council house was ‘your’ house for life

We moved from the Birmingham slums to a new suburban council estate in the early 50s. It was wonderful, but there was no resemblance to today’s sink estates. First, everyone worked. Second, your council house was ‘your’ house for life, and everyone looked after their property accordingly. Third, we knew our neighbours and hardly anyone moved away. Fourth, there were no gangs of riff-raff making life a misery, and we didn’t even have to worry about locking the door. In Birmingham there were even annual garden competitions that were taken very seriously. This peace and stability for ordinary, lower-income working people – and particularly their children – was destroyed by Thatcherite dogma, and will never return.

Frankie

Excellent plans to reverse the damage done

Excellent plans to reverse the damage done by Margaret Thatcher and the successive Conservative governments that followed. Notwithstanding the lack of council housing, the most serious issue facing would-be house buyers is excessive house price inflation – particularly in London, where property investors and existing homeowners are using equity from that inflation to fund second homes and first-time purchases for their children. These buyers make up a significant percentage of house purchases. Taxing house price inflation as a capital gain would discourage investors and release houses for genuine home buyers.

Rack

Being PM is a poisoned chalice

Being PM is a poisoned chalice. No matter what they pledge and what they do, people will always moan and find fault. I really hope Burnham can find a way to build more social housing, but I won’t join in with those who’ve already written him off so soon. Remember, the alternative is Reform – and that doesn’t bear thinking about.

LV426

Some of the comments have been edited for this article for brevity and clarity.

Hundreds of thousands of pensioners are set to be contacted by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) as it begins work to cut £370 million from the benefits bill.

The department said it has started contacting “selected customers” as part of a Pension Credit case review campaign, first announced by former chancellor Rachel Reeves at last year’s Budget.

Around 95,000 to 100,000 claimants are expected to see their payments reduced over the course of the work, estimates calculated by The Independent suggest.

The number of Pension Credit claimants who are selected for review will likely be much higher, although the DWP has declined to share how it is selecting cases.

In an update to employment groups, it said: “Being selected for a review does not mean the customer has done anything wrong.”

Some claimants will need to provide additional information if their case is reviewed, the message added, which could include recent bank statements.

open image in gallery The DWP has started contacting ‘selected customers’ as part of a Pension Credit case review campaign ( Getty/iStock )

Details of the Pension Credit review drive released by the Treasury last year show that the government expects it to save £370 million by April 2031.

This year alone, the DWP is set to claw back £15 million from the reviews. This will mean around 10,700 claimants seeing their entitlement reduced, based on an average overpayment of £1,400.

Pension Credit provides a financial top-up to those above pension age who are on a low income. It can boost weekly income to £238 for single claimants (or £363.25 for couples).

This equates to £12,376 a year – below the full state pension.

There are also extra rates payable to claimants who have a severe disability, caring responsibilities, young children or certain housing costs.

It comes after a similar drive to reduce overpayments in the Universal Credit system, which the government projects will save £13.6bn by 2030.

Fraud and error statistics released by the DWP in May revealed that the proportion of Pension Credit claims overpaid rose to 33 per cent in 2025/26, up from 28 per cent the year before.

open image in gallery Around 10,700 claimants are likely to see their entitlement reduced this year, based on an average overpayment of £1,400 ( PA Wire )

The two main causes of this were claimants under-declaring their financial assets, or going abroad for a longer period than is allowed under the rules.

Pension Credit is often called a ‘passport’ benefit as it can also unlock eligibility for extra support like housing benefit, support with mortgages and a free TV licence.

Taken together, the benefit could be worth up to £9,665 for the most vulnerable pensioners, but it has historically gone vastly underclaimed.

Around 761,000 pensioners are estimated to have missed out on the benefit in 2025/26, figures from research unit Policy in Practice have found – worth a combined £1.6 million.

Last October, the government launched a take-up campaign for the benefit, resulting in an extra 33,500 awards.

A DWP spokesperson said: “We know that a claimant’s circumstances can change throughout their claim, which can lead to their claim being incorrect. By reviewing claims, we can ensure claimants are receiving the correct entitlement.

“The government wants all pensioners to get the support they are rightly entitled to and thanks to our biggest ever Pension Credit take-up campaign, we have seen an additional 33,500 Pension Credit awards in 2025, worth on average £87 a week, compared with the previous year.”

News.title: Five more people arrested over fatal A66 crash that killed two police officers
News.content:

A 16-year-old boy is among five more people arrested by detectives investigating events leading up to a crash on the A66 that killed two police officers and five others.

It brings the total number of arrests to 17 following the fatal crash near Middlesbrough in the early hours of Saturday.

PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, were killed when a Volkswagen Passat, which had been pursued by police, was driven the wrong way along a dual carriageway and hit their marked armed-response vehicle.

Cleveland Police say they have now arrested five more people with the help of the National Crime Agency and the North East Regional Organised Crime Unit.

The force said those arrested were a boy aged 16, an 18-year-old and a man of 21, all on suspicion of participating in an organised crime group; a 23-year-old on suspicion of making threats to kill and a 55-year-old on suspicion of assisting an offender.

Two of the 12 people previously arrested have already appeared in court.

Kai Beattie, 19, of Foxrush Court, Redcar, appeared before Teesside Magistrates’ Court charged with possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life, according to police.

open image in gallery Two police officers were killed in the crash ( Getty )

Cameron George, 26, of Micklow Close, Redcar, was remanded in custody to appear at Teesside Crown Court on 21 September charged with drugs offences and possession of criminal property.

Detectives say the five young men in the Passat may have had links to “serious and organised criminal activity”.

Four of the five had criminal convictions, and were believed to be linked with another car that had rammed properties earlier that morning.

Inquests are due to open on Thursday morning for the two officers.

Inquests on the five people in the Passat, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and 23-year-olds Michael Robert Cahill and Jacob Matusiak, are scheduled for the afternoon at Teesside Magistrates’ Court.

Cleveland Police say they received reports of two cars being driven dangerously on the morning of the collision.

The first, believed to be a Volvo XC60, was seen ramming properties in the Middlesbrough area.

open image in gallery The scene near the A66 in South Bank, near Middlesbrough following a fatal crash involving a police car and a Volkswagen Passat in which seven people died, including two police officers (Richard McCarthy/PA) ( PA Wire )

The second, a Volkswagen Passat, is believed to have been linked with the activities of the Volvo. Police said both cars had cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number-plate-recognition technology.

The Volvo was later found in Middlesbrough.

Police said there was no evidence that filming of the activities on Friday night and Saturday morning was “for the purposes of TikTok”.

Last week, four people were seriously injured in Ireland when a BMW sped the wrong way up a motorway, smashing into a family car, amid a surge in reckless driving for videos to post on social media. The five teenage boys in the BMW were killed.

Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox, of Cleveland Police, responsible for the strategic leadership of the investigation, said: “This has been a fast-moving and complex investigation, with significant links to serious and organised criminal activity.”

He added: “We have a duty to respond to, and thoroughly investigate, the serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident, and to bring all those responsible to justice.”

More than £750,000 has been raised for the families of the two police officers who were killed.

A fundraiser created by the Cleveland Police Federation said funds raised would be split equally between the two officers’ families and the federation would continue to provide support.

Cleveland Police launched the chase after receiving intelligence relating to “numerous incidents” linked to a Passat, which activated an ANPR camera and is believed to have been using cloned plates, investigating watchdog the Independent Office for Police Conduct said.

open image in gallery Tributes have been paid to the police officers who died in the crash ( Getty )

Pc Blades and Pc Clough were not involved in the original pursuit, but had been called to the area to assist with the search for the Passat.

Family members described former Civil Nuclear Constabulary officer Pc Clough as “our hero” who was “always on public duty”.

In a statement issued by Cleveland Police, Pc Blades’ wife called him “my beloved husband, my best friend, and the most devoted father to our two young boys”.

Tributes for the five young men were also shared on social media, with many of their friends saying they “can’t believe it” and were “heartbroken” and “lost for words”.

Balloon releases have been announced in their memory at different locations.

Meanwhile, Paul Williams, acting deputy national chairman for the Police Federation of England and Wales, appeared on BBC Breakfast on Tuesday morning as he claimed young people are “baiting police officers” with dangerous driving.

Williams said: “Every day we can identify now numerous examples of young people sensationalising dangerous driving.

“Not just dangerous driving, but baiting police officers who are out there to protect the public. It’s a real problem. It’s causing officers concern.

“They shouldn’t have to be going out and worrying about whether they’re going to return home from their shift or not. But on top of that, wondering if they’re going to be plastered all over social media.

“It’s absolutely unacceptable and social media platforms need to take some action.”

News.title: Polygamous leader featured in Netflix series faces sentencing after girls rescued from trailer
News.content:

A polygamous sect leader featured in Netflix’s Trust Me: The False Prophet is set to be sentenced Tuesday after three girls were rescued from harrowing conditions inside an unventilated trailer.

Samuel Bateman, 50, is already serving a 50-year federal prison sentence for orchestrating sex involving children. In a separate case, he was convicted of three counts of child abuse stemming from an August 2022 traffic stop in Flagstaff.

Someone had tipped off authorities after seeing small fingers reaching through gaps in the doors of a trailer. Three girls, ages 11 to 14, were found inside the trailer, which had a makeshift toilet, sofa and camping chairs and lacked air conditioning and seat belts.

open image in gallery Samuel Bateman is a self-proclaimed prophet who previously claimed to have more than 20 ’spiritual wives,’ including 10 girls under the age of 18 ( Coconino County Sheriff's Department )

Each count carries a mandatory sentence between four and eight years. A judge will have discretion to run the counts consecutively or concurrently.

Samuel Bateman’s previous conviction

Bateman, a self-proclaimed prophet, previously claimed to have more than 20 “spiritual wives,” including 10 girls under the age of 18. His small group was an offshoot of the polygamous sect once led by Warren Jeffs.

He is currently serving 50 years in federal prison for coercing girls as young as 9 to submit to sex acts with him and other adults, and for scheming to kidnap girls from protective custody.

In the state case, Bateman admitted he knew the girls were in a hot trailer for hours and that the ventilation wasn’t good but he downplayed the conditions.

open image in gallery Bateman’s small group was an offshoot of the polygamous sect once led by Warren Jeffs (pictured) ( Getty Images )

Bateman isn’t a lawyer yet represented himself at trial. He claimed he thought the girls had gotten out when they stopped.

He said he was as “shocked as could possibly be” when he learned that they were still inside when he was pulled over.

Federal authorities said Bateman traveled extensively between Arizona, Utah, Colorado and Nebraska as he built an offshoot network of the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, which historically has been based in the neighboring communities of Colorado City, Arizona, and Hildale, Utah.

He and his followers practiced polygamy, a legacy of the early teachings of the mainstream Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, which abandoned the practice in 1890 and now strictly prohibits it.

open image in gallery Federal authorities said Bateman traveled extensively between Arizona, Utah, Colorado and Nebraska as he built an offshoot network of the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints ( AP Photo/Rick Bowmer )

Bateman was one of the trusted followers of Jeffs, who previously led the sect and is serving a life sentence in Texas for sexual assault of children.

The influence of the polygamous sect has waned significantly over time in the towns where it has historically been based. In 2017, a court order placed the towns under supervision, excising the church from their governments and shared police department.

The area has since transformed so quickly that the towns were released from court-ordered supervision last summer, almost two years earlier than expected. Practicing sect members are now believed to account for only a small percentage of the towns’ populations.

Siya Kolisi has been passed fit to captain South Africa in the second Test against New Zealand in Cape Town in a significant boost for the Springboks.

Kolisi had been bracketed alongside Paul de Villiers in the No 6 shirt when Rassie Erasmus named his team for the encounter on Monday, with the 35-year-old having suffered two hamstring injuries this summer.

But the flanker has now been declared good to go as the Springboks look to hit back having fallen 1-0 behind, with Kolisi taking the captaincy from Pieter-Steph du Toit after coming through training.

“Siya will be starting and he will captain the team,” Erasmus said with De Villiers displaced after starting the first Test.

“It was a hamstring niggle, not something major like he had before 2019 or 2023. It was a grade two tear, and it takes a little time to recover, and that's why we've been cautious.

“Last week it was touch and go, but we told him he had to run full out on Monday and he did so on Tuesday as well without any discomfort, so he's good to go.”

Fellow flanker Du Toit had led in Kolisi’s stead during July’s Nations Championship, and at Ellis Park on Saturday.

He will win his 100th cap in Cape Town, which Erasmus explained had played a part in his captaincy call.

“Pieter-Steph just took the captaincy for us on Monday so Siya could fully concentrate on his recovery and his work, and I had a chat with Pieter-Steph today and he agreed,” Erasmus stressed.

“In this match you probably don't want captaincy responsibilities, with the 100 to think about, and on top of that needing to play well, so Siya is our captain.

“The 23 guys who played together against Argentina played really well, and it’s not just his game that is good, he's a very inspirational person who means a lot to this team on and off the field.”

The four-match Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series continues with another meeting in Johannesburg on 5 September, before concluding in Baltimore seven days later.

North West might belong to a family worth billions of dollars, but she is ready to cut her grill-adorned teeth behind the Starbucks counter.

The 13-year-old daughter of Kim Kardashian and Kanye West revealed in an interview with Dazed magazine published Monday that, following the release of her debut album N0rth4evr in May, she plans to pursue music full-time one day — but not before she lives out her dream of being a barista.

“I still wanna work,” the teen told the outlet. “I wanna work at, like, Starbucks next year. I think I can next year ‘cause I’m gonna be 14, so… I think I can.”

“I want to have a regular job, I guess,” she added.

Employees typically have to be at least 16 years old to work at most Starbucks locations. The Independent has reached out to Starbucks for comment.

open image in gallery North West says she wants to have a ‘regular job’ amid her growing music career ( Instagram )

Although she is eyeing coffee as a side gig, North made it clear that she is serious about her music career by pushing back on critics who encourage her to wait until she is older to put out records.

“It’s like, nah, this is my hobby,” North explained. “This is what I like to do, this is what I wanna do with my life.”

North was just 12 years old when she flung herself into the rock star scene by dropping her debut EP and then making a surprise appearance on stage with Molly Santana at Rolling Loud festival in Orlando shortly after.

In June, she went on to make her first-ever solo music festival performance at Lyrical Lemonade’s Summer Smash in Bridgeview, Illinois.

open image in gallery North West is the eldest daughter of Kim Kardashian and Kanye West ( Getty )

However, the young rapper’s fans were disappointed when plans for her first headlining tour were called off earlier this month.

The 14-date North American tour with Molly Santana was set to kick off August 5 in Dallas, Texas, and end August 27 in Los Angeles, but was abruptly canceled days before the first show.

“I was really excited to go on tour (with) Molly Santana, sadly it isn’t happening anymore, but I have something special for you guys, see you soon,” North said in a statement at the time.

Plus, the teen is not limiting herself to one creative pursuit. Before her Starbucks dreams, North and her mom appeared to be laying out the groundwork for her to launch her own fashion empire when the Kardashians’ family lawyers filed three trademark applications earlier this year for the brand NOR11.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed ​that Iran tried to kill one of his sons.

However, he gave no details about when the alleged plot took place, which son was targeted or how close it came to ⁠being carried out.

Netanyahu's allegation underscores the heightened tensions since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran began in February, during which Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and other senior Iranian leaders were killed.

Netanyahu, whose coalition is trailing in opinion polls two months before ⁠an October 27 general election, made ​the ⁠claim in a telephone interview with Israel's Channel 14. He was responding to reports that one of Israel's security agencies had refused ⁠to provide protection for a political rival ahead of the nationwide vote.

"As ​for ⁠my sons. Here, I think ‌there is something quite unbelievable, yes. Iran targeted one of my sons. Iran tried to kill, to murder one of my sons," Netanyahu ‌told the conservative channel known for its favourable ‌coverage of the government.

"Iran tried to murder one of my sons, and therefore this security protection is not a luxury," he said, without providing any further details about the ⁠alleged plot or how close it came to being carried out.

It was not immediately clear which of his sons he was referring to. Netanyahu's elder son, Yair, lives in Miami.

open image in gallery Avner, the son of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ( AFP/Getty )

Iran's mission at the United Nations in New York did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the accusation.

Netanyahu also said he had told the Shin Bet ‌security agency chief David Zini that appropriate security should be provided for ​any prime ministerial candidate.

Israeli media had reported earlier that ‌Zini declined to provide security for ⁠Gadi Eisenkot and told the country's election authority there was no ⁠plot to harm him.

Eisenkot's party is projected to win the largest number of seats in ‌the election, although ​Israeli governments are usually formed through coalitions ‌among multiple parties rather than ​by a single party winning a parliamentary majority outright.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
News.content:
“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

Sports.title: Chelsea legend QUITS England role after five years after landing ill-fated first role in management
Sports.content:
ASHLEY COLE has quit his England under-21 role after five years and SunSport understands he made the decision months before his ill-fated first job in management.

The Chelsea legend stepped down from his position with the young Lions in March before taking charge of Italian side Cesena.



The FA has now confirmed Cole will not return to his role with England.

His departure comes after the 45-year-old ended his short-lived spell as Cesena boss following just eight games in charge.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

Cole landed his first managerial job with the Serie B club in March, having previously worked as part of the coaching staff at Everton and Derby.

But after just three months at the helm, he decided to walk away following discussions with Cesena’s sporting director over a change in the club’s strategy.



Cole announced his departure on Instagram.

He wrote: “As my tenure at Cesena FC concludes today, I want to thank the players and staff for their hard work and commitment over the last few months.

“I was proud to bring my experience to such a passionate club, and I’ve truly enjoyed working with the squad to introduce a new identity and prepare for the season ahead.

“Following recent discussions with the Sporting Director regarding a change in the club’s strategy, I have decided that it is best for me to move on.



“I leave with great respect for all the people there, as well as the fans, and look forward to my next challenge.”

Cole signed a short-term contract with Cesena when he took over in March, with the option to extend if he met “certain conditions”.

But his first spell in management proved a major struggle.

He managed just one victory during his eight games in charge, alongside three draws and four defeats.

His appointment was met with a mixed reaction from Cesena supporters, while there were also reports of unrest among some players.



Cole also admitted he had struggled with the language barrier after moving to Italy.

The former Arsenal and Chelsea full-back had previously spent two years in Italy as a player with Roma, making 16 appearances for the club.

Sports.title: Man Utd are leaving it too late with Luke Shaw transfer decision – the club’s longest-serving player should be long gone
Sports.content:
LUKE SHAW has been at Manchester United for so long it is easy to forget that Louis van Gaal scolded him over his lack of fitness weeks into his Old Trafford career.

Van Gaal branded Shaw “not very fit”. The Dutchman was such a hard taskmaster during Shaw’s first pre-season tour he made him train on the morning of a friendly with Inter Milan in Washington DC.



Shaw, 31 and into the final year of his United contract, was fit last season. He became only their sixth player to start all 38 Premier League games in a season. Shaw completed 90 minutes in 25 of them.

It was the first season that Shaw came through unscathed and he started his 13th with United at Hull on Saturday.



Shaw has played in at least 30 games in five out of 12 United seasons. Between February 2024 and April 2025, Shaw started more games at the European Championship than for United.

He returned from Euro 2024 and sustained a calf injury on his first day of pre-season at Carrington. Shaw was back for Ruben Amorim’s first game in charge at Ipswich three months later.

Some cynical United fans feel Shaw tends to be available when there is something to play for: a new manager’s arrival or an international tournament on the horizon.

Shaw has had three good seasons in 12. One was in Erik ten Hag’s first year and the other two were heading into international tournaments.

There was a time when it was fair to accuse Shaw of being more invested in his country than his club. Shaw was the standout left back at Euro 2020 and regressed upon his return to United, playing in barely half of their Premier League games in 2021-22.

Shaw has spent twice as long at United as Cristiano Ronaldo did during his first spell. He has played more times for the club than Duncan Edwards, Norman Whiteside and Ruud van Nistelrooy.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

By rights, Shaw should be long gone. Jose Mourinho felt Shaw was too immature and tracked numerous left backs. He was overruled by that football specialist Ed Woodward in a power play back in 2018.

A United player was once recovering from injury and so astonished to see United’s fitness coach outsprinting Shaw during a lap that he started filming it. The video surfaced in WhatsApp groups in professional football.

Those who encountered Shaw during his early years at United have noticed how much he has matured. He once blamed his late arrival for training on his mother sleeping through her alarm and not waking him.

Shaw and his partner, Anouska, welcomed their fourth child this year, so they have plenty of back-up alarms now.

The true endurance test of Shaw will come next month when United get back into the swing of midweek Champions League nights. Their first tie precedes the Manchester derby at Old Trafford.



The last time Shaw managed successive weekend and midweek starts was in May 2025, shortly after his comeback from another spell on the treatment table.

Shaw started three successive games, culminating in the woeful Europa League final loss to Tottenham. He only got the nod as Diogo Dalot had not fully recovered from a rare injury to start.

The previous time Shaw recorded a sustained starting run in domestic and European fixtures was eight starts in November and December 2023. Shaw has not lined up in at least ten consecutive league and European games since March 2020 – before the Covid-19 pandemic.

United looked leaden at Hull and Shaw was one of six starters who had a full pre-season. He saw out the 90 minutes and completed four ‘key’ passes (when a pass directly leads to a teammate’s shot).



Time will tell if Shaw has shot his last bolt this season. Whether or not this is his last at United, they have belatedly decided he needs competition.

United have left it too late with their prime target, Lewis Hall. New Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle scoffed at an attempt by Peter Schmeichel to reignite speculation..

United have ample alternative left backs: Harry Amass and Patrick Dorgu are left-footed while right back duo Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have both filled in on the opposite side.

There is another. Diego Leon was pointlessly presented to the Old Trafford crowd last year and has never trained under Carrick.

Dorgu is considered a left winger by Carrick and United are prepared to cash in on academy graduate Amass. But they have shown such reluctance to invest considerably in a statement signing that Hall seemed a long shot before Jaissle shot it down.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Defensive midfield and left back would have been high on United fans’ priority lists. If they are to make two more signings, they will arrive in the final week of the transfer window.

That happened under Van Gaal 12 years ago. Shaw was injured at the time.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes dreams of TATTOOING Premier League and Champions League trophies on his body as Arsenal ace eyes titles
Sports.content:
BRUNO GUIMARAES is dreaming of tattooing the Champions League and Premier League trophies on his body after joining Arsenal.

The midfielder, 28, moved to the Gunners from Newcastle this summer as part of a deal worth £75million.



And the Brazilian has set his sights on trophies after making the move down south to the Prem champs.

Guimaraes has the silverware he has won tattooed on his body – including Newcastle’s Carabao Cup triumph last year.



And asked what trophies he wanted to add to it, the Samba star said: “I would say the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, Carabao Cup – everything is possible.

“I just want to win no matter what and, like I said, I am so competitive. Everything for me is important.



“But yeah, I would say the Premier League and Champions League would be very special.

“I have a lot of space for trophies. I don’t know where they (the tattoos) would go, on my legs probably.”

Guimaraes, who missed Arsenal’s opening Prem victory over Coventry last week with a groin issue, took the No39 shirt after moving to the Emirates.

The number is significant to the midfielder as it is the one that his father had on his taxi when working in Rio de Janeiro.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Guimaraes chose to have it on his shirt as a reminder of the sacrifices his family made to progress his career.

He told the Men In Blazers Media Network: “The number and the history of my father just gives me more inspiration.

“Every time I put the shirt on, I remind myself where I come from, where my family comes from.

“Not just my father, but my mum and everyone. They give me inspiration to, no matter what, be hungry for more.

“That is the mentality, that when my kids grow up, I want to teach them as well because my family has come so far – and now it is time to improve.



“My father always believed. My mum always believed. The times when I wanted to give up when I was kid, when I heard my first ‘no’ in my career, they said, ‘No, you will not quit’.

“And that was very important and now I just describe myself as a warrior because I have been through many, many things in my life.

“A warrior means never giving up, no matter what the situation you are going through. You have to always believe.”

Sports.title: Fans say Carabao Cup third round draw is ‘FIXED’ as ‘pre-draw’ with only eight teams in it set to take place
Sports.content:
THE Carabao Cup third round draw is set to include a “pre-draw” only featuring the eight teams competing in the Champions League and Europa League.

And some fans are unhappy with the format, making unfounded claims that the draw is “fixed”.



The pre-draw is set to take place ahead of Everton‘s tie at Preston.

Carabao Cup chiefs confirmed: “Before the main draw, there will be a pre-draw to decide whether each of the eight Champions League and Europa League Clubs will be at home or away.”



This means that Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Sunderland and Crystal Palace cannot draw each other until round four.

Brighton, meanwhile, are NOT part of the pre-draw, as the Conference League does not get underway until October.

The main draw will take place after Preston vs Everton, with the EFL confirming: “In the main draw, to be conducted after the Round Two tie, the first eight ties will involve those Champions League and Europa League Clubs, with their home or away position already having been decided, and each will be drawn against a club from a separate bowl containing the remaining teams.

“Once those eight ties have been drawn, the final eight ties will be drawn as normal.”

The change first came into effect during the 2024-25 season, when Uefa revamped their competitions to include a 36-team “Swiss model” league phase.

Extra games for European sides meant that certain Carabao Cup ties could create scheduling conflicts.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Carabao Cup second round fixtures Tuesday 25 August: Cardiff vs Norwich Doncaster vs Middlesbrough Barnsley vs Crewe Blackburn vs Sheffield United Blackpool vs Lincoln Cambridge vs Millwall Fleetwood vs Shrewsbury Ipswich vs Leicester Plymouth Argyle vs Coventry Sheffield Wednesday vs Wolves Southampton vs West Ham Stevenage vs Reading Stoke vs Hull Walsall vs Leyton Orient Watford vs Peterborough Birmingham vs Brentford Nottingham Forest vs Leeds Wednesday 26 August Bradford vs Burnley Newcastle vs West Brom Tottenham vs Charlton Preston vs Everton Thursday 27 August Chelsea vs Luton Fulham vs AFC Wimbledon

The third round is set to be split between the weeks commencing September 7 and September 14.

With the Champions League kicking off during the first of those weeks, and the Europa League the second, those clubs drawing each other in the Carabao Cup would leave them without an available fixture slot in which to play the game.

Despite the clear explanation, some fans were left fuming.

One cried on X: “Elaborate way of pretending its not fixed.”

And a second fumed: “Bulls***, paving the easy route for the European clubs. Sick of football man”.



A third blasted: “Pure corruption……no wonder we don’t get any surprises in this competition anymore….sponsors want the big teams in the final….games gone”.

And another added: “Better still, just put the top 8 Premiership teams in the QF…. and we can all save wasting our time.”

Having not qualified for Europe this term, both Chelsea and Tottenham have entered the competition at the second round stage.

Spurs are set to host Charlton on Wednesday, while Chelsea welcome Luton 24 hours later.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes calls out three Man Utd stars for Hull embarrassment as he tells Bruno Fernandes ‘keep your mouth shut’
Sports.content:
PAUL SCHOLES has slammed a number of Manchester United stars following the club’s embarrassing opening weekend defeat to Hull.

The Red Devils were stunned by two set-piece goals from the newly promoted outfit – the first time they have ever lost to a promoted side on opening day.



Some of the players chose to air their frustrations after the match, with captain Bruno Fernandes being especially vocal about his side’s short-comings.

He said: “Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game we give too much of the ball to them.



“We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set-plays and not concede these types of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.”

But Scholes was none too impressed by the skipper’s comments, and slammed Fernandes and another United star for their own part in the shocking result.



Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite, Scholes said of the comments: “I’d be interested to know what (Fernandes) means by that. What mistakes were they giving set-piece goals away?

“Especially when you perform the way he did as well, I think it’s probably best to keep your mouth shut, because he didn’t have his best performance either, and there was quite a few of them like that.

Paddy McGuinness chimed in to add: “Luke Shaw said they could have been better prepared as well.”

To which Scholes responded: “Luke Shaw always says something.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“That’s a slight on your staff, that’s a slight on your manager. If one of your players was saying that, f***ing hell you’d have him in Monday morning wouldn’t you, ‘what do you mean by that?'”

The pair were not the only United stars that Scholes singled out. He and co-host Dion Dublin were perplexed by Harry Maguire‘s role in Hull’s first goal.

The England international appeared to mark Noussair Mazraoui rather than an opposition player in the box, allowing Semi Ajayi to pounce on a rebound which either man could possibly have cleared if they were not in each other’s way.

Scholes said: “I think he’s (Maguire) just lost his bearings or something, I don’t know. I don’t think he’s looking at the players, he’s looking at the ball, isn’t he?



“The only thing I can think is that he’s lost his bearings and he’s looking at the ball and he could feel somebody in front of him, and he’s just gone like that (hugged him).”

Dublin added: “It’s an odd one because if he hadn’t had that instinct, then he might have been able to stop the goal or kick the ball away, but he just sort of froze and looked and he’s hugging his mate and he’s gone, ‘They’re gonna score in a minute!'”

Scholes even called for Maguire to break down the moment himself, adding: “It doesn’t look good, does it? I’d like to hear him explain it.”

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola's behaviour speaks volumes as Liverpool transfer chances emerge
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola's behaviour speaks volumes as Liverpool transfer chances emerge

Liverpool are still trying to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain before this summer transfer window ends, as new head coach Andoni Iraola wants wingers

View 2 Images Liverpool are determined to take Bradley Barcola to Anfield before the transfer window shuts (Image: LOU BENOIST, AFP via Getty Images)

Bradley Barcola and his entourage are not panicking about the length of negotiations between Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain as his transfer saga drags on. It is said they remain confident that both clubs will reach an agreement before the end of this summer transfer window at 11pm on 1 September.

‌



PSG have left Barcola out of the squad for their last two matches. The first was the French Super Cup, which they lost 1-0 to Lens. However, he was photographed training the day beforehand, and also attended the match.

‌



Barcola has not been involved for a fortnight since being an unused substitute in the UEFA Super Cup win over Aston Villa. PSG's only remaining match before the transfer deadline is on Friday night against Lille.

‌



All sides involved in Barcola transfer negotiations appear hopeful that a switch to Liverpool will be finalised during the final days of the summer window. The winger has been linked with the Reds in recent months, however, the process has required patience from all concerned, as several critical elements still need to fall into place.

The initial considerations for Liverpool focused on a genuine willingness to pursue a deal. With Barcola entering the final two years of his Parc des Princes contract, he needed to signal his readiness to leave to force PSG into a decision.

Liverpool will ignore Jamie Carragher's desperate transfer plea with focus elsewhere READ MORE :

Virgil van Dijk sends Liverpool chiefs transfer message with Andoni Iraola in agreement READ MORE :

Once that became apparent, the French and European champions faced the question of whether a sale would best serve their interests in maximising the player's market value. This decision subsequently came to pass.

‌



Liverpool then needed to establish themselves as the leading contenders to land Barcola, which happened swiftly, before PSG set about identifying replacements in the transfer market to bolster their own attacking ranks. Everything fell into place for the Reds, who then faced the most daunting hurdle of all: club-to-club negotiations.

Les Parisiens placed a hefty price tag on the winger, creating a significant gap between the two clubs that needed to be closed before any deal could be struck. PSG knocked back initial bids as Liverpool looked to formalise their interest, with talks continuing deep into the final week of the transfer window.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola has not been in a Paris Saint-Germain matchday squad since the UEFA Super Cup (Image: SOPA Images, SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It now appears the drawn-out saga is at last moving towards a conclusion that works for all involved, with widespread expectation that Barcola will ultimately complete his move to Anfield. According to a report from L'Equipe, Liverpool are readying a final bid for the winger that they are confident PSG will accept, following a narrowing of the valuation gap between the two clubs over recent weeks.

It is understood that Barcola and his representatives are growing increasingly optimistic that a deal will be struck, with 'nobody in panic mode', despite the apparent lack of progress thus far. There is an expectation that the transfer fee will exceed the Ligue Un record for a sale to a foreign club, surpassing both Ayyoub Bouaddi's impending switch to Manchester City this summer and Neymar's move to Al-Hilal in 2023.

‌



The exact final sum remains unclear, with those details to be finalised in the dying days of the summer transfer window. Nevertheless, the deal would significantly strengthen Liverpool's attacking arsenal.

This marks just one of multiple expected transactions in Liverpool's late transfer flurry, with attention still focused on Minteh to bolster the right-wing choices at Andoni Iraola's disposal. Meanwhile, Cody Gakpo remains the subject of rumours regarding a potential exit. All of which suggests a frantic final week in the market for the Reds, with substantial business to be completed both incoming and outgoing at the club.

Sports.title: Joao Pedro predicts trophies for Chelsea thanks to 'very special' attacking weapons
Sports.content:
Joao Pedro predicts trophies for Chelsea thanks to 'very special' attacking weapons

Chelsea kicked off their Premier League campaign under Xabi Alonso with a 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday night, with Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers all scoring

View 2 Images Chelsea put Fulham to the sword at Craven Cottage (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC)

Joao Pedro believes Chelsea’s deadly trio will leave Premier League defenders chasing shadows this season.

‌



Chelsea forwards Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer were all on target in their first win of the season at Fulham to send out a clear title warning to the rest. They have got big trophies in their sights under new boss Xabi Alonso and Chelsea might just have the best forward line in the top flight.

‌



Brazil star Pedro believes their movement, understanding and goals will make them “very special” and incredibly difficult to stop.

‌



He said: “Cole and Morgan are special players. Everyone knows that. I'm very grateful to play with them because I know if I make some runs, if you know Cole, Morgan's going to give the ball to me and I have to be ready to score. So it's very special.

“I think now in the game, if we move a lot, it will be difficult for defenders to pick up one player to stay. And the manager let us be free on the pitch, so we understand each other well. I think this helps us, and hopefully, it can happen more times.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“When you play for Chelsea, you always need to look for that (the biggest trophies), and I think we’ve already had a great game to show our power and hopefully we can continue like this in the season.”

Chelsea boss Alonso clearly has a turbo-charged front three because Pedro and Palmer had the summer off after not making the Brazil and England squads respectively. Rogers is the club’s £117m British record transfer buy and looks energized after England’s World Cup campaign.

‌



They have been marked down by many pundits as potential challengers to champions Arsenal as they have an elite manager and, with no European football, time to work in training as well as extra rest.

Pedro believes Rogers will be a huge addition to the squad while they are also relishing the chance to work under Alonso. He said: “The summer was very good because I didn't go to Brazil squad in the World Cup, so I had a time to recover myself, relax a bit, to be ready.

View 2 Images Joao Pedro lifted home a brilliant opener after just 30 seconds against Fulham (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“I think we need to go step by step. We have to focus on the Premier League and the cups. We have a lot of time to train as well to know what the coach wants from us. I think everyone wants to be at Chelsea. It's a big club. It's a pleasure to play here, and I'm very happy here. I will enjoy this season with Morgan because I think we can achieve high.

“I know Morgan from a long time ago because we played against each other. So when he joined the club, I knew. It was very good for us because he's a very good player, and I think he can help us like he has already.”

Pedro has also taken the No9 shirt this season which is a big thing for Chelsea fans because they have seen so many big names fail wearing that in the past. Mateja Kezman, Hernan Crespo, Fernando Torres, Radamel Falcao, Alvaro Morata, Gonzalo Higuain, Tammy Abraham, Romelu Lukaku, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Liam Delap have all worn it in the past and struggled.

Article continues below

But Pedro insists he has no fears about it - and is relishing the chance to score a lot of goals this season after getting off to a good start. He added: “I just try to do my job. I don't believe in that. Every player is different. I think now I know my responsibility in the group, but I don't think numbers can decide this pressure.

“I just try to enjoy and try to help my team every game. Any day of the season, see what I get. I think I just try to score every opportunity I have.”

Sports.title: Paul Scholes lashes out at Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd skipper slated team-mates
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes lashes out at Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd skipper slated team-mates

Bruno Fernandes has so often been the hero for Manchester United, but the Reds skipper has been the subject of ire from club icon Paul Scholes

View 3 Images Paul Scholes was not happy with Bruno Fernandes' recent comments (Image: YouTube/The Good, the Bad and the Football podcast)

Bruno Fernandes has been told to "shut his mouth" by Paul Scholes after the Manchester United skipper criticised his team-mates. Fernandes blasted United for repeating the clumsy errors they repeatedly made last season after their 2-0 defeat to Hull City.

‌



The shock result was only Michael Carrick's second Premier League defeat as United manager, but there is already an inquisition about the Reds' transfer business. They spent £85million on midfield duo Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, who were both hauled off in the second half as United looked for a route back into the game.

‌



After Fernandes' cutting honesty about how he and his team-mates played against Hull, Scholes expressed his unhappiness with the Portuguese ace's comments.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

When quizzed about the United captain's criticism, Scholes, speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite, said: "When you perform the way he did as well, I think it's probably best to keep your mouth shut, because he didn't have his best performance either."

Following the defeat to the relegation favourites, Fernandes told TNT Sports: "Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game we give too much of the ball to them. In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

‌



"We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set-plays and not concede these type of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.

View 3 Images Fernandes' comments were not received well by Paul Scholes (Image: PAUL ELLIS, AFP via Getty Images)

"We knew before the game set-pieces would be a big part of their game. They played all pre-season with a back four but had a five against us for some height, for these moments. The most frustrating thing is that we lost the game."

‌



Fernandes slotted alongside Tielemans and Santos in United's midfield, which endured a torrid afternoon against the Tigers. Reflecting on the outcome, Scholes does not believe any of the new additions have been an upgrade, stating: "You speak about recruitment wise and I saw the central midfield the other day and I thought 'that is no better than last'.

"I mean, when you're recruiting players and looking for a different team, you think, 'I've got to get better.' To me, on Saturday, that wasn't better than Kobbie Mainoo and Casemiro together."

View 3 Images Hull were by far the better team against United (Image: George Wood, Getty Images)

‌



United are hopeful of shortly unveiling Carlos Baleba as their latest signing. The Brighton & Hove Albion star appears set to become the third central midfielder to arrive at the club this campaign.

Baleba is anticipated to complete a £70m switch to United, which would push the Reds' total spending on central midfielders to £135m. United welcome Ipswich Town to Old Trafford in their next Premier League outing on Sunday, August 30.

Sports.title: Chelsea braced for new Enzo Fernandez bid from Man City 11 days after deadline
Sports.content:
Chelsea braced for new Enzo Fernandez bid from Man City 11 days after deadline

Enzo Fernandez could leave Chelsea for a reunion with Enzo Maresca at Manchester City in the final stages of the summer transfer window after being booed on Monday

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso could lose Enzo Fernandez in the coming days (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

Chelsea are braced for Manchester City to make a fresh bid for Enzo Fernandez.

‌



Argentina star Fernandez’s future has been uncertain this summer as he became a target for new City boss Enzo Maresca. Chelsea set a strict deadline for clubs to meet their £120million price on August 14 - and that has now long since passed.

‌



It remains to be seen whether City will make a formal bid and if that gets any encouragement, but Chelsea have made their position clear that they did not want to sell. But it is believed there could be one last attempt by City to get Fernandez as the Chelsea midfielder has been unsettled at the club since being axed last season for flirting with Real Madrid.

‌



Fernandez got heavily booed by Fulham fans in his first appearance in the Premier League as a substitute on Monday night. That was a reaction to Fernandez’s part in Argentina’s bad tempered win over England in the World Cup semi-final.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

But, interestingly, Chelsea fans sang his name and Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso also made it clear he wants clarity over Fernandez’s future this week.

‌



Alonso told BBC Radio 5Live: “In football, I am not surprised by anything. We will see. My wish is that we know what will happen for the future but we will see this week.”

The transfer window will shut at 11pm BST on Tuesday, September 1.

Manchester City have already splashed out £116m on Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest but are in need of reinforcements in central midfield. Maresca fielded defender Marc Guehi in midfield in their 2-1 win over Bournemouth, which saw six defenders named in the starting XI.

‌



View 2 Images Enzo Maresca wants a reunion with Enzo Fernandez (Image: Getty Images)

Anderson, Matteo Kovacic and Mateus Nunes could soon be the only specialist options available, with Nico Gonzalez heading to Newcastle for around £50m. They have just sold Rodri to Barcelona for £65m and Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah for £52m, meaning there is plenty of cash available.

Maresca coached Fernandez at Chelsea, but refused to be drawn on the possible deal. He said: "In this moment I have to give you the same answer since day one, which will be always the same. He is a player from another club and I don't think it's correct to talk about other players.

Article continues below

"I'm not going to say anything about players who are not with us. Not today, to be honest. I don't think we're going to do something today."

Sports.content:

Chelsea kicked off their Premier League campaign - and the Xabi Alonso era - with a 3-2 win over Fulham, but Robert Sanchez's performance in goal left a lot to be desired

View 2 Images Robert Sanchez was arguably at fault for both Fulham goals (Image: AFP / Getty Images)

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has encouraged Robert Sanchez to "relax and carry on" despite his dreadful start to the Premier League season.

‌



The Blues picked up a 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday night, with Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers all scoring at Craven Cottage. But while their attack looked impressive, there was an obvious issue at the other end.

‌



Sanchez was beaten at his near post by Josh King's low effort and he was also at fault for Fulham's second goal, pushing out a shot for Gonzalo Garcia to head in a rebound.

‌



The Spanish goalkeeper's erratic performances are nothing new, with mistakes a feature of his three-year Chelsea career. But Alonso refused to criticise his goalkeeper when speaking to reporters post-match.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"It's about the team, it's not about the individual," Alonso said when asked about Sanchez's mistakes. "The first goal, we can do better to defend, we can do better to avoid, but it's part of the game. We need to accept and to learn. This is going to be a process.

"All the lines, from the strikers, the midfielders, the defence, the goalkeepers, we want to do better in everything. The goal was to start good, and we've been able to start well. Relax and carry on."

Sanchez has been Chelsea's number one goalkeeper since joining for £20million from Brighton three years ago. He has made 112 appearances, keeping his place in the side in spite of Chelsea's busy nature in the transfer market.

‌



View 2 Images Xabi Alonso dismissed concerns about his goalkeeper (Image: Jacques Feeney/Getty Images)

Mike Penders, a 21-year-old goalkeeper who has never made an appearance for Chelsea, was on the bench against Fulham. The Belgian joined last summer from Genk and spent last season on loan at sister club Strasbourg. Filip Jorgensen, who was the back-up last season, has been sent to Strasbourg on loan for the 2026/27 season.

Both Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville have urged Chelsea to sign a new goalkeeper before the transfer window closes on September 1 to replace Sanchez.

‌



"I do think [there are] concerns defensively," Carragher said on Sky Sports after the Fulham game. "They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper issue out because it's going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight."

Neville added: "I don't know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do. The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It's a problem."

Sports.title: Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher make Premier League predictions with shock relegation candidate
Sports.content:
Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher make Premier League predictions with shock relegation candidate

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher have named their picks for the title, top four and relegation, with the Sky Sports pundits struggling to agree on much after the opening weekend

View 4 Images Gary Neville has disagreed with Jamie Carragher with his choices (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher have given their full predictions for the Premier League season - and while they both agree Arsenal will win the title, there is little consensus elsewhere.

‌



The first weekend of the Premier League campaign has been and gone, with Manchester United and Tottenham suffering heavy defeats at the hands of Hull and Brentford respectively. Arsenal kicked off their title defence with a convincing win over Coventry while Manchester City came from behind to beat Bournemouth.

‌



Liverpool snatched a late point in a 2-2 draw at Newcastle before Chelsea overcame Fulham in an entertaining 3-2 victory on Monday night.

‌



We have now seen every side play and there is now less than a week remaining in the summer transfer window for teams to bolster their squads. It means prediction time for Sky Sports pundits Neville and Carragher, who have opened themselves up to embarrassment by sharing their calls.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



There are no surprises for the title, with both ex-players tipping Arsenal for a second consecutive title. "They're way out in front," according to Neville. But the two cannot agree on the remainder of the top places.

Neville feels that Chelsea's summer recruitment and the arrival of Xabi Alonso can push them up from 10th place last season to second this time around. "Just purely because of the fact that they've got no European football," he explained. "If they keep Enzo Fernandez, with Moises Caicedo in midfield, with that front three, and they're only playing 45 games, they're going to amass an enormous amount of points.

"That's based upon the fact that they're going to have more free weeks, they're not going to have the injury pressures, they're not going to have the travelling that comes with European football, and the mental fatigue that comes with that. I think they'll just edge past Manchester City."

‌



View 4 Images Jamie Carragher has tipped Sunderland for relegation (Image: YouTube/The Overlap)

In typical Carragher-Neville fashion, both is tipping their ex-club to finish about the other's in fourth place. "I can't separate Man Utd and Liverpool in fourth place, I genuinely have no idea," Neville said. "I think City are in a better position than United. At the moment, I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool, but I do think they'll finish fourth and fifth."

Carragher said: "I think Liverpool would want more, but I think just looking at the Chelsea situation, Liverpool where they are right now, I don't see any way they'd be in the top two, and I don't see any way they can mount a title challenge."

‌



At the other end of the table, Carragher has surprisingly tipped Sunderland to get relegated. The Black Cats finished seventh in their first campaign back in the top flight last season to earn a place in the Europa League - and that could cost them.

View 4 Images Arsenal won their first Premier League title in 22 years in May (Image: Getty)

"The fact that they've got European football, they're going to be doing a lot of Thursday-Sunday," Carragher explained. "I think Sunderland last season reminded me a little bit of Sheffield United under Chris Wilder, where they came up and had a really brilliant season, finished high up the table but a lot of the games, like Sunderland, you win by the odd goal. I'm not saying it's luck but their underlying numbers had them not far away from relegation."

‌



Meanwhile, Neville has picked the three promoted sides - Hull, Coventry and Ipswich - to go straight back down, but feels that Fulham under Alvaro Arbeloa could also be in trouble.
