Sports.title: Gary Neville tells Xabi Alonso the one signing Chelsea must make after Fulham win
Sports.content:
Gary Neville tells Xabi Alonso the one signing Chelsea must make after Fulham win

Chelsea kicked off their Premier League season with a 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday night, but the match revealed a clear weakness that needs addressing in the transfer window

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso started his Chelsea stint with a win (Image: Jacques Feeney/Getty Images)

Chelsea have been told they need to replace Robert Sanchez in the final days of the summer transfer window after the goalkeeper endured a poor start to the season.

‌



The Blues kicked off their Premier League campaign with a 3-2 win over local rivals Fulham on Monday night. But while their new-look attack of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro sparkled, Sanchez looked like his error-prone self at the other end of the pitch.

‌



He allowed Josh King's effort to beat him at the near post before pushing out another shot into the path of Gonzalo Garcia, who headed in Fulham's second goal.

‌



Sanchez has been at Chelsea since a £20million move from Brighton in 2023 and has made 112 appearances for the club. The 28-year-old Spaniard has managed to hold onto his position as number one goalkeeper in west London, despite Chelsea's prolific dealings in the transfer window.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

That needs to change, according to Jamie Carragher, who has urged Xabi Alonso to bring in a new goalkeeper before the window closes on September 1.

‌



"There were things to really like," he said on Sky Sports. "On paper, that front three is sensational. It really is. It looked it in the game. I think Joao Pedro is fantastic. Rogers' first game, what a start. But when you think of him, Palmer and Pedro - that's as good as anything in the Premier League right now.

"But I do think [there are] concerns defensively. They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper issue out because it's going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight."

Gary Neville added: "They've added an experience player in centre back, centre midfield and centre forward. I don't know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do.

‌



View 2 Images Robert Sanchez was arguably at fault for both Fulham goals (Image: AFP / Getty Images)

"The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It's a problem."

Martinez's future at Aston Villa is far from certain after the club signed Japan international Zion Suzuki from Parma for around £30m. Martinez had been linked with a move to Juventus and was left out of the squad for their opening day defeat by Brighton.

‌



"Martinez transmitted to us the possibility to have another challenge in his career," Unai Emery said after the game. "Even last year, he was thinking in case he can have one possibility to change for his challenges.

"He didn't do it last year and he performed fantastic with us. This year, again, he transmitted us the possibility to have another challenge and we decided to sign Suzuki because I think he's a fantastic goalkeeper."

Sports.title: Warren thinks Fury-AJ fight will go ahead in America
Sports.content:
Frank Warren says he thinks a long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go ahead in America despite claims the bout is in doubt.

Everything seemed to be in place for the British pair of former world champions to meet in London in November, but Saudi organisers Sela's desire to instead hold the event in the USA has created a hold up.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been pushing to keep the fight in London, which led to Fury claiming last week that the contest was in "serious doubt" because his rival was asking for "more money".

However, Fury's promoter Warren has allayed fears the fight could be called off, and insists The Gypsy King would also have preferred it to take place in the UK.

Warren told Sky Sports News: "I genuinely think it will happen. His Excellency, Turki Al-Alsheikh, he will announce that fairly soon.

"I know there's been some issues with contracts with Matchroom and AJ; I believe they will iron all those out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Hearn claimed that Anthony Joshua feels a responsibility to UK fight fans that AJ vs Fury should happen in the UK.

"In the meantime, Tyson [Fury] has flown off to the States, he's in Miami and he's preparing for the fight.

"I think they both want the fight at Wembley, but it's out of their hands now. That's not quite right, actually, they could refuse to fight. We don't get the fight we want to see.

"I think because of the amount of money involved, I hope I'm wrong, but I think it will go on in America."

'Nothing unusual' for all-British clash to take place abroad

Warren says the fight taking place outside of the UK would be "nothing unusual" in terms of boxing's history.

"You had two massive American heroes in Muhammad Ali and George Foreman," Warren said. "Two American fighters, all the Americans wanted to see it, Vegas wanted to put the fight on, Madison Square Gardens wanted to see it, and it went off to Zaire.

"Everybody thought: 'What on earth was that all about?' But it became not just an iconic fight and an iconic moment in sport.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury doesn't hold back as he lashes out at Anthony Joshua as the wait goes on for the pair to confirm a much-anticipated showdown. Credit: @tysonfury.

"Ali had the 'Thrilla in Manila' with Joe Frazier. Joe Bugner fought Ali in Kuala Lumpur, it's nothing unusual.

"I think it's like all sportsmen, say, for example, David Beckham, he went off and played at the end of his career [abroad], and he did that because of the money.

"And that's why these guys are doing this, they are professional boxers.

"Would I like to see it at Wembley? Would all the fans like to see it at Wembley? Of course they would. But they are in the hands of another broadcaster who wants the fight in America."

Sports.title: What is the reality of Villa's finances ahead of Deadline Day?
Sports.content:
All of this is a far cry from the euphoria of Istanbul in May, and that is what adds to the feeling of bemusement about how significant the changes have been to Aston Villa's squad and how quickly it has occurred.

Last season was their most successful since 1982, when they won the old European Cup.

This time round, it was a Europa League win and a fourth-place Premier League finish - each of those achievements would have been enough to guarantee the riches and prestige of Champions League football.

Unai Emery was lauded as a hero by Villa fans even before last spring's spectacular, and rightly so.

He has won the Europa League title five times with three different clubs. A key question now is whether his downbeat assessment following the humbling by Brighton is indicative of a wider concern.

Clearly, Emery was upset with Ollie Watkins, and it currently seems a tall order for the striker to be reintegrated into the Villa squad, having made his desire to leave clear.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Unai Emery was short of words when asked about the future of Ollie Watkins and then after the match said to find out we should call the striker

But more worrying is the overriding sense that Emery is struggling with the lack of options he has at his disposal right now.

After all that he has achieved at the club, his reward has been widespread disruption within the squad after four key player departures, potentially more to come, and limited finances.

Emery described it as having "had an intelligent market", amid efforts by the club to strengthen the squad before the deadline. "We know where we are and we know what we want to do again for the next year," he said.

There is mitigation for Villa's bosses, however, who have been frustrated by PSR rules, which they feel have been an ambition killer and stalled their progress.

The switch to Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) rules this season has only added to that and caused deeper resentment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports explains the new financial Squad Cost Ratio rules that Premier League clubs will have to adhere to this season

As regulars in European competition now, they are limited to spending 70 per cent of their football revenue on transfer fees and player wages.

Remember, they have already been fined twice by UEFA recently, being hit with a £9.5m penalty last year and a £19.4m fine in June, although £13m of that was suspended after Villa came to a settlement agreement.

That means, inevitably, Villa are a club that has to generate income from player trading in order to buy new talent.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher discuss the outgoings of Aston Villa this transfer window and how much of an impact this could have on their season

The proof of that is in the figures from sales over the last three years; Villa have made over £410m selling the likes of Douglas Luiz, Jhon Duran, Jacob Ramsey and Moussa Diaby, before this summer's sale of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne.

Should Emiliano Martinez and Ollie Watkins follow, that number will be close to the half-a-billion mark, in terms of funds generated.

It is a big ask for Emery to see the castle that he has built taken down keystone by keystone, knowing he has to rebuild again. Last summer, the transfer upheaval contributed to the director of football Monchi leaving the club.

Importantly, Villa currently feel confident their manager is secure. After all, his contract has another three seasons to run, following the bumper new five-year deal he signed in May 2024.

But many of the biggest clubs in Europe have noticed with admiration the job Emery has done at Villa Park, and he will always be on the shortlist of the top clubs for as long as he keeps doing such a stellar job under the circumstances.

Sports.title: 'Stupid mistakes' - Root 'hacked off' by latest off-field incident
Sports.content:
A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket.

England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain.

Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

Carse, who was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts, with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background, has subsequently been withdrawn from the squad for the second Pakistan Test at Lord's with an investigation by the Cricket Regulator underway.

"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off," Root told a press conference. "I'm really disappointed that after last week's performance we are sat here and we're talking about something not related to it at all.

"In terms of the incident itself, obviously with the regulator, there's not a lot I can say on it. It's in their hands now.

"I've spoken to Brydon when I first found out; my first concern was for him as a person. In my time in the dressing room, you obviously develop personal relationships with players.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn when I say he's been very upset and has been very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.

Image: Carse was seen in handcuffs outside a nightclub in Derby

"It's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact that we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."

The Carse incident is not the first off-field episode England have had to navigate.

White-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer while out the evening before a one-day international in New Zealand last autumn.

An unverified video appeared to show opener Ben Duckett drunk while the team were on a mid-series break in the beach resort of Noosa during their ill-fated Ashes tour.

Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test of the 2-1 home defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew to attend a Chelsea nightclub as they celebrated victory in the first game of the series at Lord's.

Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of violent conduct but hit with written warnings after "breaching specific contractual obligations".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the day three of the first Test between England and Pakistan as Joe Root's side cruised to an innings victory at Headingley.

'We have to earn a lot of trust back'

Asked if English cricket had an image problem, Root, who previously called for his players to "be adults" while announcing the removal of the curfew, said: "We have an opportunity going forward.

"Clearly we're not portraying ourselves as we want to. We've got an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong and we can be proud of that's player-driven.

"That's not going to happen overnight. We've had conversations about what is expected from us, what it means and takes to play for England.

"We want to create something we can be proud of, what people following us can be proud of. We want supporters to look at us and revere, not just what we do on the field but off it as well.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, Michael Atherton and Nasser Hussain praise England's winning fast bowler combinations during the three-day victory over Pakistan in first Test.

"Over the next little while, as leader of this team, with Stephen [Fleming], and with the group of players as well, is creating something that is just that."

Root continued: "We have a chance to build something that lives alongside what we achieved last week on the field. I thought it was a brilliant performance. The way we played was exceptional.

"We have to align that with being exceptional off the field as well and understand what that looks like and how we want to represent ourselves and our nation.

"With what we've got coming up, there are plenty of opportunities to do that. But like I say, it's not going to happen overnight, in many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back.

"And something we're going to have to live and breathe consistently."

Sports.title: Baumgardner to face undefeated Turhan as blockbuster Dubois showdown nears
Sports.content:
Alycia Baumgardner will move up a division to fight Elif Nur Turhan for her IBF lightweight world title on November 8 in a seismic move that brings a blockbuster showdown with Caroline Dubois a step closer.

Baumgardner, the reigning unified WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion, will jump up five pounds to the 135lbs division to face the undefeated Turhan in the headline bout of MVPW-07 at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.

"When I set my mind to something, I see it through, and 135 will be no different," Baumgardner said. "This is a super fight, the kind of fight boxing deserves, and the beginning of my next chapter.

"I know what it takes to become undisputed. I've done it before, and I'll do it again."

Turhan added: "Alycia is a boxer who steps into the ring determined to win, never even entertaining the possibility of defeat. I know I am facing an opponent who steps into the ring solely for victory.

"I do not want to lose either. As two boxers sharing a 'win at all costs' mentality, we guarantee a fierce, relentless battle where everything is left on the line. Two warriors, one fight and only one winner."

Victory for Baumgardner would see her become a two-weight world champion in the same division as Dubois, who holds the WBC and WBO titles.

The 32-year-old is set to be ringside for Dubois' clash with Amelia Moore on Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

Since December, Dubois has been vociferous in calling out Baumgardner, and those calls have only intensified since she beat Terri Harper to unify the division in April.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Baumgardner dismissed the prospects of facing Caroline Dubois after her win over Bo Mi Re Shin. Instead, the fighter called out Katie Taylor and Amanda Serrano

Baumgardner has maintained that, despite her status as a unified world champion, Dubois has yet to reach the level required for her to entertain a fight between them.

But should Baumgardner inflict a first career defeat on Turhan, all roads will surely lead to a blockbuster unification bout with Dubois, where the winner would move to within one victory of becoming undisputed champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dubois is determined to fight Baumgardner sooner rather than later

The co-main event on November 8 will see England's Ellie Scotney fight the undefeated Tiara Brown over 10 rounds for the WBC featherweight world title.

Former undisputed super bantamweight champion Scotney will step up to 126lbs as she bids to become a two-weight world champion.

"MVPW-07 is one of the biggest championship events in boxing history, with four back-to-back world title fights, bringing together eight elite fighters from around the world with belts at stake in every match-up," said Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions.

Sports.title: Littler and Van Gerwen to headline World Series of Darts Finals
Sports.content:
Luke Littler, Michael van Gerwen and Gerwyn Price will headline a packed field competing for a top prize of £100,000 at the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals.

The event, which has a £450,000 prize pot, will return to the AFAS Live in Amsterdam and is set to take place between September 17-20.

Reigning champion Van Gerwen will be out to defend his title on home soil after he bested Littler in last year's final to scoop an £80,000 cheque at last year's event.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael van Gerwen ended his two-year wait for a top-level PDC title by beating Luke Littler at last year's event

Van Gerwen has been in excellent form on the circuit this year, having already won the Bahrain Darts Masters in January and the Nordic Darts Masters in June.

He also came close to winning the inaugural Saudi Arabia Darts Masters in January, but was bested by Littler 8-5 in the final.

World Matchplay champion Littler enters the tournament as the third seed, while Price, who was beaten by the 19-year-old in the final at the Winter Gardens in Blackpool, is the second seed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler comes into the event after winning the Saudi Arabia Darts Masters in January

Luke Humphries also joins the 32-player field as the fourth seed, after he claimed victory at the US Darts masters in June, while New Zealand Darts Masters winner Jonny Clayton and Australian Darts Masters champion James Wade are seeded sixth and seventh, respectively.

Gian van Veen and Stephen Bunting, seeded fifth and eighth, make up the final seeded players on the list.

Those inside the top 24 of the final World Series rankings will gain a berth to play in Amsterdam.

Australian Brody Klinge, who was beaten by Wade in the final of the Australian Darts Masters, will make his debut at the World Series of Darts Finals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Humphries is also in the field for the World Series of Darts Finals after winning at the US Darts Masters in June

Nathan Aspinall, Josh Rock and Danny Noppert will also join the field, while Ross Smith, who won the Players Championship 20 in June after picking up his maiden European Tour title earlier in the year is also in the field.

Ryan Searle, Wessel Nijman, Chris Dobey and Jermaine Wattimena have also gained tickets to Amsterdam as the four top non-qualified players from the PDC World Rankings as of August 23.

The field was confirmed following Monday night's Tour Card Holder Qualifier in which Rob Cross was among four names to book their place at the World Series of Darts Finals.

Cross bested Dirk van Duijvenbode in Leicester to book his place in Amsterdam, and was joined by Kevin Doets, as well as Karel Sedlacek and Callan Rydz, who will both make their debuts at September's event.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rob Cross (right) secured his spot at the event folllowing Monday's Tour Card Holder Qualifier

The first round of the tournament will commence over two sessions on Thursday 17 and Friday 18 September, before round two begins on Saturday, September 19.

The finals will then begin on Sunday, September 20, with the quarter-finals set to get under way in the afternoon, before the semi-finals and final later in the evening.

Sports.title: 'Not the best version of me' - Hamilton regrets frustrated Dutch GP comments
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says he didn't present "the best version" of himself when criticising his Ferrari team over the radio and in television interviews at the Dutch Grand Prix.

Hamilton sounded irate in a series of radio messages sent when he was being held up by team-mate Charles Leclerc despite the pair being on different strategies during the race in Zandvoort.

The seven-time world champion felt as though the lost time ultimately cost him a podium as he finished fourth just behind George Russell having been unable to overtake the Mercedes in an exciting finale.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix.

Hamilton, who joined Ferrari from Mercedes in 2025, doubled down on his criticism of his team after the race when he compared the Italian squad's hesitation to get Leclerc out of his way to the Silver Arrows decisively ordering Russell to let his team-mate, championship leader Kimi Antonelli, pass him later in the race.

Reflecting on the weekend an in Instagram post on Monday, Hamilton said: "I've listened back to some of my radio and TV comments. In the heat of the moment frustration can come out, especially when you care as deeply as I do.

"But that wasn't the best version of me. I take responsibility for that, and I'll be better."

Despite the race - won by McLaren's Lando Norris - representing a third successive grand prix for Hamilton without a podium, the 41-year-old insisted the fight for the title "is absolutely still on".

"To the team at the track, thank you. The commitment and effort never go unnoticed. We still have work to do, particularly over one lap, but we'll keep digging in, learning and improving together."

Rosberg urges Ferrari improvement

Hamilton's former team-mate Nico Rosberg urged Ferrari to improve their execution of races as he believes they have the potential for "much better results".

Sports.title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner York arrested
Sports.content:
Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences

Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools

Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.

Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct.

York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution , according to prosecutors.

York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.

Records also show that York had his cell phone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.

Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.

"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email.

"You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offences in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."

The 49ers Enterprises - who are the investment arm of York's San Francisco 49ers - own Leeds United. The Premier League club have declined to comment.

They are also part of the US consortium who acquired a majority shareholding in Rangers last summer. However, York is not listed on the club's list of board members.

When contacted by Sky Sports News, Rangers chose not to comment.

The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy.

Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy.

Sports.title: WSL academy teams to play in third tier after FA approves controversial plan
Sports.content:
Four Women’s Super League academy sides will play in tier three of the pyramid from the 2027-28 season after the controversial proposal was approved by the Football Association’s board.

The change forms part of what the FA described as a package of reforms to the Women’s National League “designed to strengthen the women’s football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players”.

The FA said data showed that young English players were getting significantly fewer competitive minutes than their counterparts across Europe’s leading leagues.

Quick Guide How do I 

The FA said WNL clubs would receive central funding for the first time and that changes to the loan market would encourage clubs from the top two divisions to loan players to clubs in the third and fourth tiers.

The WSL academy teams will not be eligible for promotion and will be chosen against criteria to be developed in the coming months, the FA said. With the third tier split into two geographical regions, it is expected that two academies will be placed in the northern division and two in the southern.

Sue Day, director of women’s football at the FA, said: “For the game to continue moving forward, the FA Women’s National League must evolve alongside the professional game, and we need to create more opportunities for talented young English players to develop in senior football.”

Sports.title: Savinho seals £75m Spurs move from Manchester City – and changes name to Sávio
Sports.content:
Savinho has completed his £75m move to Tottenham from Manchester City and marked the beginning of a new chapter in his career by indicating that he wants to be known as Sávio from now on.

The Brazil winger, who will cost up to an additional £10m in add-ons, will have Sávio on the back of his shirt. The fee represents a record sale for City, who signed him from Troyes in 2024 for £30.8m.

The deal for Sávio takes Spurs’s summer spend to £304.5m and they are not finished. They are close to signing the City forward Omar Marmoush for somewhere between £50m and £75m. They are also monitoring Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo.

The Spurs manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has been keen to add greater punch in his attacking line, a feeling that intensified after the team’s 3-0 defeat at Brentford on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

Sávio prefers to play off the right wing, where he can cut inside on to his stronger left foot. De Zerbi started the 18-year-old Mikey Moore on the right at Brentford. His other option in the position is Mohammed Kudus, who is “almost ready” to return, according to De Zerbi, from the thigh injury sustained in January.

Sávio had three goals and 13 assists in all competitions in his first season at City, 10 of the latter coming in the Premier League. He was less productive last time out with four goals and three assists in all competitions. In 53 Premier League appearances he has scored twice.

Quick Guide How do I 

“It’s taken a while but I’m very happy to be here,” the 22-year-old told the Spurs website. “As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team.”

De Zerbi said: “Sávio is a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity.”

Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.

“I don’t think that [Infantino] has done anything wrong,” he said. “All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.

“I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After president Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”

Sports.title: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York pleads no contest after arrest at Ohio trailer park
Sports.content:
The San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York has pleaded no contest to two criminal charges after being arrested at an Ohio trailer park over the weekend.

KRON4 News in San Francisco reported that York was initially arrested on suspicion of engaging in prostitution but that count was amended to a charge of disorderly conduct. He was also charged with possessing criminal tools.

A no contest plea is not an admission of guilt but the defendant in question does accept the punishment for the alleged crimes in question. York was sentenced to a day in jail for each count to be served concurrently and was released on Monday morning. He was also fined a total of $1,150 and ordered to complete an online course. The arrest report does not specify what the criminal tools were in York’s case.

According to the New York Post, court documents say York responded to an advert on a website and “arranged to have sexual activity with [a] female in exchange for $140.” York was arrested later arrested at a trailer park in East Palestine, Ohio, on Sunday morning. The East Palestine Police Department and the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force were involved in the arrest. York, 46, was born and raised in Youngstown, a 30-minute drive from East Palestine and still has a home in the area.

York is the nephew of former 49ers majority owner Edward J DeBartolo Jr. York took day to day control of the 49ers in 2008 when he became the team’s CEO. After acquiring his mother’s shares, he became the team’s principal owner in 2024.

View image in fullscreen Jed York pictured in a handout from the Colombiana County Sheriff’s Office. Photograph: Colombiana County Sheriff's Office

“As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time,” the 49ers said in a statement. The NFL said in a statement that it is “aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy.”

Since York took over as CEO, the 49ers have reached three Super Bowls but lost each time.

He also owns stakes in the Premier League’s Leeds United and Scotland’s Rangers through 49ers Enterprises. He filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May.

Sports.title: Another set of Sullivan brothers are making football waves in Bangladesh
Sports.content:
Ronan Sullivan had tried a panenka twice in his life. Both attempts were at practice on the other side of the world, and one hit the crossbar. But his twin brother, Declan, was hardly surprised when Ronan turned to him and told him he’d chip the fifth penalty of a shootout that could win a scoreless tournament final, as millions tuned in online to see his Bangladesh side play against India in the Under-20 South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) Championship.

“He didn’t even need to say it. I knew he was gonna do that the whole time,” Declan remembered, sitting next to his brother on the couch of their dorm room at Saint Joseph’s University. “I knew that if he got the last pen to win it, he was gonna do that. That’s just the him thing to do.”

Moments later the ball gracefully splashed into the back of the net, and the thousands in attendance on 3 April in Malé, Maldives erupted.

“I wouldn’t have believed you if you told me it [would have] went like that,” Ronan said.

Less than two years after he began exchanging messages on Instagram with the “Save Bangladesh Football” fan page, the brothers were celebrating a U-20 title, made possible by their maternal ancestry, as members of essentially the home team. (Bangladesh is the largest source of migrant workers in the Maldives.)

“Flying in there alone was incredible. Like the water’s so blue. I’ve never seen anything like it. Like we go to Ocean City, New Jersey, where the water is brown, and it’s our favorite place ever,” Ronan said. “So when we saw this water, we were like, ‘Oh my gosh!’ It looked like the water from [the movie] The Waterboy. At the end [of the movie], that special water … I think it’s just Maldives water.”

The story seems ripped from the pages of a Hollywood script. Two kids from Philadelphia with very Irish names who had never visited Bangladesh before their tryout for the country’s U-20 squad prior to the tournament, then returned to its crowded capital triumphantly. They allowed a few days for the media frenzy, and a few more for themselves to explore, enjoy the food and time with their grandmother, whom they’d only seen in the US until this trip.

But this could be part of the opening scene for Bangladesh, ranked 181st by Fifa, with nearly 180 million people and, according to the United Nations, the world’s sixth-largest diaspora. The vast majority of it is concentrated in southern Asia or the Middle East, but there’s a well-established community in the UK, growing ones in the US and Italy, and pockets elsewhere in the West.

“I think a lot of people saw what we did over there and saw how good of an experience that was, and now all of a sudden I’m seeing a lot of foreign players interested in playing for Bangladesh, a couple kids from England who are on pretty good academies over there, so we have talent all around the world. It’s just about utilizing that,” Declan said.

The Sullivans are well known in Bangladesh, the US and beyond, and so too is former US men’s national team captain Thomas Dooley. The son of an American serviceman who grew up and played in Germany then joined the USMNT by happenstance, Dooley was announced as the head coach of the Bangladesh senior team seven weeks after the U-20 side brought a trophy home. He spent most of the coaching chapter of his life in Southeast Asia, where he heard about “a fanatic country in football” he is now leading into a new World Cup cycle.

“We are a country of being fans. We need to change that. We need to be a country of playing football,” Dooley told the Guardian. “That’s what we need to be, and we need to find a way to do that.”

View image in fullscreen The Bangladesh U-20 national team celebrate winning the SAFF Championship. Photograph: Courtesy Bangladesh Football Federation

Ronan, Declan, and their brothers Quinn and Cavan – both attackers for the Philadelphia Union – were eligible to play for the US and Germany as well as Bangladesh. While Quinn was cap-tied by the USMNT last summer and Manchester-City bound Cavan is a top American prospect, the twins were more realistic bets for Bangladesh.

“It all started with an Instagram DM, which is kind of crazy,” Declan recalled. The message came from that Save Bangladesh Football account. Initially confused that a fan page was encouraging them to come for a camp before they had a passport, Ronan and Declan soon realized the account was a legitimate asset and facilitator for the federation, eventually connecting the Sullivans to federation vice-president Fahad Karim when they expressed interest in the SAFF U-20 tournament.

“[We had] a bit of time before college. It would be awesome to go play, represent the country, become more part of the culture,” Ronan said. The next three months were “a bit of a crazy process,” primarily because obtaining a Bangladeshi passport when their mother didn’t have one wasn’t straightforward. But in March the twins flew from New York to Delhi, then Delhi to Dhaka, easily the longest journey of their lives.

There wasn’t a red carpet waiting for them, though. They had not been promised spots in the squad, arriving for a camp with more than 30 players, including three fellow “origin” players whom the Sullivans knew of and could easily communicate with. The manager spoke English too but on the pitch, to varying degrees, there was a language barrier.

“When you’re foreign, it’s harder to get the ball at first because you don’t speak the language and maybe the guys weren’t super thrilled that we’re there. But once you get the ball a couple times and show what you can do, it helps out,” Ronan said. After a few days of training they were confident they’d make the roster, and socially their integration progressed.

Dooley adamantly defends the right of players with Bangladeshi roots to choose their national team. His Asian coaching odyssey started in the Philippines, where he shrugged off many fans resistant to foreign-born recruits, and he’s encouraged by the culture of the Bangladesh senior team he’s inherited, highlighting the leadership and humility of Leicester City midfielder Hamza Choudhury.

“Everybody was happy that Hamza came in, and they understand – the players understand that international players can help them because they can look up to them,” Dooley said. “What kind of attitude they have, the work ethic that they bring in. So everything, they can look up to them, how they handle stuff.”

The more they search for players abroad, the more they find – not necessarily in a major European league but at a level that can raise the standard of the pool. But it’s a balancing act. Dooley is getting “thousands” of messages about players and acknowledges “we have to be careful,” noting the budgetary constraints.

“It’s not everybody who sends a picture of a free kick that he does is a good player, or maybe can help us. We have good players in this country over here too that we can actually afford,” he said. “We are not spending $2,000, $3,000 on a player to bring him over, and he’s sitting on the bench. So if the players who are coming over are the ones that really can help us, otherwise we’re using that money and putting all the local players in the camp and train them twice a day for two weeks, and you will see that they’re getting much, much better.”

Dooley says that coaching a decent group of players who can cover plenty of ground to change the way they think about the game – “most of the players, they don’t think, they play” – and to limit mistakes can improve the team 20 to 30%. He thinks climbing to the 150s of the FIFA rankings is certainly achievable.

Of course, there’s a much bigger dream than that.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Celebrations at the SAFF U-20 Championship in the Maldives. Photograph: Save Bangladesh Football/Courtesy Save Bangladesh Football

The Instagram comment sections of all four Sullivan brothers have been flooded with Bangladeshi flags for years. The twins were checking their phones in the Maldives, absorbing as the buzz online reached a different stratosphere. They noticed the rivalry with India in particular.

“They were making edits of me walking a dog that was painted like the Indian flag. Like it was crazy. There was a lot of heat there, for sure. A lot of tension,” Ronan said.

The fervent support in the Maldives created an atmosphere they had never felt on the pitch, a surreal experience that carried into a heroes’ welcome in Dhaka.

“That was a lot. Got a lot of flowers, met a lot of people. I feel like our team was the hot new thing in Bangladesh,” Declan said. Indeed, when the Sullivan twins walked around Dhaka they already stood out because, in Declan’s words, “we’re white, for everyone there at least.”

“We met a bunch of people, and everyone was so happy and so grateful that we brought the trophy back to the country. Like they were really, really hype about that, and that’s not something you would see in America [for] youth soccer.”

And you probably wouldn’t see a media presence at the airport for a senior national team almost anywhere, no matter the circumstances, comparable to what met Dooley at the airport when his group departed for a friendly against San Marino in June.

“I thought we are going to the World Cup,” Dooley said. “I was like, this is amazing, and I cannot imagine [the scene] if we would qualify for the World Cup.”

“I think the country would explode if we qualify for a World Cup,” Ronan said.

It seems far-fetched. No country from the Indian subcontinent has ever appeared at a men’s or women’s World Cup. Its viral passion for international soccer continues to be channeled towards South American giants.

However, with further expansion of the men’s World Cup looking inevitable, and a bridge to their diaspora being built, a new dimension awaits this sport in Bangladesh. Something even greater awaits if a country from the subcontinent can qualify. While recruiting players is increasingly common in international sport, what it could unlock in this scenario is rare.

“Whenever I think about the 64 team [World Cup], I’m thinking, ‘Look, if we get all these players, we have a chance to qualify.’ Like, that’s the dream. That’s the ultimate goal,” Declan said. He mentioned his friend, former Union academy teammate and Penn State winger Nehan Hasan, and Stanford striker Trevor Islam as possible additions, and hopes there will be many more candidates.

“We have to convince them. We have to tell them you can actually leave a legacy here in this country,” Dooley said about eligible players.

Dooley preaches qualifying for the Asian Cup (the Bangladesh men only have once in their history) or the World Cup is a process, but in the same breath he says “it can go fast”. He mentions 19-year-old winger and Fulham academy product Farhaan Wahid and 25-year-old Louie Watson, an attacking midfielder in the English fourth division, as the next potential pieces for his project. Choudhury and a New York Cosmos summer signing, Canada-born midfielder Shamit Shome, are the cornerstones. Dooley stresses that goalkeeper will be a key position to address.

After their fall friendlies, the next notable step for the program will be the senior level SAFF Championship in Bangladesh in November. Bangladesh have won the tournament just once, as hosts in 2003. It’s Dooley’s main focus, but after that, he’s planning to be more involved in the development of the sport domestically. In his view, it’s a top-down mission: the success of the senior team drives the interest, sponsorship, and investment for a proper pyramid structure, with youth academies feeding adult leagues.

Until he moves into an apartment in the affluent Gulshan area of Dhaka, Dooley is living at a hotel. He’ll look out the window at densely populated high-rise buildings, lamenting only a school or two in sight with a soccer field. This is the deeper challenge, one of infrastructure, culture and mindset for the next generation.

“We would love to have the kids not want to be a fan of Argentina. They want to be a player to play against Argentina, against Brazil,” he said.

Sports.title: Post-Pep Premier League era begins with blast of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
There has been something oddly narcotic and moreish about the drip‑drip of fresh Pep Guardiola content either side of the start of the new Premier League season. Eras come and go. Everything dies, baby, that’s a fact. But four‑part Amazon Prime documentaries make angels of us all.

So we have continued to feast on the Pep-at-City visuals: dead jeopardy, reheated beefs, the uplifting team talks of a departed manager to the departed players of a departed team, and moments that often feel far more gripping than the daily churn of what we must, out of habit, call the real world.

The thought occurred watching all this: has the Premier League found its Tupac? Is Pep just going to keep on doing this, dropping new material, fresh hits, posthumous platinum albums? A bald, thin charismatic man who keeps on releasing his lost tapes. We have exactly the thing, sir. Is he even actually dead?

Probably this won’t happen. But a profound absence is still a profound presence at moments like these. The ghosts continue to pull the strings. This weekend was the first of the new Premier League season. More significantly, it was also the first of the post‑Pep era.

And this has been a genuine era, 10 years in the game and an entire tactical culture shift in the making. Unsurprisingly, there was an odd sense of lightness across those nine fixtures on Friday through to Sunday, of old bonds cast aside, even a little giddiness. Suddenly dad isn’t home. The chair by the door is empty. Let’s all just rip it up a bit, shall we?

This relies on a slightly out‑of‑date notion of what Guardiola‑ism became in its later years. But the fact is, something interesting did happen in those Friday‑to‑Sunday games. Think of pure Pep-ball and what are you seeing? Possession. Cold, high‑craft control. This is a coach who famously said: “My desire is to have 100% possession,” after a 5-1 thrashing of Arsenal in Munich during which Thiago Alcântara complete 122 passes.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledges the fans before City’s opener against Bournemouth. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Admittedly, Guardiola was speaking out of frustration that day, talking more about not losing the ball at key moments, possession as defence. But these ideas did have a profound mimetic effect in England. During Guardiola’s decade at Manchester City the team that had the least possession in the Premier League would win, on average, only 30%-35% of games, a figure that fell as low as 28% in 2021‑22 but which had begun to pick up in the last two seasons as even City’s own version of Pep‑ball became more mixed and next‑gen.

But this weekend the opposite thing happened. In six of nine games played from Friday to Sunday one team took significantly more possession while failing to win. Liverpool had 60% possession plus 27 shots but still just scrambled a draw and looked, frankly, pretty wild. Manchester United had 71% possession and were well beaten by Hull. Tottenham had 60 % possession and lost 3-0. Nottingham Forest had 56% and lost. Sunderland had 62%, Crystal Palace 58%, and both lost.

There were three exceptions to this, all outliers in their own way. Manchester City had 66% possession and won at home against Bournemouth, but spent 84 minutes looking like they were losing. Brighton had 73% possession and beat an Aston Villa team that had made a collective decision to play with their eyes closed and their legs on the wrong way round. Arsenal dominated every metric against a promoted Coventry team that looked, frankly, a little spooked by their first sight of that fresh Everest.

So, a tiny sample size. It may mean absolutely nothing. It could get flipped on its head before we hit September. Also, it is important to note that pure possession stats have rarely dictated with any certainty who will win a game. The top teams always tend to have most of the ball, thus skewing the overall stats.

Otherwise, possession has been a far less reliable guide to victory than, say, expected goals, which speaks clearly to the effectiveness of a system. Whereas simply keeping the ball is often a sign of the opposite of good health, of football as a collective anxiety attack, out there playing with your worry beads, tramping a horseshoe shape into the grass while your opponents mass for the decisive blitzkrieg.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

But it wasn’t just the possession numbers that were notable this weekend. The rhythms of the matches were striking. All three Sunday games featured nine or 10 substitutes in the last 40 minutes or so, and a sense of two separate halves, of finishers brought into play, of a broken, episodic tactical to‑and‑fro in response to shifts in the scoreline and the flow. The World Cup also had that pattern. Maybe this is what football is now.

Mainly there was a striking level of targeted physicality, rehearsed blitz-transitions, groups of players running suddenly forward quickly in formation at certain triggering events. Anthony Elanga’s opener for Newcastle captured this best: 12 seconds, two passes, 70 metres covered in a single perfectly straight line, no off‑the‑cuff inventions or what you might call conventional “creativity”, but a perfect moment of planned collective intelligence and breathtaking athleticism.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This was the pattern elsewhere too, games defined by rapid breaks, by powerful players sourced for their ability to win duels and to carry the ball, and a weekend that felt like another ratcheting up in the Premier League’s journey into hyper‑physicality.

Isn’t it a trend? Is this the next stage in the league’s narrow but furiously intense evolution? There are several managers in new jobs who have reputations for the game of sprints, blitz‑ball: most notably Matthias Jaissle at Newcastle and Roberto De Zerbi at what was, on Saturday, the least De Zerbi‑ish of Spurs, a Spurs that seemed to have absorbed only the mouse part – play dead, hide, roll over – of that fast‑breaking cat‑and‑mouse football.

There are two things worth saying about this. This is not a rejection of Guardiolaism and positional play. Keeping the ball was always about preparing for the moments when you don’t have it. Guardiola’s later Manchester City team would often win by direct means.

But pure possession can also be boringly risk-averse, a kind of footballing atrophy where everyone just sits quivering on the touchline like a swarm of beached jellyfish at dusk. The spectacle is more gripping when the emphasis is on those transitions either side of the passing patterns.

More specifically, it is also an interesting development for Pep’s successor at City, Enzo Maresca, Coolio to his Tupac, whose methods are still very much pure Pep origins, based in control of the ball and rigid positionism, like the last soldier still fighting the second world war from inside a bush on Iwo Jima in 1976.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle’s Anthony Elanga celebrates his superb strike against Liverpool. Photograph: Simon Davies/ProSports/Shutterstock

Is Maresca ready for this? Is he even ahead of it? He gave a televised interview at the weekend where he spoke about the tension between control and risk, possession and creativity, and where he defined players being encouraged to run into unexpected positions as “chaos”. On Monday morning there were headlines describing the Premier League weekend in those terms. But this isn’t chaos. We’ve seen chaos. We’ve seen attack ships on fire off the shoulder of Orion, jinking wingers, dogs of war, hitting the space, Lee Chapman, Rod Wallace and Eric Cantona making heavy metal music with two bass guitars and an antique viola. You want chaos. We can give you chaos.

What the Premier League brought at the weekend, the quick breaks, the freedom to attack at selected moments, was more a kind of hyper-managed shock and awe, targeted speed and physicality born out of calculated risk, numbers, data, heavy briefings.

It was also exciting to watch, which is no bad thing in the world’s most tightly contested, space‑averse league. No doubt there will be tightening, a reaction to the reaction, instant counter‑moves and contingency planning. August can also be odd and silly season-ish, the dog days of a World Cup summer. But it did at times feel as if we were in a post‑something moment. If not quite post‑Pep, whose influence will continue to loom, a tactical Machiavelli with plenty of tapes still left in the vault.

Sports.title: Glaring weakness in goal remains but early signs Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea should be fun | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
After a weekend on which pretty much every potential challenger to Arsenal had demonstrated their flaws, there was a sense, perhaps even a need, for Chelsea to emerge as a serious contender – if only to prevent the title race becoming a procession. And while they were far from flawless, there were at least some indications that they could mount some kind of challenge.

They looked extremely dangerous in the final third, and Cole Palmer was involved in all three Chelsea goals, perhaps benefiting from a first summer off in three years. But they were rather less impressive through midfield or at the back, despite Josh Acheampong’s all-action performance, while goalkeeper remains the problem it has been since Thibaut Courtois left.

It could easily have gone wrong: in the final quarter-hour; Antonee Robinson lofted an effort wide with Robert Sánchez off his line and Ryan Sessegnon smacked a shot from a narrow angle straight at the Spanish keeper. But neither opportunity was taken and so Chelsea got Xabi Alonso’s reign off to a winning start.

At this stage, performances and learning the system are probably the most important thing, but if there is to be some sort of dart at the title, results matter if only to keep Chelsea somewhere near the race until the point at which Alonso’s principles are absorbed and they do find something close to top form.

Perhaps what’s most striking, though, is how different the approach is to Enzo Maresca’s. Where Maresca prioritised control to often stultifying effect, Alonso’s game is based on rapid turnovers and transition. It’ll probably settle down as his systems become deeper rooted but there was a sense of recklessness at times to their play. It was harum-scarum, end-to-end, thrilling stuff, which is all very well to watch, and may even come as a relief after the sterility of Maresca and the shambles of Liam Rosenior, but may not be great for consistency or sustained runs of form.

Alonso could hardly have dreamed of a quicker start, João Pedro putting Chelsea ahead after 31 seconds, matching the record for the quickest goal scored in the reign of a Premier League manager, David Unsworth’s goal – also against Fulham – in David Moyes’s first game in charge of Everton in March 2002. João Pedro had scored eight goals in eight pre-season games; and this a player Maresca told not to focus on scoring goals shortly before he went on a run of seven games without a shot. That was a first indication of a forward line starting to show signs of an impressive understanding. All three combined for the third goal, Morgan Rogers flicking on for João Pedro who held the ball up for the overlapping Palmer to slip his shot cleverly between Bernd Leno’s legs.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro (second from left), Cole Palmer (second from right) and Morgan Rogers (right) combined impressively on their first outing as Chelsea’s front three. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Alonso’s first go at finding a pattern amid the legions of players assembled by BlueCo involved a midfield made up of two players who, despite being at Chelsea together for the past three years, had never previously been paired in the centre: Roméo Lavia and Reece James. It was not entirely by choice: Moisés Caicedo was left out as a precaution while Enzo Fernández remained on the bench until the 65th minute as Manchester City continue their pursuit of him. And it didn’t entirely work. It may look a defensively robust pairing but there were long spells when Fulham had control of midfield.

A feature of Alonso’s approach, and one of the reasons it takes time and commitment to learn – qualities that were notably lacking at Real Madrid – is that players can emerge in unexpected positions. Which doesn’t entirely explain how the right-sided centre-back Maxence Lacroix found himself running on to Palmer’s pass in the Fulham box but, having got there, he demonstrated great poise to skip around Jorge Cuenca and cut the ball back for Rogers to score his first Chelsea goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Yet for all that was new and positive, and for all that was raw and unintentionally exciting, there was one glaring and inexplicably familiar failing for Chelsea: in goal. Sánchez’s positioning seemed very strange for Fulham’s first goal, drilled in at his near post by Josh King (who also benefited from a bizarrely ineffectual attempt to track from Rogers), and while it was a far less glaring error, he pushed Timothy Castagne’s shot straight to Gonzalo García for Fulham’s second.

Although Sánchez doesn’t perhaps quite deserve the negative reputation he has among certain Chelsea fans, he did make a league-high five errors leading to goals in 2024-25 and three last season. It remains mystifying that a club that signs wide forwards by the dozen continues to refuse to invest in a top-class goalkeeper. That may yet hold Chelsea back.

Generally, though, Alonso can be satisfied with his start: a win against Chelsea’s local rivals, an impressive display from Acheampong, a number of fluent interactions from his front three and plenty of signs of his system beginning to take hold, with a few obvious improvements to be made. And from the point of view of fans and casual observers, it looks like it should be fun.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 4: Brighton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 6th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 7th

Prospects

A first FA Cup final was a historic moment for Brighton. Despite losing to Manchester City at Wembley, it will have filled Dario Vidosic and his team with the belief that they are on the right track.

It has been a summer of relative stability on the south coast. While there are seven new faces, departures have been limited to four. The arrivals of Lia Wälti and Gabby George bring vast experience and increased defensive acumen to the ranks while the Republic of Ireland’s Emily Murphy and Poland’s Nadia Krezyman are young attacking talents who have started to make a name for themselves.

Brighton’s inconsistency was their downfall last season. They were seriously hampered by the lack of an out-and-out centre-forward after the anterior cruciate ligament injury suffered by the Arsenal loanee and England Euros hero Michelle Agyemang. Kiko Seike finished as their highest scorer in the league with eight and she was their only representative in the Women’s Super League’s top 20 for goals and assists. That problem remains unsolved and will surely be a focus for the remainder of the transfer window.

The conclusion of their season certainly gave Brighton something to build on over the summer. They secured an impressive league victory over City and a draw against Arsenal and will hope to outdo the latter when they host Renée Slegers’s side at Crawley in their opener on 6 September. That on paper is the toughest of Brighton’s opening four fixtures.

Off-field picture

Pinterest has become the first solo sponsor of the women’s team with a four-year partnership. The deal pivots around the concept of ‘matchday style’, bringing to life the way fans show support for their team. Plans continue for the construction of Europe’s first purpose-built women’s football stadium. Located next to the Amex Stadium, the hope is it will open for the start of the 2030-2031 campaign.

The manager

Now entering his third season, Vidosic is the second-longest serving manager in the WSL, a period that has brought much-needed stability to the club and allowed the Croatian-born Australian time to fully implement his aggressive pressing and possession-based style. He has been on a journey, developing an out-of-possession style to help his team deal with some of the bigger clubs in the WSL The 39-year-old has never hidden from his desire to bring silverware to Brighton and last season’s FA Cup final will have given him a taste of the steps required to realise that ambition.

Star signing

The acquisition of Wälti remains one of the biggest coups of the summer. The 33-year-old Switzerland captain returns to England after a year in Italy with Juventus, bringing with her a wealth of experienceand, from her seven years with Arsenal, a WSL title and a Champions League winners’ medal. Wälti’s technical ability is second-to-none, as is a level of intelligence that allows her to dictate play from the middle of the park. She leads by example and guided Switzerland to the quarter-finals at Euro 2025. If Wälti can stay injury-free, she could play a significant role this season.

View image in fullscreen Lia Wälti should bring quality and know-how to Brighton. Photograph: Neil Holmes/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Stat attack

Brighton had a finishing problem in 2025-26. Not in terms of hitting the target – no other side had as strong a shot accuracy – but only three teams converted a lower proportion of their on-target efforts. If the Seagulls can fire towards the corners of the goal rather than close to the goalkeeper, they could fly this season.

Set for a breakthrough

Sophie Peskett has already made history when in 2021, aged 18, she became Ipswich’s first professional player. The winger spent the best part of seven years at Ipswich, making 127 appearances and helping them earn promotion to the WSL 2 twice. Now 23, it would have been a big decision for her to leave, but Brighton seems like a sensible next step. A nifty player with an eye for goal, Peskett will prove useful to Brighton’s attacking output.

What they say …

“Brighton is not a team that has to hide. In the last couple of years, they’ve been able to hurt the big teams in many moments, and they reached the FA Cup final last season as well. We’re not going to be favourites in every single game, but that’s a nice position to be in.” – Lia Wälti

Where are they playing their home games?

Brighton will continue to play most of their home games at Crawley’s Broadfield Stadium although four of their six opening home fixtures will be at the Amex. The club have added an Amex 4-Match Pack to their ticketing options, priced at £45 for adults. The club have also launched ‘Built For Her’, their dedicated women’s football membership option that offers a bundle of exclusive perks as they look to build their fanbase before the stadium move.

Sports.title: Joe Root admits he was 'hacked off' by nightclub arrest of Brydon Carse as England stars 'keep making stupid mistakes' - and reveals bowler was 'very upset and apologetic'
Sports.content:
Joe Root admits he was 'hacked off' by nightclub arrest of Brydon Carse as England stars 'keep making stupid mistakes' - and reveals bowler was 'very upset and apologetic'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Joe Root has said he is ‘hacked off’ by Brydon Carse’s arrest in Derby on Saturday night, and frustrated that England’s cricketers ‘keep making stupid mistakes away from the game’.

Carse, who was handcuffed by police for being drunk and disorderly outside a nightclub after celebrating Durham’s win over Derbyshire in the County Championship, has since apologised to Root and – according to the captain – ‘understands his actions’.

But Root could not hide his irritation about having to address another alcohol-related incident only two days before the start of the crucial second Test against Pakistan at Lord’s.

‘If I’m being brutally honest, I’m really hacked off,’ he said. ‘I’m really disappointed that, after last week’s performance at Headingley, we’re sat here talking about something that is not related to it at all.

Brydon Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub in Derby following Durham's victory on Saturday

‘I’ve spoken to Brydon, and when I first found out my first concern was him as a person. I don’t think I’m speaking out of turn in saying he’s very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I’m sure when he gets his chance he will say that himself.

‘It’s not the isolated incident itself, it’s the fact we continuously keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it’s detracting from what we are doing on the field.’

Carse, who was part of England’s 16-man squad for the first two Tests, will miss the game at Lord’s while the Cricket Regulator investigate the events that led to his arrest, swiftly followed by his ‘de-arrest’, outside Molly Malone’s Irish Tavern.

And Root urged his team to use the incident to put a raft of adverse headlines behind them – from Harry Brook’s set-to with a bouncer in Wellington, to Ben Duckett’s misadventure in Noosa, via Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson’s late-night drink in Chelsea’s Rex Rooms.

Today at Lord's ahead of the second Test, Joe Root admitted he was 'hacked off'

‘Clearly we are not portraying ourselves how we want to, and I think we have an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong, that we can be proud of, that is player-driven,’ said Root.

‘Of course, that isn’t going to happen overnight. In many ways, we are going to have to earn a lot of trust back. It’s something we are going to have to live and breathe, consistently.

‘I’ve made it very clear to the players what is expected of them, how we want to conduct ourselves, and over time we’ve got to show people what I see on a day-to-day basis in the dressing-room – the characters we have, and how much they care about playing for England, and not having isolated incidents be how we are seen as a group of players.

‘I’m not trying to sit here and ask people to be saints. Everyone’s going to make mistakes at the odd time. But it’s understanding where we currently sit and what’s expected of England players.

‘We’ve had a very robust discussion, and I think there’s real clarity there. I can understand why we are viewed in a certain way at the moment. We have a responsibility and opportunity to change that.’

Asked whether the players had to be more careful about being goaded by members of the public, Root replied: ‘I just think if we don’t put ourselves in certain situations, it’s not something we have to worry about.’

Sports.title: Savinho welcomes 'brilliant opportunity' after completing £85m Spurs move, Aston Villa explore finances for Rafael Leao deal... and Man City are set to go back in for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Savinho welcomes 'brilliant opportunity' after completing £85m Spurs move, Aston Villa explore finances for Rafael Leao deal... and Man City are set to go back in for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez: WINDOW WATCH

To catch up on all of yesterday's developments - including Aston Villa making contact with AC Milan over Rafael Leao - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Bees still buzzing about Diouf

Brentford are continuing discussions with West Ham for left wing back El Hadji Malick Diouf. The Senegal international joined last summer from Slavia Prague for £19m but had an indifferent season.

West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf is a target for Brentford

Forest talk over £13.6m move for Andre

Nottingham Forest are in talks over a £13.6million move for Corinthians midfielder Andre.

The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but has quickly established himself as one of the best young midfield talents in the Brazilian league.

AC Milan attempted to sign him in January but he wanted to see out the season with Corinthians. Crystal Palace have also been watching him .

Forest have been looking to strengthen their midfield since selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City.

They have made offers for Lucas Bergvall at Spurs and Tijjani Reijnders who left City for Al Qadsiah.

Wrexham close on £8m move

Wrexham are closing in on a move for highly-rated Angers wing-back Jacques Ekomie as they look to bolster their side for a Premier League push.

Phil Parkinson has been keen to add to his squad before next week’s deadline and it’s understood there has been a breakthrough with Angers for Ekomie, who is valued at around £8million.

Co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac were in attendance for Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Watford and Parkinson revealed he had a ‘good chat’ with the Hollywood pair about transfers.

Ekomie has been a man in demand this summer with interest from Hamburg and West Ham but Wrexham are confident they have won the race to land the 23-year-old.

Wrexham's first bid for Ekomie, rejected on Friday, was £4.3m.

They are also trying for Millwall forward Femi Azeez and Ipswich's attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti.

NATHAN SALT

Olympiacos in for Edson

Olympiacos have made an offer to take West Ham defensive midfielder Edson Alvarez on loan.

The Mexico international has also had interest from Real Sociedad and Ajax so far.

Doncaster living the life O'Reilly

Doncaster Rovers are set to sign Aston Villa starlet Tommi O’Reilly on a season-long loan.

A plethora of clubs, including Sheffield Wednesday, have been interested in the midfielder who got over 20 goal contributions in League Two last season while on loan at Crewe.

Tommi O'Reilly starred at Crewe Alexandra on loan last season

Tottenham seal Savinho deal

Tottenham have confirmed the signing of Manchester City winger Savinho.

Daily Mail Sport reported last week that a fee had been agreed comprising £75m plus £10m in add-ons.

Roberto De Zerbi's side lost 3-0 at Brentford in their Premier League opener and their new signing will come into the mix ahead of tomorrow's League Cup clash with Charlton. Spurs are also expected to bring in Omar Marmoush in a double swoop from City.

Savinho said: 'It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here. It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world.

'As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team.'

De Zerbi described Savinho as 'a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity.

'We’re very pleased to have him with us, and I’m looking forward to working with him, helping him continue to grow and seeing him bring his personality to the team.'

Savinho signs on the dotted line for his move to Spurs

Pinnock in for Coventry medical

Ethan Pinnock is due to have his medical at Coventry today ahead of singing a three-year contract with an option to extend.

The promoted club agreed a £6m fee with Brentford for the 33-year-old defender yesterday.

Ethan Pinnock is set to bolster Frank Lampard's squad at Coventry

Chelsea in talks over Guiu exit

Napoli are continuing talks with Chelsea for Marc Guiu and defender Mamadou Sarr’s proposed loan to Sociedad is progressing. Chelsea have asked about Atalanta defensive prospect Honest Anahor.

Villa look at Leao deal

Aston Villa are exploring the finances of a deal for AC Milan's Rafael Leao.

Daily Mail Sport reported last night that the club had made contact over the winger, 27. Turkish giants Galatasaray remain in the mix for the Portuguese as well.

Rafael Leao in pre-season action against Chelsea

Bakwa off to Lille

Nottingham Forest winger Dilane Bakwa is joining Lille on loan.

The 23-year-old signed for Forest from Strasbourg last September in a deal worth £30million but has failed to have the desired impact.

He is due for a medical today and will play in the Champions League with Lille.

Dilane Bakwa is set to leave after just one season at the City Ground

City set to go back to Enzo

Manchester City are expected to go back in for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez.

The Blues previously set City a deadline of 5pm on August 13 to pay £120m to get the deal done - a deadline City did not meet.

But contact has continued with his agent Javier Pastore so City know the 25-year-old is open to coming and now they are set to come back in for the midfielder, who played the final half-hour of Chelsea's 3-2 win away at Fulham on Monday night.

For more on this story click HERE

Enzo Fernandez came on as a substitute at Fulham on Monday night
