“The rule of law is not an abstract phrase for law school lecture halls,” Weah said. “It is the practical guarantee that a citizen’s rights do not depend on who is in office or what favor they can secure.”

He argued that the rule of law must provide equal protection to ordinary citizens, including journalists, traders and students, regardless of their social or political status.

“When that guarantee weakens, everything else in a nation weakens with it: investment, security, public trust, and peace itself,” he said.

Warning Against Judicial Interference

The former Liberian president also cautioned against executive interference in the judiciary, citing what he described as examples across the region involving manipulation of judicial budgets, questionable appointments, pressure on judges and the creation of special courts for political purposes.

He also referenced the wave of military takeovers that has affected several African countries since 2020.

While condemning coups, Weah argued that governments operating under democratic labels must also guard against institutional erosion.

He called on the Nigerian Bar Association to remain vigilant in defending judicial independence and citizens’ rights.

“This is why I say to you: the Nigerian Bar Association is not merely a professional association negotiating welfare for its members,” he said.

“You are a standing sentinel of this Republic’s democracy.”

According to Weah, when the legal profession remains silent, courts become more vulnerable to political capture, while a united and principled Bar can deter executive interference.

Weah Revisits 2023 Concession

The former president also used the address to revisit his decision to concede Liberia’s 2023 presidential runoff election to current President Joseph Nyuma Boakai.

Weah said he congratulated Boakai while the vote count was still underway after preliminary results indicated that his opponent was leading.

He said some people around him had advised waiting until the final results were formally certified before conceding.

“I chose to concede while the counting was still underway, because I have always believed, and still believe, that the will of the people must stand above the ambition of any one man in a democratic setting,” Weah said.

He argued that electoral disputes and the failure to respect democratic principles can have serious consequences for national peace and security.

Weah said the NBA’s recognition of his 2023 concession was particularly meaningful because it demonstrated the importance of placing national peace and the people’s will above personal political ambition.

“If a small nation like mine can insist on that standard for itself, then surely this continent…can insist on standards beyond the limits others have too often assumed for us,” he said.

From Monrovia’s Ghetto to the Presidency

Weah also drew heavily on his personal journey, linking his rise from the Gibraltar community in Monrovia to the broader theme of overcoming limitations.

The former football star recalled growing up largely under the care of his grandmother in circumstances where few people expected him to reach the highest levels of international football or become president of Liberia.

“I did not accept them—not out of arrogance, but because the limits placed on us by man are not the same as the limits placed on us by God,” he said.

Weah became the first and remains the only African male footballer to win the Ballon d’Or, following a celebrated international football career before entering politics.

He later became a senator and was elected president of Liberia in 2017, serving from 2018 to 2024.

Beyond ‘Brain Drain’

Turning to Africa’s development, Weah said the continent’s greatest limitations are not a lack of talent or intelligence, but inadequate infrastructure and insufficient political and institutional organization to harness African expertise.

He called for a shift in thinking about the African diaspora—from viewing migration primarily as “brain drain” to developing systems that encourage “brain circulation.”

Weah argued that African professionals living and working abroad can contribute significantly to national development if governments establish mechanisms that enable them to share their expertise without requiring them to abandon opportunities overseas permanently.

He cited African diaspora remittances as evidence of the enormous economic contribution already being made from abroad.

“Imagine that same energy formally invited into legal reform and judicial modernization, as a deliberate national strategy,” he said.

Five Values for Breaking Limits

Weah said Africa’s effort to overcome its challenges must be anchored in five values: discipline, hard work, respect, perseverance and spiritual strength.

He drew parallels between football and the legal profession, saying talent without discipline is insufficient for success.

In the legal profession, he said, intellectual brilliance must be matched by discipline, ethics and commitment to justice.

He similarly described hard work as essential to overcoming corruption, weak infrastructure and institutional inertia.

Respect, he said, must extend to the dignity of every human being, national constitutions and independent institutions.

Perseverance, he added, is necessary because individuals and nations will inevitably face setbacks.

“Perseverance is the internal voice that says, ‘I will rise again,’” Weah said.

He also stressed the importance of spiritual strength, arguing that leadership should be viewed as temporary stewardship rather than permanent ownership of power.

‘Africa Must Stand Up for Democracy’

In closing, Weah called on African lawyers and institutions to defend justice, equality, accountability and free elections.

He urged the Nigerian Bar and legal professionals across the continent to remain independent and protect the rights of people regardless of wealth, political influence or social status.

“The law must never be an instrument of chaos. It must never become a weapon of war,” he said.

“It must remain what it was always meant to be: an instrument of remedy, of peace, of unity, and of accountability.”

Weah concluded by calling on Africa to stand for the rule of law, fairness, impartiality, gender equality, human dignity, peace, democracy and free and fair elections.

“Africa must continue in peaceful coexistence, and we must all stand up for the rule of law,” he said.

The address comes as Weah remains active on the African and international stage following his presidency. He has also signaled his intention to seek the Liberian presidency again in 2029, setting the stage for his continued political relevance ahead of Liberia’s next presidential election.

World.title: Liberian Model Francis Dine Set to Chase Africa’s Next Supermodel Crown
World.content:
MONROVIA — From the classrooms of BlueCrest University to the international fashion spotlight in Nairobi, Liberia’s Francis A. Dine is preparing to take her runway ambitions to the continental stage after being selected to represent Liberia at Africa’s Next Supermodel this November in Kenya.

Dine, a student of BlueCrest University, was discovered and recommended for the competition by Liberian-American international fashion show producer and talent scout Junda Morris, who has built a reputation for identifying and mentoring emerging African talent.

Morris said Dine’s striking presence, discipline and runway potential made her stand out as a promising representative of Liberia.

“As a Liberian fashion producer and talent scout, I am proud to see Francis step onto this international stage,” Morris said. “She represents the beauty, confidence, resilience, and limitless potential of young Liberian women. Nairobi is about to experience Liberia’s next superstar.”

From Liberia to the Continental Runway

Dine’s selection provides another opportunity to showcase Liberia’s emerging fashion and creative talent beyond the country’s borders.

Her participation in Africa’s Next Supermodel, described by organizers as one of the continent’s leading model-search platforms, is expected to bring Liberia into greater focus within Africa’s competitive fashion industry.

For Dine, the Nairobi appearance will be more than a personal modeling opportunity. It will also place her in a position to represent Liberia’s style, creativity and growing generation of young talents seeking opportunities on the international stage.

A New Face for Liberian Fashion

Morris’s involvement highlights the increasingly important role of talent scouts and fashion producers in identifying African models and connecting them with opportunities outside their home countries.

According to the statement announcing Dine’s selection, Morris recognized her potential and recommended her for the continental platform after seeing qualities he believed could translate to an international runway.

Her selection comes as Liberia’s creative sector continues to seek greater international exposure, particularly in fashion, music, film and other youth-driven industries.

‘Representing Liberia With Purpose’

As she prepares for her trip to Kenya, Dine is expected to carry with her the support of Liberians at home and in the diaspora.

Her journey from university student to continental modeling contestant is being presented as a story of ambition, confidence and opportunity—and a reminder that Liberia’s fashion talent can compete beyond its borders when given the right platform.

With Nairobi as her next runway destination, Dine now has an opportunity to turn recognition at home into a much bigger continental breakthrough.

Francis A. Dine — representing Liberia with elegance, confidence and purpose.

World.title: Liberia: Boakai: Flag Day Must Move Us To Action
World.content:
Monrovia – President Joseph Nyuma Boakai has urged Liberians to turn national pride into daily responsibility, warning that the Lone Star demands unity, discipline, and service as the nation marked 179 years of its flag.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

Speaking at the official program marking this year’s National Flag Day, President Boakai said the flag is more than a national symbol. The event was held at the Executive Pavilion on Ashmun and Broad Streets in Monrovia.

‘’It is beyond the cloth and the recognizable colors of our flag lies a powerful expression of our national identity, our national history, and the struggles and aspirations of our people,” President Boakai told a crowd of government officials, diplomats, students, and citizens.

From Independence to Identity

The President noted that this year’s Flag Day, which follows last month’s 179th Independence Anniversary under the theme: “Strengthening National Identity Through Liberian-Led Historical Leadership,” must give Liberians one national identity – a visible, enduring symbol.

“It reminds us of who we are, where we come from, and the Liberia we must continue to build.”

He recalled the role of the seven women led by Susanna Lewis who sewed the first flag in 1847.

“Our national flag derives from the courage and determination to give physical form to the aspirations of our people as a nation in the making,” he stated.

Say No to Drugs – A Warning To The Students

Directing part of his remarks to young people, President Boakai called on students to live by the Flag Pledge by rejecting vices that destroy the future such as drugs.

“Learn the words of the pledge, but more importantly, understand and live by them. Loyalty to Liberia means respecting your fellow citizens, obeying the laws of the Republic, rejecting violence, protecting our national symbols, working hard and preparing yourself to serve your country,” he urged.

“In particular, I urge you to say no to drugs. Drug trafficking and the use of our country as a transit and operational center pose a serious threat, especially to our young people. Do not let anyone steal your future. Stay focused, disciplined, and determined to become the citizens that Liberia needs.”

The President praised students who participated in the parade, noting: “I saw discipline. I saw precision. I saw confidence and patriotism in the eyes of our young people. I am very proud of them.” He congratulated schools recognized as Best Salute, Most Disciplined, and Best Dressed.

Lead by Example – A Message To Adult Liberians

President Boakai challenged adults and public officials to match their words with action.

“We cannot ask our children to love Liberia while we undermine its institutions. We cannot ask them to respect the law while we disregard it. We cannot demand patriotism while we place personal, ethnic, religious, or partisan interests above the national good,” he declared.

As the head policymaker of the country, the Liberian leader announced the reintroduction of civic education in primary schools and the launch of standardized civic textbooks nationwide as a step toward restoring knowledge of the Constitution, history, and citizenship.

Commemoration, Not Complacency

Calling for national unity and development, the President intoned that the flag demands action against division and corruption.

“Our flag calls on us to action. It demands that we reject division, hatred, corruption, violence, and every force that threatens our national fabric,” he said.

“It calls on us to build a Liberia where our roads connect our people, electricity reaches more communities, healthcare improves, education is transformed, opportunities expand, our young people are not subjected to drugs, and every citizen can take pride under the Lone Star,” the President asserted, emphasizing that the flag belongs to every Liberian.

“To the elder in the village and the leader in the city, to the farmer in Lofa, the fisherman on the coast of Maryland, the worker in Monrovia, and to every Liberian at home and abroad. It belongs to all of us.”

One People, One Destiny

President Boakai called on Liberians to honor the sacrifices of the past and build for the future.

“May our flag continue to fly proudly over land and sea, and across the world, where for nearly two centuries it has served as a beacon of hope… May it remind us always that we are one people, one nation, with one destiny,” he said.

“As we always say, in all that we do: let us think Liberian, love Liberia, and together build Liberia. God bless the Lone Star. God bless the Republic of Liberia.”

Meanwhile, Education Minister, Dr. Jarso Maley Jallah, said the reintroduction of civil and the launch of its textbooks will help propel Liberian young learners into responsible leadership and love for nation.

The Minister extolled President Boakai for his stewardship of the country that continues to bring improvement in the educational sector of the country.

World.title: Government calls for TRALARD II Support
World.content:
A Senior Government official in Mpulungu District has called on stakeholders to support the success of the Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development (TRALARD) II project.

Mpulungu District Commissioner Gehard Sikazwe says the project should be supported by relevant stakeholders for it to bring about socio-economic development of the district.

Mr Sikazwe disclosed that the project has the potential to significantly improve the living standards of people and boost local economic activities in Mpulungu and the surrounding areas.

Speaking during the District Development Coordinating Committee meeting, Mr Sikazwe explained that the Tralard II project is part of the broader national development agenda which focuses on enhancing social amenities and promoting sustainable livelihoods.

“This project is designed to create opportunities for local residents, especially in the areas of small-scale enterprises and cooperatives. this is why community participation and stakeholder support are vital for the project,” he explained

Mr Sikazwe has since urged stakeholders to ensure that the project benefits the most vulnerable groups and marginalized populations in Mpulungu.

TRALARD II Project District Operations Officer James Chilufya reaffirmed the project’s commitment to helping the community with necessary support that will make them realise the full benefit of the project.

Mr Chilufya emphasised that shared responsibility among all stakeholders is essential for overcoming challenges that the project might face and maximizing the project’s impact.

He assured stakeholders that adequate resources and technical assistance would be provided to facilitate smooth implementation.

Mr Chilufya has also called on stakeholders to share their expertise and innovative ideas to enhance the project’s effectiveness.

He said with strong community involvement and strategic partnerships, the initiative is poised to bring about meaningful change in the district.

World.title: Wedson sets African target for Malawi’s Bullets
World.content:
FCB Nyasa Big Bullets head coach Wedson Nyirenda says he is building a side with ambitions that go beyond winning the Malawian league, with a target of conquering Africa.

The former Chipolopolo coach was hired by Bullets last June on a two-year contract and says the project is still very much a work in progress.

Nyirenda made it clear his vision for Bullets extends past domestic dominance.

“Like I always say, I am not looking at a team that is only going to be champion in Malawi. We do not want to be local champions. We want to be champions in Africa,” he told the club media.

“Every day we are moving in that direction. We want to go where other people do not even think they can swim. That is where we want to go,” Nyirenda added.

The Zambian tactician said the foundation of that ambition is constant player development and recruitment.

“We are still building. I have always said scouting and recruitment are the only constant things in football. If you stop scouting and recruiting, then the team is dead,” he said.

“Every day you have to scout and think about who is going to come in, at what point and in which position. Our scouting continues because we are still building this team,” Nyirenda explained.

Nyirenda believes Bullets are showing greater cohesion as his rebuild continues.

“I think it is the organisation. We have improved so much in communication and in the way the defence is cooperating with the midfield. All the departments are firing well. We are defending as a team and attacking as a team,” he said.

He also praised the work of goalkeeping coach Rabson Chiyenda.

“The goalkeeping department is also doing a very good job. Coach Rabson Chiyenda is a very serious man and deserves credit for the work he is doing. I think we are looking good and we are looking ready.”

Bullets were held to a goalless draw against Luanar in an FDH Bank Premiership encounter at Dedza Stadium on Sunday.

(Image by FCB Nyasa Big Bullets)

World.title: SADC members seek qualifications harmonisation
World.content:
The Zambia Qualifications Authority (ZAQA) has emphasised the importance of mutual recognition of qualifications across SADC member states in enabling professionals to work freely and contribute meaningfully to the socio-economic development of the region.

Board Chairperson, Victor Zulu, has observed that Zambia’s universities attract students from several SADC countries, noting that many, however face challenges as they are subjected to further examinations and assessments back in their countries, before recognition.

Professor Zulu has explained that such bottlenecks hinder regional integration and professional growth, adding that similar challenges affect graduates from other countries seeking employment elsewhere in SADC.

He has stressed that harmonising qualifications across the region is therefore essential to remove such obstacles and allow graduates to work freely.

The ZAQA Board Chairperson said this when he opened a 3-day SADC Qualifications Framework Technical Working Group workshop in Lusaka, being attended by representatives of Qualifications Authorities from member states.

“So we are here also to look at the guidelines that will make it easy for our qualifications and national occupational standards to be recognised in the region”, Professor Zulu stressed.

Speaking at the same meeting, Chairperson of the SADCQF TWG who is also Chief Director of South Africa’s Department of Higher Education and Training, Philip Tshabalala, echoed similar sentiments, affirming his country’s commitment to the cause.

He pledged South Africa’s strong support for the SADCQF, further assuring of South Africa’s the country’s readiness to collaborate both within the region and across the continent.

He highlighted that South Africa was well positioned to contribute to the framework’s advancement, noting that it had championed this agenda through its leadership of the G20 Education Working Group in 2025.

“We have got the Ministry or the Department of Basic Education colleagues here. We have got the colleagues also from the Ministry of Higher Education and Training and our very own South African Qualifications Authority. And so we really want to welcome the SADCQF”, he indicated.

And speaking earlier, ZAQA Director General, Mercy Ngoma, explained that participants would review the portfolio of SADCQF activities for 2026 and 2027, share developments from member states, and advance regional guidance on referencing.

She added that governance, funding, and capacity renovations would also be considered.

Ms Ngoma noted that ZAQA had deliberately extended invitations to the Examinations Council of Zambia, TEVETA, and the Higher Education Authority to ensure Zambia contributed an integrated national perspective.

World.title: Hikapulwe assures prompt FRA payments
World.content:
Kafue District Commissioner Maurice Hikapulwe has reaffirmed government’s commitment to ensuring that farmers delivering maize to the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) are paid without delay.

Mr Hikapulwe said farmers who have so far delivered their maize to FRA satellite depots are receiving payments promptly.

“Government is committed to ensuring that our farmers are paid on time for the maize they are delivering to the Food Reserve Agency. Farmers should therefore continue taking their produce to the designated FRA buying centers,” he said.

He noted that timely payment is important in helping farmers meet their financial obligations and prepare for the next farming season.

Mr Hikapulwe encouraged farmers in the district to take advantage of the FRA maize marketing season by delivering their produce to designated depots, and urged them to follow the required procedures to ensure the payment process runs smoothly.

He added that the government will continue monitoring the maize marketing exercise in the district to ensure the payment process remains smooth and timely.

“We want our farmers to benefit from their hard work, and that is why the government is making every effort to ensure that the payment process is smooth and timely. Farmers should have confidence in the process and continue delivering their maize,” he said.

World.title: Chongwe fire brigade retrieves body from dam
World.content:
Chongwe Fire Brigade on Sunday, 23 August 2026, retrieved a body of an unidentified man from Sunrise Dam in Silverest area.

Chongwe Municipal Council Assistant Public Relations Manager Cecilia Musonda said the fire brigade received a report of suspected drowning at around 15:59 hours, prompting officers to immediately attend to the incident.

Ms Musonda told the media that the deceased was an unidentified adult male believed to be aged between 35 and 37 years, discovered by members of the public who were fishing in the area.

She said upon arrival at the scene, fire brigade officers found the body floating near the water bank and immediately commenced recovery operations.

Ms Musonda explained that the officers successfully retrieved the body from the dam and handed it over to Zambia Police officers for further investigations and other necessary procedures.

She further said the body was later deposited to Chongwe District Hospital Mortuary, awaiting a postmortem examination to establish the cause of death, while police are expected to assist in establishing the identity of the deceased.

World.title: ZDA, LuSE Partner to enhance businesses
World.content:
The Lusaka Securities Exchange (LuSE) and the Zambia Development Agency (ZDA) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at improving access to long-term capital for businesses and strengthening private sector-led economic growth.

Speaking during a joint press briefing today, ZDA Director General, Albert Halwampa, says lack of access to capital remains a major obstacle to the actualisation and expansion of investment projects in the country.

Mr Halwampa notes that the partnership will particularly support existing and expanding businesses, including small and medium enterprises (SMEs), to list on LuSE and raise capital for investment, job creation and economic growth.

He has disclosed that many investment projects facilitated by ZDA fail to reach financial closure because investors struggle to access appropriate capital.

Mr Halwampa has further noted that the partnership will also leverage the Zambia Investment Deal Room, a digital platform established to connect local and foreign fund seekers with potential fund providers.

He explained that the MoU will strengthen collaboration between ZDA and LuSE in investment promotion, access to markets, green financing and trade promotion, including support for exporters seeking capital to expand.

Mr Halwampa pointed out that SMEs are critical to the future of Zambia’s economy and should be encouraged to consider LuSE as an alternative platform for raising capital.

“ZDA has registered close to 3,000 greenfield and brownfield companies between 2021 and 2026, many of which require financing to actualise or expand their investments,” he added.

He further said the partnership will help create a pipeline of businesses that can access capital through LuSE while supporting the government’s agenda of promoting trade, investment, job creation and economic growth.

Mr Halwampa reaffirmed ZDAs commitment to work with LuSE to ensure that investors, both local and foreign, benefit from the opportunities created through the MOU.

Meanwhile, LuSE Chief Executive Officer Nicholas Kabaso said the partnership will connect ZDA’s investment promotion and enterprise development mandate with the exchange’s role of mobilising long-term capital.

Mr Kabaso also re-echoed that access to long-term capital remains a major constraint for businesses despite Zambia’s significant entrepreneurial potential.

He said the partnership will encourage more businesses, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), to consider the capital market as part of their growth strategy.

“Listing on the Exchange provides businesses with access to capital while strengthening corporate governance, credibility and visibility,” said Mr Kabaso.

He said the partnership will also focus on financial literacy, corporate governance, financial reporting and identifying barriers that discourage companies from accessing the capital market.

“LuSE currently has four companies with market capitalisation exceeding US$1billion, so there is need to develop a stronger pipeline of businesses capable of reaching that scale,” he added.

He said the success of the MoU should ultimately be measured by the businesses supported, capital mobilised, investments attracted and companies brought to the exchange.

Mr Kabaso said the partnership marks the beginning of efforts to build a pipeline from entrepreneurship to investment, growth and ultimately listing, further calling for continued collaboration.

World.title: Mnangagwa toasts HH victory
World.content:
Congratulatory messages from across Africa and the rest of the world have continued to pour in for President-elect Hakainde Hichilema following his re-election as President of the Republic of Zambia.

World.title: Kateka: UPND’s Fear Of Petition Is Shocking
World.content:
Kateka, Katuta Demand Explanations As Courts Branded “Crime Scenes” During Petition Window

New Heritage Party president Chishala Kateka says the fear of a presidential election petition being exhibited by the United Party for National Development government is shocking, accusing authorities of deliberately obstructing a constitutional process by closing the very court premises where the petition was to be submitted.

In an interview, Kateka said government’s impunity and apparent fear of the petition had reached the point where the judiciary was instructed to close court premises altogether. She said the sequence of events, first soldiers stationed at the courts for several days, and now the courts themselves closed, meant the petition simply could not be submitted through ordinary channels.

“We are really shocked by the United Party for National Development government’s phobia of the presidential election petition,” Kateka said, describing petitioning as a constitutional right and questioning why authorities would move to close court premises if they had nothing to fear from the process. She said the government’s conduct in this instance amounted to abrogating the Constitution and proved that those in power do not respect the rule of law.

Kateka argued that allowing the petition to proceed would in fact be the best way to legitimise the election outcome, since courts provide the proper forum to prove a victory was legitimately won. She said the refusal to allow that process to unfold as normal suggested government itself was uncertain about what scrutiny might reveal, and that Zambians deserved to know what was happening to their constitutional rights.

Separately, losing independent presidential candidate Given Katuta has demanded government accountability for the classification of key public institutions, including multiple High Court buildings, as crime scenes. Her demand follows the designation of High Court premises in Lusaka, Ndola, Livingstone, Kitwe, Chipata, Kabwe and Kasama as crime scenes, a classification that forced them to shut their doors to the public nationwide.

Katuta said it was shocking that all High Court buildings across the country had been described in this way, questioning openly what sort of crime could plausibly have occurred simultaneously at so many separate institutions. In a statement, she noted that according to the yellow “crime scene” tape surrounding them, the High Court and the Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal Security headquarters had now been declared crime scenes.

Katuta pointed to Zambia’s 35-year record of democratic governance since 1991, during which citizens had consistently held their leaders accountable for decisions affecting them, and questioned why that culture of accountability appeared to be shifting under the current administration. She said public institutions belong to the people of Zambia and demanded that government urgently inform the nation of what was actually taking place.

She further urged those in leadership to recognise that Zambians have the right to know what is happening in their country, particularly where a matter involves a public institution central to a live constitutional process. Both Kateka and Katuta’s interventions add third-party political voices, distinct from Mundubile’s own camp, to the mounting chorus of concern over the timing and justification of the court closures.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 25, 2026
World.content:
Two UN Peacekeepers Killed in South Sudan Ambush

Two UN peacekeepers have been killed and seven others injured after unidentified gunmen ambushed a UNMISS patrol in South Sudan's eastern Jonglei state. The injured include three peacekeepers, two national police officers and two civilian staff. UNMISS chief Anita Kiki Gbeho condemned the attack and called for a prompt investigation, warning that attacks on peacekeepers may constitute war crimes. The incident comes as renewed violence puts South Sudan's fragile peace process under increasing strain. The country remains one of the world's most dangerous places for aid workers, with at least 36 humanitarian workers killed since January.

Prince Harry Steps Down from African Parks Board

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Prince Harry has stepped down from the board of African Parks, an African wildlife charity he supported for 10 years. However, he remains a supporter of its conservation mission. His departure follows an independent investigation into allegations that rangers managed and funded by the organisation committed human rights abuses, including beatings, rape and torture, against indigenous people in Congo-Brazzaville. African Parks admitted the abuses last year and said it had since strengthened its safeguarding measures and governance. Harry's exit comes as he and Meghan prepare to relocate with their children from California to the UK.

Kagame Slams 'One-Sided' US Sanctions Over DR Congo Conflict

Rwandan President Paul Kagame has criticised US sanctions imposed over Rwanda's alleged involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. He said that they add to existing problems without addressing the root causes of the crisis. The US sanctioned the Rwanda Defence Force and four senior commanders in March, accusing them of supporting AFC/M23. Kigali described the measures as one-sided. Kagame said international pressure should also address the role of the FDLR, the Congolese government and other actors, arguing that the conflict cannot be blamed solely on Rwanda. He said Rwanda would continue pursuing peace while taking measures it considers necessary to protect its security.

Former DP Gachagua Vows to Contest 2027 Presidential Election

Former Kenyan Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has said that his impeachment does not automatically prevent him from contesting the 2027 presidential election. Gachagua is challenging the decision in the Court of Appeal and potentially the Supreme Court. Gachagua argued that the High Court acknowledged his right to a fair hearing was violated. However, they still upheld his removal from office, which he called a constitutional "absurdity". Gachagua insists he remains a presidential contender, declaring that he is not a "kingmaker" but a potential candidate himself. He said that his opposition to President William Ruto is driven by concerns over governance rather than personal bitterness.

Close 

Tanzania Commission Begins Probe Into Election Violence

The Presidential Commission of Inquiry into the Individuals Involved in Violence and Violations of the Law during and after the October 2025 General Election has officially begun preparations to investigate those responsible. Commission chairperson retired Court of Appeal Judge Shaban Ali Lila said it will collect evidence from the public and other stakeholders. He said the commission would receive oral testimony, examine documents, and visit locations identified as connected to the incidents under investigation. The commission, established by President Samia Suluhu Hassan, will assess the evidence in accordance with Tanzanian laws and regulations.

US Seeks Wider UN Arms Embargo on Sudan

The United States has proposed expanding the UN arms embargo on Darfur to cover all of Sudan, as the country's civil war enters its fourth year. US Envoy Massad Boulos told the UN Security Council that weapons and financial support from outside powers were fuelling the conflict and proposed including drones and related technology under the embargo, as well as increasing monitoring. Sudan has backed a technical extension of the existing embargo but warned against measures that could weaken its army. Russia has expressed concerns about expanding the sanctions. The war between Sudan's army and the Rapid Support Forces has killed tens of thousands and displaced millions, with Darfur among the areas worst affected by violence.

World.title: South Africa: Businessman Seeks Bail in Trafficking Case - South African News Briefs - August 25, 2026
World.content:
KwaZulu-Natal Businessman Seeks Bail in Trafficking Case

A KwaZulu-Natal businessman accused of human trafficking and sexual exploitation is set to apply for bail at the Durban Magistrates Court, reports EWN. The 65-year-old, whose identity is protected by law, was arrested by the Hawks. He is accused of being the ringleader of a trafficking operation in which four women were allegedly lured from Johannesburg to Durban with promises of sales jobs before being forced into prostitution and pornography. His alleged accomplice, a 48-year-old man, is also expected in court. The businessman has also been linked to senior police officers and politicians through testimony at the Madlanga Commission.

Acting as executor, while Peter "Gagash" Nonyane is alleged to have been involved in the fraud. World.title: Kenya: Ruto Warns Opposition of Tough Political Contest
World.content:
Nairobi — President William Ruto has issued a warning to his political opponents, saying they will face a tough political contest.

Speaking during a public address in Narok North, Ruto said some people opposing his administration's programmes would be surprised by the political response.

"I can see there are some people whom we are going to give a very tough political battle, and they will be surprised, won't they?"

"I told them the other day, that even if they have been paid, even if they have been hired, even if you have been organised and sent to oppose housing, can't you use a little common sense to understand how you are going to oppose this housing programme? You come and tell us that you oppose housing because a chicken cannot climb a storey building," the President said.

The President accused sections of the opposition of mobilising people to reject government initiatives, including the Social Health Authority and affordable housing programme.

"I am telling my competitors, stop treating us like fools. You are telling us that we should go back to NHIF, which covered only eight million people, and abandon SHA, which covers 32 million people."

"Why are you testing our intelligence?

You are telling us to go back to NHIF, where you had to wait for three months before getting treatment, while with SHA, when you go and register that same day, you are already eligible to receive treatment that same day," the Head of State said.

World.title: Tanzania: Vice President Nchimbi Resigns
World.content:
Tanzania's Vice President Emmanuel Nchimbi has announced his decision to resign from office.

Nairobi — Tanzania's Vice President Emmanuel Nchimbi has announced his decision to resign from office on September 4, barely a month after he urged rights groups to "fight" for a new constitution.

Nchimbi announced Tuesday that he had written to President Suluhu informing her of his decision to retire from politics and public service and relinquish the Vice Presidency.

The announcement comes a week after local media reports on mounting pressure for the Vice President to resign, which prompted the suspension of a local media outlet.

Tanzania's Swahili Times confirmed Nchimbi's resignation on Tuesday, while the Vice President's Office did not share the resignation letter on its social media platforms.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Nchimbi cited President Samia Suluhu Hassan's desire for change as the reason for his decision.

He said he had promised Suluhu in August 2025 that he would assist her and Tanzania "to the best of my ability and with integrity," and would step aside whenever she felt the need for another Vice President.

"I am fully satisfied without a doubt that the Hon. President desires a change, so I have decided to fulfill my promise," he said.

His resignation will take effect on September 4 in accordance with Articles 50(2)(c) and 149(2) of Tanzania's Constitution.

AU declares Tanzania's election flawed and undemocratic

SADC declares Tanzania's election flawed after failing democracy test

The announcement comes about a month after Nchimbi made a strong call for Tanzanians to push for a new constitution during the opening of the 15th General Meeting of the Tanzania Human Rights Defenders Coalition (THRDC) in Dar es Salaam.

"If I were given the chance to tell Tanzanians just one thing, I would tell them: 'Fight to get a new constitution,"' Nchimbi said on July 24.

He said a new constitution based on national consensus was essential for strengthening human rights, good governance and democracy.

"Fight to get a constitution that has the agreement of all stakeholders, a constitution with consensus in the nation," he said, arguing that it should guide Tanzania for the next 50 years and protect citizens' rights.

Nchimbi said constitutional reform offered a foundation for addressing the various demands raised by Tanzanians and different groups.

"When you listen to many of the demands from different people, you find they have lined up many things all at once. You must choose the single major thing that can carry everything in the country. It is the Constitution," he said.

The constitutional reform process began in 2011 under former President Jakaya Kikwete but stalled in 2014 before a referendum could be held.

Close 

Suluhu has previously indicated that the process would be revived before 2030, while the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) pledged in its 2025 election manifesto to continue the process.

Nchimbi thanked Suluhu and CCM for their confidence in him and Tanzanians for their cooperation throughout his public service career.

He pledged to remain a "good citizen of Tanzania" after leaving office.

World.title: Uganda: Hundreds of Passengers Stranded As Taxi Crackdown Bites
World.content:
Kampala — Hundreds of passengers were left stranded across the Kampala metropolitan area on Monday as traffic police launched a crackdown on commuter taxis in dangerous mechanical condition. The operation, which began as early as 6:00 a.m., targeted dilapidated 14-seater taxis commonly known as "gganyegenya" operating in Kampala, Wakiso and Mukono districts.

Police deployed heavily along major routes, including Gayaza Road, Jinja Road, the Northern Bypass at Busega, Namugongo, Kawempe and Hoima Road, stopping and impounding taxis found to be in dangerous mechanical condition. At Rubigi Police Station along Hoima Road, one of the busiest checkpoints, police impounded at least 40 taxis serving routes to Kakiri, Nansana-Gganda and Nansana-Nabweru, areas known for having large numbers of older taxis.

Passengers were ordered to disembark and find alternative transport, while the impounded vehicles were towed by police recovery trucks to the Nakawa parking yard, which has been gazetted by Kampala Capital City Authority for impounded vehicles. Tifu Nabapa, the Officer in Charge of Traffic at Rubigi Police Station, said some taxis were identified through visual inspection, while others were checked both inside and outside."Yes, it is easy to see that this vehicle is in dangerous mechanical condition. You only look at it outside and inside and tell people to get out. We're not arresting drivers; we're telling them to go back home. But most of them have parked their vehicles; they have not shown up," Nabapa said.

The crackdown was announced last Thursday by Minister of State for Works and Transport Fred Byamukama, who directed police to begin impounding taxis in dangerous mechanical condition from Monday. Byamukama said the operation covers the Kampala metropolitan area and is intended to remove old and poorly maintained taxis from the roads.



He said the government was specifically targeting vehicles that pose a danger to passengers and other road users. "These taxis are beyond repair. You find them loading people, but when you enter, the seats are torn and smell. Some are tied with superglue. The conductor is holding the door with superglue, the doors cannot lock, and the driver is using a steering wheel tied with ropes. When you look at the tyres, the people are moving at the mercy of God," Byamukama said.

He cited Katooke Road in Nansana, Gganda-Kyebando, Kalerwe-Gayaza, Nakawa-Luzira, Kakiri and Busunju as some of the routes where the taxis operate. Byamukama said some vehicles have boots tied with ropes and warned that such vehicles endanger both occupants and other road users. He also linked some old taxis to highway robberies, saying worn-out vehicles are sometimes abandoned by owners in garages and later sold by mechanics to desperate buyers.

At Gganda-Nansana, the crackdown disrupted the morning commute, with passengers who normally board 6:00 a.m. taxis to Kampala remaining stranded for hours. Joan Nabakooza, a market vendor, said she had spent more than three hours waiting for a taxi to the city. "I'm going back home, because most of the taxis on this road are very old. That is why none of them have shown up. They have stayed away because their colleagues are telling them that police in Rubigi are impounding every vehicle coming from this road," Nabakooza said.

Some taxi operators said they had been aware of the operation but were caught between complying with the directive and trying to earn a living. Joel Musasizi, a taxi driver from Wakiso whose vehicle was impounded at Rubigi, said his employer had instructed him to drive the vehicle empty to Kisenyi-Mengo for repairs. He said he nevertheless picked up stranded passengers along the way in an attempt to earn some money before being stopped at the checkpoint.

"I don't know what I will tell my boss, because he had warned me not to load people, but I wanted some money along the way for survival today. Things have not moved well for me," Musasizi said. He appealed to the government to give taxi operators more time to repair their vehicles. Muzamir Ndibo, Chairperson of Bwaise Taxi Park, welcomed the crackdown but questioned whether it would be enforced consistently. Ndibo alleged that some traffic officers allow drivers of unsafe taxis to continue operating after receiving bribes. "They get cash from the drivers who give them bribes.

Close 

They stop them on the road with worn-out tyres, sometimes with no side indicators, clearly in bad condition but with passengers on board. The driver gets out, gives 10,000 shillings to the officer, and he will gradually let him go and return with other passengers day by day," Ndibo alleged.

The operation is part of intensified road-safety enforcement by the Ministry of Works and Transport and traffic police. Other measures include impounding vehicles without valid inspection certificates, cracking down on overloading and reckless driving, and conducting mechanical spot checks at major taxi parks and highway entry points.

World.title: South Africa: Fired for Being Foreign - How Employers Gave in to March and March Threats
World.content:
There has been a rise in reports of unlawful treatment of immigrant workers (file photo).

The Casual Workers Advice Office has recorded a sharp rise in reports of xenophobic labour practices in Gauteng

The Casual Workers Advice Office has noted a sharp rise in reports of unlawful treatment of immigrant workers by employers in Gauteng.

Reports include payments withheld, exploitation, exclusion from UIF and unfair dismissals.

People we spoke to who have lived in South Africa for years believe that "there is much more hatred" against immigrants in recent months.

"They used us and threw us away when they were done," Raphike Bado, a Malawian immigrant who had worked in South Africa for many years, told GroundUp at the Casual Workers Advice Office (CWAO) in Germiston.



The CWAO says it is dealing with a wave of cases targeting immigrant workers in Gauteng. Many have been unable to work since the run-up to the 30 June "deadline". Many have now completely exhausted their savings and cannot afford the travel costs to leave South Africa.

Gugu Moyo, the CWAO's immigrant liaison officer, said immigrant workers "are being treated as less than human" and are being exploited.

She worries that there "is no end in sight" as politicians and anti-immigration "activists" continue to scapegoat immigrants and spread hatred.

The workers are "ordinary people just trying to create a life here like all of us", she said.

The CWAO said it has, since June, taken on over 100 cases of Gauteng workers being fired, suspended or shut out of their jobs. Many of them have valid papers.

None of the immigrant workers it has assisted has successfully claimed UIF, despite contributing to the fund, because their employers have refused to co-operate. CWAO is trying to assist with CCMA cases.

The workers CWAO is assisting described cases of exploitation, including low wages, unpaid overtime and unsafe working conditions.

CWAO said it has also helped hundreds of immigrants who wanted to contact embassies, sort out documents or arrange repatriation.

The workers

"We can no longer trust anybody. If you are a foreigner, whether you have documents or not, you fear for your life," an emotional Rejoice Moyo told GroundUp.

Moyo's is one of two dozen stories related to GroundUp by immigrant workers who had approached the CWAO Germiston office for assistance.

Originally from Zimbabwe, she has lived in South Africa for 17 years. But she was dismissed after the anti-immigrant group March and March turned up on 10 June at the shop where she worked as a sales consultant.

"These foreigners you are hiring must be gone," a March and March supporter told her employer and informed him of their 30 June "deadline" for undocumented immigrants to leave South Africa.

Moyo is documented and living and working legally in the country, but her employer "didn't care" she said. He dismissed her and a colleague and tried to coerce them into writing a resignation letter stating they had resigned "because we were scared of March and March".

She said she was only paid for the days she worked in June. She was not given notice pay or accrued annual leave.

Mbombo Nana and Sylvia (who preferred not to give her last name) fled war in the Democratic Republic of Congo and have lived in South Africa for over a decade.

"Now I face violence here," said Nana. "What do I do? I have nowhere else to go."

Nana and Sylvia have refugee papers and are legally allowed to work. But they were both dismissed after people turned up at their workplaces demanding that "only South Africans" be hired.

"We are working very hard, but they treat us like nothing because we are foreigners," said Sylvia. She said she was chased by a mob yelling, "Abahambe!" (They must go, a Zulu catchphrase adopted by anti-immigrant groups).

Monica Chifamba, who came from Zimbabwe in 2010, was also recently dismissed without payment. A single mother with two children, she is struggling to feed her family and pay rent and school fees.

Close 

She said she is often told to "go back to Zimbabwe".

She said she has experienced xenophobia during previous election periods, "but 2026 is different". She and her children are "living in fear", too afraid to answer the phone or speak in public.

She is an orphan and has nothing to return to in Zimbabwe, she said.

Raphike Bado has worked in plastic manufacturing since he came from Malawi in 2013. He said that the company he worked for hired "many foreigners" as they were "cheaper" and "could work longer".

On 15 June, he and fellow employees were told not to come to work the following day, "because March and March" were coming.

Bado was subsequently dismissed without compensation.

CWAO organiser Andile Nyembezi said that "xenophobic forces are mobilising based on ethnicity and tribalism which only divides" and does not create jobs or improve working conditions.

Out of fear, none of the workers we spoke to agreed to be photographed.

World.title: Nigeria: 150 Terrorists Surrender As Military Pressure Mounts in North-East
World.content:
ABUJA -- More than 150 terrorists, including commanders, fighters and affiliates, have surrendered to troops of the Joint Task Force North East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), in the past week, the military has said.

The figure represents a significant increase from the more than 50 terrorists who surrendered in the previous week, according to the Acting Military Information Officer, Captain Mohammed Goni.

Goni, in a statement on Monday, attributed the surge to sustained intelligence-led operations, intensified military pressure and coordinated kinetic and non-kinetic efforts aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and encouraging voluntary disengagement.

He said the development indicated growing pressure within terrorist formations, particularly on their freedom of movement, logistics, supply chains and ability to retain personnel in their enclaves.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"The significant increase reflects the cumulative impact of sustained intelligence-led operations, intensified military pressure and coordinated kinetic and non-kinetic efforts aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and encouraging voluntary disengagement from terrorism," he said.

Goni added that the recovery of weapons and ammunition from some of the surrendering terrorists further demonstrated the impact of sustained military pressure on terrorist networks.

He said the increase in surrenders also reflected the effectiveness of Operation Hadin Kai's counter-insurgency strategy, which combines intelligence-led operations with strategic communication, civil-military engagement and other non-kinetic measures.

According to him, the measures were disrupting terrorist activities and support networks, weakening hostile narratives and encouraging more members of the groups to abandon terrorism.

He said strategic communication remained central to the military's efforts by conveying credible messages to those willing to renounce terrorism and highlighting the consequences of continued association with terrorist groups.

Goni said all persons who surrendered were profiled, documented and handled in accordance with established procedures and applicable laws.

He said the theatre command would sustain the current momentum to encourage further disengagement and weaken terrorist recruitment and sustainment mechanisms.

The Military High Command, he added, commended troops for their resilience, discipline and operational effectiveness, urging them to maintain pressure on terrorist elements and deny them freedom of action across the theatre.

"Operation Hadin Kai remains resolute in its mission to sustain pressure on terrorist networks, disrupt their capabilities and support structures, protect civilians and create the conditions necessary for the restoration of lasting peace, security and normalcy across the North-East region," he said.

World.title: Zimbabwe: Mnangagwa Dragged to Constitutional Court, Accused of Packing Senate With Zanu-PF Politicians
World.content:
President Emmerson Mnangagwa has been dragged to the Constitutional Court over his appointment of 10 senators, with two applicants accusing him of packing the Upper House with politicians instead of independent professionals as required by the Constitution.

Thamsanqa Ncube and Ibhetshu LikaZulu are seeking an urgent order blocking the nominees from being sworn in and ultimately declaring their appointments null and void.

The respondents are Mnangagwa, the Speaker of Parliament, Justice Minister Ziyambi Ziyambi, the Attorney-General and the 10 nominees, Jabulani Sibanda, Makhosini Hlongwane, Mary Mliswa, Nokuthula Matsikenyere, Kudakwashe Tagwirei, Godwills Masimirembwa, Lucy Chitaga, Gen Gibson Mashingaidze, Brilliant Dube and Iren Mutumbwa.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The applicants argue that Section 120(1)(e), introduced through Constitution Amendment No. 3, requires the President to appoint 10 senators based on their "professional skills and other competencies" and after consultation with the National Assembly.

But they claim the nominees are predominantly Zanu-PF politicians or closely linked to the ruling party, defeating the purpose of the amendment.

The application says the appointments are "the precise opposite" of assurances given by Justice Minister Ziyambi during debate on the amendment.

Ziyambi had told Parliament: "The appointment power is not unbounded. The text requires that these 10 Senators be chosen for their professional skills and competencies."

He said the new senators were intended to bring expertise "in finance, in science, in law, in technology, in public health".

The applicants also challenge the consultation process, saying Mnangagwa's nominees were simply announced in Parliament before the Speaker declared: "Recommendations put and agreed to."

"There was no debate, no question, no point of order, and no opportunity for meaningful consultation," Ncube says in the founding affidavit.

The applicants further argue that there is no legislative or parliamentary framework regulating the consultation process, making the appointments premature and unconstitutional.

They fear the dispute will become academic if the nominees are sworn in and begin voting in the Senate.

"The ten individuals are awaiting swearing-in. Once sworn, they will sit and vote in the Senate with full rights," Ncube says.

The applicants want the court to stop the swearing-in and order that any fresh appointments only be made after proper procedures are established to ensure the nominees have the professional expertise required by the Constitution.

The case comes shortly after Constitution Amendment No. 3 increased the Senate from 80 to 90 members by creating the 10 presidentially appointed seats.

World.title: Federal judge slaps down Ghislaine Maxwell petition for new trial as ‘rambling,’ ‘meritless’

A federal judge rejected Ghislaine Maxwell’s latest effort to overturn her conviction, blasting her petition as "lengthy and rambling" and finding her claims "all meritless" and "all or almost all" frivolous.

U.S. District Judge Paul A. Engelmayer denied Maxwell’s post-conviction challenge in an opinion filed Monday in the Southern District of New York and made public Tuesday, writing that the evidence against the convicted Jeffrey Epstein associate at trial was "overwhelming."

Maxwell, representing herself, had moved to vacate her conviction and 20-year prison sentence, alleging that her constitutional rights were violated at trial and sentencing.

TODD BLANCHE SAYS 'NO CLOSED INVESTIGATIONS' IN EPSTEIN CASE, VOWS DOJ WILL PURSUE NEW SUSPECTS

Engelmayer said the vast majority of her arguments were procedurally barred because she either raised and lost them on direct appeal or could have raised them earlier but did not.

The judge also shot down Maxwell’s reliance on material released under the Epstein Files Transparency Act, finding that the purported new evidence did not support her claims. The supposedly "new" evidence was largely irrelevant to Maxwell 's case, the judge said.

FORMER ATTORNEY GENERAL PAM BONDI HAILS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 'JUSTICE AND TRANSPARENCY' ON EPSTEIN FILES

"To the extent it is relevant, far from exculpating her, it incriminates her or reinforces the correctness of the legal rulings Maxwell challenges," Engelmayer wrote.

"The Court accordingly denies Maxwell’s petition," he concluded.

Maxwell was convicted in December 2021 on five felony counts stemming from her participation with Epstein in the sexual abuse of young girls over the course of a decade.

World.title: Denmark's left-wing PM warns: 'Big enemy has started to grow from within' as Europe faces migrant reckoning
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Denmark's left-wing prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, has sent shockwaves throughout the European left after recent comments about the Scandinavian nation's — and the continent's — failure to deal with radical Islam among migrant communities.

Her comments come after the mass migration chaos in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, when Frederiksen criticized the actions of Spain's leftist leader, Pedro Sánchez, during a special session on Ceuta in the Danish Parliament.

Responding to a question from a far-left legislator on Denmark’s apparent lack of "solidarity" with Spain against "anti-democratic forces" pressuring Europe, Frederiksen said, "If we talk about undemocratic forces, then Russia is our biggest enemy. The problem is that a big enemy has started to grow from within, and it is foreigners who have come to Europe," according to an English translation.

MIGRANT CRISIS PUSHES ITALY TO RESTORE BORDER CHECKS WITH SPAIN, TESTING EUROPE'S OPEN-BORDER SYSTEM

While not singling out Denmark's integrated immigrant population, she continued, "It is Hamas supporters. It is people who commit terror against European societies. It is people who do not recognize our fundamental European values. It is people who sympathize with some of the darkest forces in this world. So, Europe is threatened. The problem is that we are threatened both from outside and now from within, but it is not because of a disagreement between the Danish and Spanish governments, but because of people with an Islamic background who do not want the open, free European society, unfortunately."

Sweden-based foreign policy expert and author Daniel Schatz told Fox News Digital, "What is striking is not that a conservative politician is talking about illegal immigration, failed integration and Islamist extremism, it is that one of Europe’s leading center-left prime ministers is saying it in such blunt terms. That tells you how far the European immigration debate has shifted."

PORTUGAL ENACTS 'BURQA LAW' LARGELY PROHIBITING FACE COVERINGS IN PUBLIC

Frederiksen came to power in Denmark’s 2019 elections on what Reuters called a "platform of radical reforms to reach climate targets, lowering the pension age for manual workers - and stricter migration policies." Denmark already had some of the strongest asylum laws in Europe before 2019, including a 2018 law targeting "parallel societies." That law allowed the government to "demolish or sell off social housing areas where more than half of residents are from a ‘non-Western’ background," if certain criteria were met, and refugees in those areas are not eligible for family reunion.

In 2021, Frederiksen introduced a new deportation law allowing for refugees to be returned to their country of origin, if Denmark deemed it safe, even if Denmark had no diplomatic relations with that country, and even as the European Commission deemed Danish legislation on transferring asylum seekers to third countries while their claims were processed "incompatible with EU law."

Since June, Frederiksen has been a leading voice in opposition to the immigration policies of Spain’s Pedro Sánchez, telling Parliament, "It is no secret that I and the Spanish Prime Minister deeply disagree on immigration policy… I and we will not accept that Danish society has to pay the price for decisions in Spain that we fundamentally disagree with."

On Aug 1, Frederiksen joined conservative Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and 20 other EU government leaders in a letter saying the EU "cannot allow mass crossings, the instrumentalization of migration or other hybrid threats to create the perception that illegal entry into the European Union is possible."

ITALY-SPAIN BORDER FEUD EXPOSES EUROPE’S DEEPENING IMMIGRATION DIVIDE

The two, currently the only female heads of government in the EU, followed that letter with an Aug 10 joint statement saying they "are both proud of Europe’s Christian cultural heritage and we want to protect it. We expect that those who arrive in our countries and choose to make Europe their home respect our values and do not try to impose ways of life that we do not share. We believe that this is the right path to protect Europe and our common values. And we believe that millions of Europeans share this conviction."

Emma Schubart of the Henry Jackson Society told Fox News Digital, "Frederiksen is right to name the ‘enemy within’. Europe has spent years pretending that uncontrolled migration and failed integration come without consequences. They do not… Parallel societies have taken root, Islamist extremism has been allowed to fester and support for groups such as Hamas is no longer confined to the margins. Denmark understands the cost."

Daniel Schatz said Frederiksen "is essentially arguing that Europe faces threats from two directions: Russia from outside and anti-democratic extremism from within. For a center-left European leader, that is remarkably strong language." He noted Frederiksen’s "political formula has been straightforward: protect Denmark’s generous system of public benefits and social services, control the border and deny the populist right a monopoly on immigration. For an American audience, that is probably the most important thing to understand about the Danish model."

Frederiksen’s position is important, he said, because she did not move politically "because Danish voters suddenly became concerned about immigration. She moved because she realized years ago that many of them already were." He added, "The important distinction is that this is not an argument that immigrants are inherently criminal. It is an argument that a democratic society must be willing to confront failed integration when it occurs."

Schubart added, "Other leaders now need to show the same courage, secure their borders, deport those with no right to remain and make clear that integration into our laws and values is not optional."

Reuters contributed to this report.

World.title: Ohio man charged over graphic threats to kill Trump, behead GOP lawmaker
World.content:

An Ohio man was arrested by the FBI after allegedly making graphic threats against a Jewish Republican congressman and calling for the death of President Donald Trump.

Alex Justin Miller, 26, is accused of sending a "true threat" to Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., and his family, according to the Department of Justice (DOJ).

A copy of the message separately obtained by Fox News Digital shows Miller allegedly called Fine and his family "Nazi f—-s" and said he would burn their house down, pledging he would "never stop until your head is hanging from the rooftops of the White House." His message ended with "DEATH TO RANDY FINE AND DEATH TO DONALD TRUMP."

Miller was charged with interstate transmission of a threat to injure by the U.S. Attorney in the Middle District of Florida and faces up to five years in prison if convicted, the DOJ said.

FAA EMPLOYEE CHARGED WITH ALLEGEDLY THREATENING TO KILL PRESIDENT TRUMP IN EMAIL TO WHITE HOUSE

The incident was investigated by the FBI and the Brevard County Sheriff's Office with assistance from the Secret Service and Capitol Police, the DOJ said.

"It was so graphic. It says, 'I'm gonna murder you. I'm going to cut your head off. I won't stop,'" Fine told Fox News Digital. "I reported it immediately. I unfortunately have learned what the difference is between a nasty message and a death threat, and this clearly was a death threat."

The full message read: "Dear fat--- piece of s---stain, I cannot wait to take a trip to you lovely home and light the whole place on fire and murder you and your entire family in the middle of the night while you sleep. I hope you disgusting Nazi f---s sleep with one eye open for the rest of your life because I will NEVER stop until your head is hanging from the rooftops of the White House. You deserve 10000% to be beheaded and have your body paraded through the streets. DEATH TO RANDY FINE AND DEATH TO DONALD TRUMP!!"

Fine said he received the threat via email on the morning of primary Election Day in the Sunshine State. He also said it reinforced his belief that federal officials need more protection.

"I don't know what this person's motives were for writing this, but it's someone not from Florida. So, you know, this was not a local constituent that was upset," he said. "I do think members of Congress need more security than we oftentimes get."

FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY THREATENING TO KILL TRUMP, RUBIO AND BONDI

He added that law enforcement found and arrested the man within 36 hours.

Don't write messages like this to elected officials, Republican or Democrat. You want to call us bad people? Be my guest, but do not do this sort of thing," Fine said.

World.title: I feared AI would leave my community behind. Now I see a path to prosperity
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

There has been worry of late that AI may eliminate jobs. I have seen the power of AI, and I can understand why some sectors are worried. I have even worried that this ongoing AI revolution may leave behind the troubled youth in my South Side of Chicago neighborhood. For the past several years, I have been building this massive Leadership and Economic Opportunity Center to teach young people the trades as a way out of poverty and violence. And I’m sitting here, wondering if I made a mistake. Have I created something that is outdated? I admit I felt this panic deep within my soul. Was I handing my youth a caveman tool when they needed the latest technology?

I wondered how we would adapt to this ever-changing world that changes so fast that sometimes I can’t even remember who was in the news last week. So I took a walk through the walls of the new building. It’s beautiful. It brings me such joy to see the rooms and the promises of opportunity that come with them. We have rooms for the trades in every aspect of construction, from wood cutting to plumbing. We have rooms for creating new electricians. We’ve also got rooms for creating HVAC workers and fiber technicians, and more. We’ve got amazing equipment for our youth to train on. But was all of this for nothing? Did time pass us by?

I did not create this building to leave another empty shell on the South Side of Chicago. Just down the street from us, Walgreens and McDonald’s fled, and there are boarded-up buildings. There are no grocery stores, and we’re a true food desert where fried foods are often our only quick and easy option. The rates of homeownership here are abysmal. Despite low home prices, some blocks have homeownership rates as low as 14% to 24%. We have a poverty rate of 40% to 51%, depending on which block you go to. And don’t even get me started on our local schools.

DIVINE PURPOSE HELPED BRING CHICAGO’S MOST-DANGEROUS BLOCK BACK TO LIFE

That is why I am so desperate to bring a symbol of hope to my community through the building of this community center. I still felt that quiet desperation as I walked past the construction workers at work. I came upon a young man who had finished his job here. After thanking him for his contribution, I asked him where he was going next. He explained that he had secured work for a major AI manufacturing facility in a nearby township. As he told me more and more, I thought to myself: There’s a building boom.

When we think of AI, we think of the Silicon Valley story about white-collar workers. The media is full of headlines about white-collar workers afraid of losing their jobs. But at the same time, I was also noticing, in my layman’s view of the world, that AI could potentially be the wealth-of-knowledge generator that places practical expertise directly in the hands of young people failed by the current systems. In other words, AI could help my youth leapfrog gaps in local schooling and training by enabling self-sufficiency faster.

THE AI REVOLUTION THREATENS OFFICE JOBS, BUT REVIVES DEMAND FOR SKILLED TRADES

I also began, thanks to my conversation with the young construction worker, to see that many people were missing the big opportunity here. While AI may transform or eliminate certain desk jobs, it is also a world unto itself that must be built. We’re talking about data centers, power grids, fiber networks and advanced manufacturing facilities.

AI could potentially be the wealth-of-knowledge generator that places practical expertise directly in the hands of young people failed by the current systems.

Who is going to help build this revolution? I looked down from the roof of my community center at the young people on the sidewalks and prayed that it would be them and their peers.

This AI boom will require, for many years, electricians, HVAC technicians, construction workers, plumbers, pipefitters, fiber technicians and other skilled tradespeople. I recently drove out to see some of these facilities being built, and they’re massive. The world is changing before our eyes, and we’re entering an entirely new era of infrastructure.

A SOUTHERN STATE JUST TOOK THE TOP SPOT IN ONE OF THE WORLD’S FASTEST-GROWING INDUSTRIES

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has called this the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Major tech companies are projected to spend roughly $700 billion this year alone on AI-related facilities. This will only increase as more and more of us adopt AI. And it is happening as hundreds of data centers are under construction or planned across the United States. One analysis estimates the nation will need 130,000 to 140,000 additional skilled trades workers by 2030 just to support AI infrastructure—before accounting for housing, hospitals and energy projects competing for the same talent.

This demand has created an urgency to develop new workers. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects electrician employment to grow 9% from 2024 to 2034, a rate much higher than average. The bureau projects about 81,000 openings each year. HVAC mechanics and installers are projected to grow 8 percent, which translates to roughly 40,100 openings annually. Plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters are expected to see about 44,000 openings per year.

WANT TO STRENGTHEN AMERICA'S ECONOMY? THE KEY INVESTMENT IS HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT

In May 2026, the construction industry reported approximately 298,000 job openings. Specialty-trade contractors already employ more than 565,000 electricians and 349,000 plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters. The Associated Builders and Contractors estimates the industry needs roughly 349,000 net new workers in 2026 alone. In data-center hotspots, skilled-trades wages already carry a 7 percent premium overall, with plumbers and pipefitters seeing gains as high as 20 percent.

More importantly, the median annual pay for these jobs is solid, at around $62,000 to $72,000. This may not seem like a lot, but for a kid who has known nothing but generational poverty, this is the way out of the culture of dependency.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Yes, one job like this can end that vicious, soul-sucking cycle that has kept so many of us stuck in the permanent Black underclass. These careers build assets, they restore dignity and pride, and they give people a stake in America.

At first, I feared that the AI revolution would leave my youth behind. But now I’m more convinced than ever that this is the greatest opportunity to come along.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

I was part of the Great Migration myself, the very tail end of it. My mother and her husband moved from a tiny town in Tennessee to Muncie, Indiana, for better jobs in industrial factories. When I visited them and later moved to Indiana, I was exposed to a world of more opportunities.

I see this cycle of life coming back around today, and I’m determined more than ever to push my youth onto this AI opportunity wagon. As they say, this is their chance to strike it rich in America.

LIONESS SEASON 3 EPISODE 2 OPENING SCENE LEAVES FANS STUNNED WITH ITS INTENSITY ON PARAMOUNT+

'Lioness' fans react to brutal new episode.

EXCLUSIVE: Los Angeles County GOP Chair Roxanne Hoge issued an impassioned appeal for Republicans to "send help" to Democratic-controlled California, describing what she sees as rampant corruption in the state and saying most people "can't understand the level of obsession they have with controlling our lives."

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Hoge addressed the online reaction to a recent viral video posted by Democratic Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass in which the mayor said the city government would match six times every dollar donated to her re-election campaign. While some social media users expressed shock, Hoge said she was not surprised.

"The rest of the country doesn't understand what we're living under here," she told Fox News Digital.

"The number one thing people need to understand about Los Angeles in particular and California in general is that they've codified all of their shenanigans," she explained. "What normal people consider cheating or weirdness in the electoral process? It's all in the rules [here]."

LOS ANGELES PROPOSAL TO ALLOW NONCITIZENS TO VOTE IN LOCAL ELECTIONS SPARKS ONLINE BACKLASH

In a recent viral social media post, Bass, Los Angeles’ 72-year-old progressive mayor, said that "when you donate to our campaign, the city can match your donation 6 to 1," adding, "If you donate $5, the city turns it into $35."

Bass said that "thanks to LA’s super match program, every qualified donation from Los Angeles residents is matched six to one by the city." She added that after this year’s mayoral primary, in which Republican candidate Spencer Pratt garnered significant support, "we had to start over from scratch."

"So, we need you to rush in your matching donation right now, to help fuel this campaign," she said.

Social media users questioned and criticized Bass’ comments.

Hoge, however, said the matching-funds program Bass describes in her campaign video is legal under city law. She noted that the rule applies not only to mayoral campaigns but also to City Council campaigns, adding that they "Have many active [Democratic Socialists of America] members currently sitting and running."
